q: A practical nurse (PN) is reviewing the day's assignments with the charge RN. Which task is appropriate for the PN to accept?
options: Collecting vital signs and intake/output data on a stable post-op client
Inserting a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC)
Developing the nursing care plan for a client with heart failure
Performing the initial admission assessment on a newly admitted client, for now
explain: Correct: A - collecting vital signs and I&O on a stable client is data collection, squarely within PN scope. D is wrong - initial assessments and care plan development belong to the RN. B is wrong - PICC insertion is an advanced procedure outside PN scope. C is wrong - the RN develops the care plan; the PN contributes data and carries out assigned interventions.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The RN asks the PN to delegate a task to the unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP). Which delegated task is appropriate?
options: Evaluating whether a wound dressing change was effective
Teaching a client how to use an incentive spirometer
Assessing a client's pain level after surgery
Measuring vital signs on a stable client with pneumonia
explain: Correct: D - measuring vital signs on a stable client is a routine task that can be delegated to UAP. C is wrong - assessment is a nursing function and cannot be delegated. B is wrong - teaching requires nursing judgment and cannot be delegated to UAP. A is wrong - evaluation of an intervention's effectiveness is a nursing responsibility.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A PN notes that a post-op client's blood pressure dropped from 128/76 to 92/58 mmHg and the client feels dizzy. What is the PN's best action?
options: Recheck the blood pressure in one hour and document the trend
Report the findings to the RN immediately using SBAR
Give the client extra fluids without an order
Encourage the client to ambulate to improve circulation
explain: Correct: B - a significant BP drop with dizziness signals possible hemorrhage or shock; the PN collects data and reports promptly to the RN. A is wrong - waiting an hour with symptomatic hypotension is unsafe. D is wrong - ambulating a dizzy, hypotensive client risks a fall and worsens perfusion. C is wrong - the PN cannot independently initiate fluid therapy without an order.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is caring for four clients. Which client should the PN report to the RN first?
options: A client with arthritis requesting help to the bathroom
A client with diabetes requesting a bedtime snack
A client with heart failure who gained 1 kg overnight and has new crackles
A client with hypertension asking when the next blood pressure check is due
explain: Correct: C - rapid weight gain plus new crackles suggests acute fluid overload/heart failure exacerbation, the highest priority. B, D, and A are routine, stable needs the PN can address through normal workflow without urgent RN notification.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The charge RN asks the PN to administer an IV push medication to a client. IV push administration is outside the PN's scope in this state. What should the PN do?
options: Ask the UAP to give the medication instead, for the duration of the patient's stay
Give the medication since the RN delegated it, before the end of the shift
Give the medication slowly to make it safer
Refuse the task and report the concern through the chain of command
explain: Correct: D - the PN is accountable for practicing within scope; an RN's request does not authorize a scope violation. The PN should decline and communicate up the chain. B and C are wrong - performing a task outside scope is unsafe and unlicensed practice regardless of who asked. A is wrong - delegating an out-of-scope task to UAP compounds the violation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is scheduled for a colonoscopy and asks the PN to explain the risks of the procedure before signing consent. What is the PN's best response?
options: Have the client sign first and ask questions later, during the current shift
Tell the client you will ask the provider to come explain the procedure
Explain the risks so the client can sign the form
Tell the client that signing is just a formality, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - explaining risks and obtaining informed consent is the provider's responsibility; the PN may witness the signature after consent is obtained. C is wrong - the PN explaining risks oversteps into the provider's role. A is wrong - consent must be informed before signing. D is wrong - consent is a legal protection, never a formality.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A UAP reports to the PN that a client's call light has been on for 20 minutes. The PN is busy with a dressing change. What is the PN's best action?
options: Ask the UAP to check on the client and report back
Tell the UAP to turn off the light and tell the client to wait
Ignore it since the UAP is already aware
Finish the dressing change, then check on the client
explain: Correct: A - the PN remains responsible for delegated work; directing the UAP to check and report back keeps the client safe while the PN finishes a sterile task. D risks leaving an urgent need unaddressed. C abandons responsibility. B is wrong - silencing a call light without assessing the need is neglectful.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which activity is within the PN's role when working with a newly diagnosed diabetic client?
options: Interpreting the client's glucose log to adjust insulin doses
Providing the initial teaching on insulin injection technique
Reinforcing teaching about consistent meal timing that the RN already covered
Developing the client's diabetes self-management plan
explain: Correct: C - reinforcing teaching the RN initiated is a core PN function. B is wrong - initial teaching belongs to the RN. A is wrong - interpreting data to adjust doses is clinical decision-making beyond PN scope; the PN reports the data to the RN. D is wrong - plan development is the RN's role.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: During a disaster drill, the PN is assigned to assist with triage. Which action is appropriate for the PN?
options: Pronouncing death for casualties who are not breathing, for now
Collecting vital signs and reporting findings to the RN leading triage
Assigning triage categories to incoming casualties
Deciding which clients go to surgery first, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: B - the PN contributes through data collection and reporting to the RN directing triage. C, A, and D are wrong - triage categorization, death pronouncement decisions, and surgical prioritization require RN/provider judgment beyond PN scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with terminal cancer tells the PN, 'I do not want to be resuscitated, but my family insists on everything being done.' What is the PN's best action?
options: Avoid discussing it to prevent upsetting the family
Change the code status in the chart to DNR per the client's request
Tell the client the family knows best and encourage full resuscitation
Document the client's wishes and report the conflict to the RN
explain: Correct: D - the PN advocates by documenting the client's stated wishes and reporting the conflict so the RN and provider can address advance directives with the client and family. C is wrong - it dismisses client autonomy. B is wrong - the PN cannot independently change code status; that requires a provider order. A is wrong - avoiding the issue abandons the client.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN delegated morning vital signs to the UAP. The UAP reports a blood pressure of 88/54 mmHg on a client whose baseline is 130/80. Who is accountable for ensuring appropriate follow-up?
options: The PN, who retains accountability for delegated tasks
No one, since vital signs are routine, in accordance with facility policy
The charge RN, who oversees the whole unit, during the current shift
Only the UAP, since they took the measurement, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: A - delegation transfers the task, never the accountability; the PN must follow up on the abnormal finding and report to the RN. D is wrong - the UAP is responsible for accurate performance, but accountability for the delegated task stays with the nurse. C is wrong - the charge RN is not accountable for this specific delegation. B is wrong - abnormal vitals always require follow-up.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client refuses a prescribed blood transfusion, stating religious beliefs. The PN's best action is to:
options: Delay reporting until the next shift
Explain that the transfusion is necessary and encourage the client to reconsider
Respect the refusal, document it, and report it to the RN
Have the family convince the client to accept the transfusion
explain: Correct: C - competent adults have the right to refuse treatment; the PN respects autonomy, documents, and reports so the provider can discuss alternatives. B is wrong - pressuring the client violates autonomy and informed refusal. D is wrong - using family to coerce is inappropriate. A is wrong - a refused blood order needs prompt reporting.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is asked to float to a unit where the client population requires skills the PN has never performed. What should the PN do?
options: Accept the assignment but inform the charge nurse of the limitations and request appropriate assignments
Trade assignments with another nurse without telling anyone, and obtain a new order if the patient's condition changes
Refuse to float under any circumstances, while keeping the patient warm and comfortable
Accept the assignment and learn the skills on the clients, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A - the PN must practice only within competence; communicating limitations allows safe assignment matching. D is wrong - practicing unfamiliar skills on clients is unsafe. C is wrong - floating itself is acceptable; the issue is the skill mismatch, which can be managed. B is wrong - undisclosed swaps break accountability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which findings must the PN report to the RN immediately? Select all that apply.
options: A client asking what time lunch is served
Urine output of 15 mL/hr for the past 3 hours
Oxygen saturation 89% on room air with increased work of breathing
A client requesting an extra blanket
Blood pressure 88/52 mmHg with dizziness in a post-op client
New-onset chest pain rated 7/10
explain: Correct: E, C, F, B - symptomatic hypotension, desaturation with respiratory distress, new severe chest pain, and oliguria (under 30 mL/hr) all signal potentially life-threatening changes requiring immediate RN notification. D and A are routine comfort and information needs the PN can handle independently.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is calling the provider to report a change in a client's condition. Which elements belong in an SBAR report? Select all that apply.
options: Situation: the client's name, room, and what is happening now
Background: relevant history and baseline status
Recommendation: what the PN thinks is needed, such as 'please come evaluate'
Assessment: the PN's collected data and vital signs
A lengthy retelling of the client's entire hospitalization
The PN's personal opinion about the provider's past orders
explain: Correct: A, B, D, C - SBAR is Situation, Background, Assessment (the PN's collected data, not medical diagnosis), Recommendation. F is wrong - personal opinions about orders are unprofessional and irrelevant. E is wrong - SBAR must be concise; a full history wastes critical time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which tasks may the PN appropriately delegate to experienced UAP? Select all that apply.
options: Performing a sterile dressing change
Measuring intake and output
Obtaining routine vital signs on stable clients
Bathing a stable client
Assisting a stable client with ambulation
Administering oral medications
explain: Correct: E, B, D, C - ambulation, I&O, bathing, and routine vitals on stable clients are standard delegable tasks. F is wrong - medication administration requires a licensed nurse. A is wrong - sterile dressing changes require nursing skill and judgment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The RN asks the PN to perform tasks during a busy shift. Which requests should the PN decline as outside PN scope? Select all that apply.
options: Collecting a sputum specimen for culture
Developing the nursing diagnosis for a care plan
Reinforcing discharge teaching the RN already provided
Interpreting arterial blood gases to adjust ventilator settings
Administering an IV push antihypertensive
Performing the initial admission assessment on a new client
explain: Correct: E, F, D, B - IV push, initial assessments, ABG interpretation for ventilator changes, and nursing diagnosis development all exceed PN scope. C is wrong because reinforcing teaching IS within PN scope. A is wrong because specimen collection is a routine PN task.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN has four clients needing attention. Which situations require the PN to notify the RN before proceeding with routine care? Select all that apply.
options: A client asks for help changing the television channel
A client with heart failure has 2+ pitting edema that was also present yesterday
A diabetic client's fingerstick glucose is 38 mg/dL and the client is sweaty and confused
A post-op client's Jackson-Pratt drain suddenly fills with 200 mL of bright red blood
A client states the pain medication is due in 30 minutes
A client's IV site shows redness, swelling, and pain along the vein
explain: Correct: C, D, F - severe hypoglycemia with neuroglycopenic symptoms, sudden bright-red drain output suggesting hemorrhage, and phlebitis signs all require prompt RN notification. E is a routine medication timing question. B is unchanged chronic edema, not an acute change. A is a comfort request the PN or UAP can handle.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN smells smoke in a client's room and sees flames in the wastebasket. What is the PN's first action?
options: Pull the fire alarm
Close the door to contain the fire
Remove the client from the room
Grab the fire extinguisher and put out the fire
explain: Correct: C - RACE: Rescue comes first; move the client to safety before anything else. D is wrong - extinguishing comes after rescue and alarm. A is second after rescue. B is containment, which follows rescue and alarm.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with a history of falls needs to use the bathroom. Which action best prevents injury?
options: Dim the lights to help the client relax, during the current shift
Keep the bed in the lowest position, call light within reach, and assist with ambulation
Place the bed in the highest position for easier standing
Apply a vest restraint so the client cannot get up alone, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - low bed, accessible call light, and supervised ambulation directly reduce fall risk. C is wrong - a high bed increases fall injury severity. D is wrong - restraints are a last resort requiring an order and do not prevent falls safely. A is wrong - dim lighting increases fall risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client in soft wrist restraints is becoming agitated. What should the PN do?
options: Remove the restraints permanently without telling anyone, and explain the procedure to the patient beforehand
Tighten the restraints so the client cannot move and report any abnormal findings to the healthcare provider
Leave the restraints on until the provider remembers to discontinue them, and record the intake and output for the shift
Check circulation and skin, offer toileting and fluids per policy, and report the increased agitation to the RN
explain: Correct: D - restrained clients need frequent monitoring of circulation, skin, and basic needs, plus reporting of status changes; restraints require ongoing RN/provider review. B is wrong - restraints must never impair circulation. C is wrong - restraints need active re-evaluation, not passive continuation. A is wrong - the PN cannot unilaterally discontinue a restraint order and must communicate.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: When should the PN perform hand hygiene? The best answer is:
options: Only after contact with a client in isolation, for now
Before and after every client contact, after removing gloves, and after touching the environment
Only when hands are visibly soiled, before administering any further medication
At the beginning and end of the shift, while observing the patient for any adverse reaction
explain: Correct: B - hand hygiene is required before and after client contact, after glove removal, and after touching the client's environment. C is wrong - routine hand hygiene is needed even without visible soil. A is wrong - it applies to all clients, not just isolation. D is wrong - twice a shift is far too infrequent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN sustains a needlestick from a used needle. What is the first action?
options: Apply bleach to disinfect the puncture, for the duration of the patient's stay
Squeeze the wound to make it bleed more, in accordance with facility policy
Wait to see if any symptoms develop, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Wash the area with soap and water and report per facility policy
explain: Correct: D - immediate washing with soap and water followed by prompt reporting and follow-up per exposure policy. B is wrong - squeezing or 'milking' the wound is not recommended and may increase tissue damage. A is wrong - bleach is caustic to tissue. C is wrong - delayed reporting can miss the window for post-exposure prophylaxis.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client begins having a tonic-clonic seizure. What should the PN do first?
options: Ease the client to the floor, turn the head to the side, and note the time
Place a padded tongue blade between the teeth
Restrain the limbs to prevent injury, as documented in the plan of care
Give the client water once the jerking slows
explain: Correct: A - protect from injury, maintain a patent airway by turning the head, and time the seizure for reporting. B is wrong - never force anything into the mouth during a seizure. C is wrong - restraining limbs can cause fractures. D is wrong - no oral intake until fully alert post-seizure due to aspiration risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A confused client keeps trying to climb out of bed despite redirection. The provider has not ordered restraints. What is the PN's best initial action?
options: Tie the client's gown to the bed frame as a reminder, since the same approach was used during the previous shift
Sedate the client with a PRN medication without an order
Use the least restrictive measures first: low bed, bed alarm, frequent rounding, and report to the RN
Apply restraints until the provider can be reached, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - least restrictive interventions come first, with ongoing reporting to the RN for further orders. D is wrong - restraints require a provider order and are a last resort. B is wrong - medicating without an order is outside scope. A is wrong - improvised restraints are unsafe and unlicensed restraint use.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client reports a latex allergy. Which action should the PN take?
options: Only avoid latex if the client is having surgery, and include the family in the discussion when appropriate
Wait for the client to have a reaction before taking precautions
Avoid documenting it since most gloves are now latex-free, at the patient's bedside
Document the allergy, report it to the RN, and ensure non-latex gloves and supplies are used
explain: Correct: D - latex allergy can cause anaphylaxis; it must be documented, communicated, and accommodated with non-latex products. C is wrong - documentation and communication are essential. B is wrong - precautions must precede exposure, not follow a reaction. A is wrong - latex is in gloves, catheters, and many supplies used in routine care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN witnesses a client fall. After ensuring the client is safe and notifying the RN, what should the PN include in the incident report?
options: Objective facts: time, place, what was observed, and actions taken
A statement that the fall was the UAP's fault
The PN's opinion about why the fall happened
The incident report information copied into the client's chart
explain: Correct: A - incident reports contain objective facts only, no opinions or blame. C is wrong - opinions and speculation do not belong in incident reports. B is wrong - assigning blame is inappropriate and legally risky. D is wrong - the incident report itself is never charted; only the factual client assessment and care go in the medical record.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which practices reflect correct use of standard precautions? Select all that apply.
options: Wearing a mask and eye protection when splashing is likely
Performing hand hygiene after removing gloves
Recapping used needles with both hands before disposal
Using the same gloves between two clients to save time
Wearing gloves when contact with blood or body fluids is likely
explain: Correct: E, B, A - gloves for blood/body fluid contact, hand hygiene after glove removal, and mask/eye protection against splashes are core standard precautions. C is wrong - needles must never be recapped; dispose directly in a sharps container. D is wrong - gloves are single-client use; reusing them spreads infection.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has a wound infected with MRSA. Which precautions should the PN follow? Select all that apply.
options: Performing hand hygiene before and after client contact
Wearing a gown and gloves when entering the room
Placing the client on airborne precautions with an N95 respirator
Using dedicated equipment such as a stethoscope for this client
Requiring a negative-pressure room
explain: Correct: B, D, A - MRSA wound infection requires contact precautions: gown and gloves, dedicated equipment, and hand hygiene. C and E are wrong - airborne precautions and negative-pressure rooms are for airborne diseases like tuberculosis, not contact-spread MRSA.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which interventions help prevent falls in an older adult client? Select all that apply.
options: Using a vest restraint as the first intervention
Providing nonskid footwear
Keeping the call light within the client's reach
Keeping the bed in the lowest position
Rounding frequently to anticipate needs
explain: Correct: C, B, D, E - accessible call light, nonskid footwear, low bed position, and frequent rounding all reduce fall risk. A is wrong - restraints are a last resort requiring an order, not a first-line fall prevention strategy, and they do not reliably prevent falls.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for an older adult about influenza vaccination. Which statement by the client indicates correct understanding?
options: The flu shot will give me the flu, so I should avoid it, at the patient's bedside
Only children need flu vaccines, before the end of the shift
I should get the flu vaccine every year because the strains change
One flu shot protects me for the rest of my life, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - annual vaccination is needed because circulating strains change. A is wrong - inactivated flu vaccine cannot cause influenza. D is wrong - protection wanes and strains change yearly. B is wrong - older adults are a high-priority group for flu vaccination.

q: A 50-year-old client asks about mammography. The PN reinforces that current guidance generally recommends:
options: A baseline mammogram only if there is a family history, in accordance with facility policy
Regular mammograms starting around age 40-50 as discussed with the provider
Mammograms only after age 65, based on the findings documented so far
No screening is needed without symptoms, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - routine mammography screening is recommended starting around age 40-50 per major guidelines, individualized with the provider. A is wrong - screening is recommended regardless of family history. C is wrong - waiting until 65 misses the highest-benefit window. D is wrong - screening aims to detect cancer before symptoms appear.

q: A client who smokes asks the PN about quitting. What is the PN's best response?
options: Tell the client smoking only harms the lungs, and discard the documentation of the event afterwards
Tell the client that willpower alone is enough, then reassess the patient's respiratory status
Suggest the client switch to smokeless tobacco instead, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Reinforce the RN's teaching about quitline resources, nicotine replacement options, and setting a quit date
explain: Correct: D - reinforcing evidence-based cessation resources supports the client's goal. B is wrong - quitting usually requires support beyond willpower. A is wrong - smoking harms nearly every organ system. C is wrong - smokeless tobacco carries its own cancer and cardiovascular risks.

q: The PN is reinforcing nutrition teaching for an older adult. Which statement indicates the client needs further teaching?
options: I can skip meals to save money since I am less active
I will drink water regularly even if I do not feel thirsty
I should eat protein at each meal to maintain muscle
I need calcium and vitamin D for my bones
explain: Correct: A - skipping meals risks malnutrition and weakness in older adults; this needs correction and possibly a social work referral. C, D, and B all reflect correct understanding: protein preserves muscle, calcium/vitamin D protect bone, and scheduled fluids prevent dehydration since thirst perception declines with age.

q: According to Erikson, the primary developmental task of adolescence is:
options: Generativity vs. stagnation
Identity vs. role confusion
Trust vs. mistrust
Integrity vs. despair
explain: Correct: B - adolescents work on forming identity versus role confusion. C is infancy. D is older adulthood. A is middle adulthood. The PN uses this knowledge to reinforce age-appropriate teaching, such as involving teens in their own care decisions.

q: A postpartum client asks when she can resume contraception. The PN's best response is to:
options: Tell her contraception is unnecessary while breastfeeding, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, on this occasion
Recommend a specific contraceptive method, and notify the charge nurse of the change in condition
Reinforce the provider's teaching that ovulation can return before the first postpartum period, so contraception should be discussed with the provider
Tell her to wait one year, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: C - ovulation may precede the first menses, so the PN reinforces the need for timely provider discussion. A is wrong - breastfeeding alone is not reliable contraception. B is wrong - recommending a specific method is prescriptive and beyond PN scope. D is wrong - an arbitrary one-year wait is not evidence-based.

q: Which factors increase the risk of coronary artery disease and can be modified? Select all that apply.
options: Family history of heart disease
Cigarette smoking
Increasing age
Hypertension
Physical inactivity
Elevated LDL cholesterol
explain: Correct: B, D, F, E - smoking, hypertension, high LDL, and inactivity are all modifiable risk factors the PN can address in teaching reinforcement. A and C are wrong because family history and age are non-modifiable; the client cannot change them.

q: The PN is reinforcing prenatal teaching. Which client statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will avoid alcohol completely during pregnancy
I will use hot tubs to relieve back pain
I will keep all scheduled prenatal visits
I will take folic acid as recommended to help prevent neural tube defects
I will eat raw sushi since fish is healthy
explain: Correct: D, A, C - folic acid, alcohol avoidance, and regular prenatal care are cornerstone prenatal health behaviors. B is wrong - hot tubs raise core temperature, a risk in pregnancy. E is wrong - raw fish risks foodborne illness dangerous in pregnancy.

q: A client says, 'I am worried about my surgery tomorrow.' Which PN response is most therapeutic?
options: Tell me more about what is worrying you
Do not worry, everything will be fine
Why are you worried? The surgeon is excellent
You should focus on positive thoughts
explain: Correct: A - 'Tell me more' is open-ended and invites the client to share feelings. B is wrong - false reassurance dismisses the concern. C is wrong - 'why' questions can feel interrogating and put clients on the defensive. D is wrong - it shuts down the client's expressed emotion.

q: A client is crying after receiving a difficult diagnosis. The PN's best initial action is to:
options: Immediately call the chaplain, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Tell the client that crying will not help, before the end of the shift
Leave the room to give the client privacy, at the patient's bedside
Sit with the client, offer tissues, and allow time to express feelings
explain: Correct: D - therapeutic presence and permission to grieve support coping. C is wrong - leaving can feel like abandonment. A is wrong - calling the chaplain without asking assumes the client's wishes. B is wrong - it is judgmental and shuts down expression.

q: A client becomes verbally aggressive toward the PN. What is the PN's best response?
options: Argue back to establish authority, during the current shift
Remain calm, set clear limits on acceptable behavior, and ensure safety
Immediately apply restraints, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Leave the unit and let someone else handle it
explain: Correct: B - calm limit-setting protects everyone while preserving the therapeutic relationship. A is wrong - arguing escalates aggression. C is wrong - restraints are a last resort for imminent danger, not verbal aggression alone. D is wrong - abandoning the situation leaves safety unaddressed; the PN should seek help, not disappear.

q: A grieving spouse says, 'I feel so guilty I was not there when he died.' Which response is most therapeutic?
options: I know exactly how you feel, as documented in the plan of care
You should not feel guilty; you did your best
It sounds like you are carrying a heavy burden of guilt
At least he is no longer suffering, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C - reflecting the feeling validates the grief without judging it. A is wrong - the PN cannot know exactly how the spouse feels. B is wrong - telling someone not to feel dismisses the emotion. D is wrong - minimizing with 'at least' statements blocks expression of grief.

q: The PN is caring for a client whose cultural practices differ from the PN's own. What is the best approach?
options: Tell the client the hospital routine takes priority over personal practices
Ask the client about preferences and accommodate them within safe care
Assume all clients from that culture share the same beliefs
Ignore cultural practices to keep care standardized
explain: Correct: B - culturally competent care means asking the individual and accommodating preferences safely. C is wrong - stereotyping ignores individual variation. D is wrong - ignoring culture damages trust and care quality. A is wrong - rigid routines that dismiss the client's values are not client-centered.

q: During an interview, the PN asks, 'Why did you stop taking your medication?' Why is this question problematic?
options: It can make the client feel defensive and judged
It gathers too much information, at the patient's bedside
It is too open-ended, in accordance with facility policy
It takes too long to answer, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - 'why' questions often sound accusatory and trigger defensiveness, reducing honest disclosure. C is wrong - the problem is not open-endedness; open-ended questions are generally good. B and D are wrong - thorough answers are desirable, not a problem.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching about incentive spirometer use after surgery. The client asks how often to use it. The PN should reinforce:
options: Once a day is enough, in accordance with facility policy
Only when feeling short of breath
About 10 breaths every hour while awake
Continuously throughout the night, in this case
explain: Correct: C - 10 slow deep breaths every hour while awake prevents atelectasis and pneumonia. A is wrong - once daily is far too infrequent. B is wrong - the spirometer prevents complications; waiting for symptoms defeats the purpose. D is wrong - hourly use applies to waking hours; sleep should not be interrupted all night.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client on bed rest is at risk for pressure injuries. Where should the PN focus prevention efforts?
options: Only where redness is already visible, without informing the healthcare provider of the change
On the abdomen, which bears the most pressure, at the patient's bedside
Only on the heels, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
On bony prominences such as the sacrum, heels, and hips, with regular repositioning
explain: Correct: D - pressure injuries form over bony prominences; prevention means offloading them with scheduled repositioning. C is wrong - heels matter, but they are not the only site. A is wrong - waiting for redness means prevention already failed. B is wrong - the abdomen is not a typical pressure point in bed rest.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assisting a client with ambulation on post-op day 1. The client suddenly feels faint. What should the PN do first?
options: Encourage the client to keep walking to push through it, before the end of the shift
Leave the client standing while getting help, at the patient's bedside
Help the client sit or return to bed safely and assess vital signs
Give the client juice immediately, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - safety first: seat the client to prevent a fall, then collect data. A is wrong - pushing through presyncope risks a fall and injury. B is wrong - leaving a faint client standing is unsafe. D is wrong - giving fluids before assessing could cause aspiration if the client loses consciousness.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client reports pain of 7/10 after surgery. Before reporting to the RN for pain medication, what should the PN collect?
options: Location, quality, onset, what relieves or worsens it, and current vital signs
The client's opinion of the surgeon, before administering any further medication
Whether the client has visitors, for the duration of the patient's stay
Only the pain number, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A - thorough data collection (PQRST plus vitals) gives the RN what is needed for safe medication decisions. D is wrong - a number alone is incomplete data. B and C are irrelevant to pain management.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for a client using crutches. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will use crutches that reach my shoulders when standing
I will keep the crutch pads about two finger-widths below my armpits
I will look at my feet while walking for balance, at the patient's bedside
I will bear my full weight on my armpits for support
explain: Correct: B - pads two finger-widths below the axillae prevent nerve compression. D is wrong - bearing weight on the axillae can injure the brachial plexus. C is wrong - clients should look ahead, not down, to maintain balance. A is wrong - crutches fitted to shoulder height are too long and unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with dysphagia is about to eat lunch. Which action should the PN take?
options: Rush the client so the food does not get cold, before the end of the shift
Offer thin liquids to make swallowing easier, in accordance with facility policy
Allow the client to eat lying flat to rest, since the same approach was used during the previous shift
Ensure the client is sitting upright at 90 degrees and reinforce swallowing strategies
explain: Correct: D - upright positioning reduces aspiration risk; the PN reinforces the speech therapist's strategies. B is wrong - thin liquids are hardest to control and most likely to be aspirated. A is wrong - rushing increases aspiration risk. C is wrong - flat positioning greatly increases aspiration risk.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN notes a stage 1 pressure injury on a client's sacrum. The correct description and action are:
options: Full-thickness tissue loss; pack the wound, while keeping the patient warm and comfortable
Non-blanchable redness of intact skin; report to the RN and continue prevention measures
Open blister; apply antibiotic ointment without reporting, and wash hands before and after the procedure
Eschar-covered wound; debride it at the bedside, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B - stage 1 is intact skin with non-blanchable redness; the PN reports it and intensifies prevention. C is wrong - a blister is stage 2, and the PN does not independently start treatments. A describes stage 3/4, and packing is not a PN independent action. D is wrong - debridement is outside PN scope.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which actions help prevent pressure injuries in an immobile client? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the skin clean and dry
Repositioning at least every 2 hours
Using a pressure-redistributing surface as ordered
Massaging reddened bony prominences vigorously
Leaving the client in a damp brief to avoid disturbing rest
explain: Correct: B, A, C - q2h repositioning, clean dry skin, and pressure-redistributing surfaces prevent pressure injuries. D is wrong - massaging reddened areas can damage fragile tissue. E is wrong - prolonged moisture macerates skin and increases breakdown risk; soiled briefs must be changed promptly.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for a client with a new colostomy. Which observations should the PN report to the RN? Select all that apply.
options: Small amount of mucus in the pouch
Skin around the stoma is red and excoriated
Foul odor noted when emptying the pouch
Stoma appears dusky purple with swelling
Stoma is pink, moist, and protrudes slightly
explain: Correct: D, B - a dusky stoma suggests ischemia and excoriated peristomal skin needs intervention; both require RN notification. E is wrong to report as a problem - pink moist stoma is normal. A is normal mucus production. C is normal - stool odor is expected with a colostomy.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which nonpharmacologic comfort measures may the PN use for a client with mild pain? Select all that apply.
options: Administering a PRN opioid without reassessment
Applying a warm compress as ordered
Encouraging the client to 'tough it out' without medication
Repositioning for comfort
Guided relaxation and distraction
explain: Correct: D, B, E - repositioning, ordered heat/cold, and relaxation techniques are within PN scope for comfort. A is wrong - PRN medications require assessment and follow the provider's parameters; the PN does not give them casually. C is wrong - dismissing pain is nontherapeutic and poor care.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client starting warfarin says, 'I take ibuprofen for my headaches.' What is the PN's best response?
options: That is fine to continue, in accordance with facility policy
Advise the client to stop the warfarin instead, and make sure the patient understands the instructions given
Report this to the RN; NSAIDs increase bleeding risk with warfarin and acetaminophen is usually preferred
Tell the client to double the warfarin dose on headache days, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - NSAIDs impair platelet function and raise bleeding risk with warfarin; the PN reports so the RN/provider can address it. A is wrong - continuing ibuprofen is unsafe. D is wrong - dose changes require provider orders based on INR. B is wrong - stopping anticoagulation without an order risks clotting.

q: The PN is about to administer digoxin. The client's apical pulse is 52 beats/min. What should the PN do?
options: Recheck in 4 hours and give it then
Give half the dose to be safe
Give the digoxin as ordered since the pulse is close to normal
Hold the medication and report the pulse rate to the RN
explain: Correct: D - hold digoxin for apical pulse below 60 and report; bradycardia can signal digoxin toxicity. C is wrong - 52 is below the hold parameter. B is wrong - the PN cannot independently adjust doses. A is wrong - delaying without reporting misses a potential toxicity signal.

q: A client asks why metformin was held before a CT scan with contrast. The PN's best explanation is:
options: Contrast dye can affect kidney function, and metformin is held to reduce the risk of lactic acidosis; the provider will restart it
The contrast makes metformin stop working forever, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment
The medication was discontinued permanently, for the duration of the patient's stay
Metformin interferes with the scan images, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, during the current shift, for now
explain: Correct: A - iodinated contrast can impair renal function, and metformin accumulation risks lactic acidosis; it is held per protocol and restarted by order. B is wrong - the effect is temporary and precautionary. D is wrong - metformin does not affect image quality. C is wrong - this is a temporary hold, not discontinuation.

q: The PN is administering furosemide. Which finding should be reported to the RN promptly?
options: Mild thirst
Urine output 40 mL/hr
Blood pressure 128/78 mmHg
Potassium 2.9 mEq/L
explain: Correct: D - furosemide wastes potassium; 2.9 mEq/L is below the normal 3.5-5.0 range and risks dysrhythmias. C is a normal BP. B is adequate urine output (above 30 mL/hr). A is an expected mild diuretic effect.

q: A client taking lisinopril reports a persistent dry cough. What should the PN do?
options: Suggest the client take cough syrup with the lisinopril, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Document and report the cough to the RN; dry cough is a known ACE inhibitor side effect
Reassure the client that cough means the drug is working well, during the current shift
Tell the client to stop the medication immediately, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - dry cough is a classic ACE inhibitor effect; the PN reports so the provider can consider alternatives. D is wrong - the PN cannot order discontinuation; abrupt advice without provider input is unsafe. C is wrong - cough is a side effect, not a sign of efficacy. A is wrong - adding an unprescribed remedy without assessment is inappropriate.

q: The order reads: amoxicillin 500 mg PO; available: 250 mg capsules. How many capsules should the PN administer?
options: 2 capsules
1 capsule
4 capsules
0.5 capsule
explain: Correct: A - 500 mg divided by 250 mg per capsule = 2 capsules. D is wrong - that would be 125 mg. B gives only 250 mg, half the dose. C gives 1000 mg, double the dose.

q: An IV of 1000 mL normal saline is ordered to infuse over 8 hours. What is the infusion rate in mL/hr?
options: 100 mL/hr
80 mL/hr
125 mL/hr
250 mL/hr
explain: Correct: C - 1000 mL divided by 8 hours = 125 mL/hr. B, A, and D reflect arithmetic errors in dividing volume by time.

q: A client is prescribed ferrous sulfate for iron deficiency anemia. The PN reinforces which teaching?
options: Take it at bedtime with an antacid, before the end of the shift
Take it with milk to improve absorption, for now
Take it on an empty stomach or with vitamin C, and expect dark stools
Stop taking it once you feel less tired, in full
explain: Correct: C - iron absorbs best on an empty stomach or with vitamin C; dark stools are expected and harmless. B is wrong - calcium in milk inhibits iron absorption. A is wrong - antacids reduce absorption. D is wrong - therapy continues for months to replenish stores, per provider direction.

q: Which findings suggest lithium toxicity and must be reported immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Confusion and slurred speech
Increased thirst and frequent urination
Mild hand tremor that was present at baseline
Severe vomiting and diarrhea
Coarse tremor and ataxia
explain: Correct: E, A, D - coarse tremor, ataxia, confusion, slurred speech, and severe GI losses signal lithium toxicity, often worsened by dehydration or low sodium. B is wrong - mild thirst and polyuria are common early side effects, not toxicity. C is wrong - a fine baseline tremor is an expected side effect, unlike a new coarse tremor.

q: The PN is teaching about a new SSRI prescription (reinforcing the provider's teaching). Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: It is safe to drink heavily while taking it
It may take 2 to 4 weeks to feel the full effect
It works immediately like a pain reliever
Report thoughts of self-harm immediately
Do not stop it abruptly without talking to the provider
explain: Correct: B, E, D - SSRIs need weeks for full effect, require tapering rather than abrupt stop, and any suicidal thoughts must be reported at once. A is wrong - alcohol worsens depression and interacts with the drug. C is wrong - expecting immediate relief is the misconception that leads clients to quit too early.

q: A client is receiving heparin IV. Which laboratory value does the PN monitor (and report) per protocol?
options: INR
Serum calcium
Hemoglobin A1c
aPTT
explain: Correct: D - aPTT monitors heparin effect, with a therapeutic range roughly 1.5 to 2.5 times control. A is wrong - INR monitors warfarin, not heparin. C reflects long-term glucose control, unrelated to heparin. B is unrelated to anticoagulation monitoring.

q: Which medications are high-risk for falls in older adults and should prompt extra precautions and reporting? Select all that apply.
options: Daily multivitamin
Opioid analgesics
Topical moisturizer
Sedative-hypnotics such as zolpidem
Orthostatic-hypotension-causing antihypertensives
explain: Correct: D, B, E - sedatives, opioids, and antihypertensives that lower blood pressure on standing all impair alertness or perfusion and raise fall risk. A and C are wrong - a multivitamin and topical moisturizer do not meaningfully affect fall risk.

q: The PN is preparing to administer insulin. Which type can be given intravenously?
options: Insulin detemir
Regular insulin
Insulin glargine
NPH insulin
explain: Correct: B - only regular insulin may be given IV. D, C, and A are wrong - NPH, glargine, and detemir are for subcutaneous use only; giving them IV is dangerous.

q: A post-op client has a temperature of 100.8 F (38.2 C) on post-op day 2. What is the PN's best action?
options: Document it, continue monitoring, and report per facility thresholds since low-grade fever is common in the first 48 hours
Report it immediately as a surgical emergency, using the equipment available at the bedside
Tell the client fevers after surgery are meaningless, before the end of the shift
Give an antipyretic without an order and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, at this stage
explain: Correct: A - low-grade fever in the first 24-48 hours is often atelectasis-related; the PN monitors, encourages pulmonary hygiene, and reports per protocol. B is wrong - this temperature alone is not an emergency. D is wrong - medicating without an order exceeds scope. C is wrong - fevers are never dismissed; trends matter.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is monitoring a client receiving a blood transfusion. Which finding requires stopping the transfusion and notifying the RN immediately?
options: Infusion running slightly behind schedule
The client asking for water, before the end of the shift
Temperature rise of 2 F with chills and back pain
Mild itching at the IV site, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - fever with chills and back/flank pain suggests a hemolytic transfusion reaction; stop the transfusion, keep the line open with saline, and notify the RN. D alone might be a mild allergic sign to report, but C is the emergency. B and A are non-urgent.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client's potassium is 5.8 mEq/L. The PN should recognize this as:
options: High, and report it to the RN promptly
A value that needs no action
Normal, before the end of the shift
Low, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: A - normal potassium is 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; 5.8 is hyperkalemia, a dysrhythmia risk requiring prompt reporting. C, D, and B misread the normal range.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is caring for a client with a nasogastric tube to suction. Which observation requires immediate RN notification?
options: The client reports nausea, at the patient's bedside
Drainage totals 200 mL over 8 hours
Drainage is greenish-yellow, in practice
The tube is dislodged and the client is coughing
explain: Correct: D - a dislodged tube with coughing suggests possible airway misplacement or aspiration risk; do not reinsert or continue suction without RN/provider direction. C is normal gastric drainage color. A is expected and managed per orders. B is a typical drainage volume.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which actions reduce the risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infection? Select all that apply.
options: Maintaining a closed sterile drainage system
Keeping the drainage bag below bladder level
Performing routine perineal hygiene
Removing the catheter as soon as it is no longer needed
Disconnecting the catheter daily to irrigate routinely
explain: Correct: B, A, C, D - gravity drainage, closed systems, hygiene, and prompt removal all reduce CAUTI risk. E is wrong - routine disconnection and irrigation break the closed system and increase infection risk.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is scheduled for surgery in the morning. Which preoperative findings must the PN report to the RN? Select all that apply.
options: Blood pressure 142/88 mmHg, near baseline
Allergy to penicillin documented on the chart
The client ate a full breakfast despite NPO instructions
The client reports a new cough and fever of 101 F
The signed consent form is on the chart
explain: Correct: C, D - eating while NPO risks aspiration under anesthesia, and new cough with fever may indicate infection requiring postponement. B is wrong to flag as new - a documented allergy is already known, though the PN confirms the band matches. A is near baseline and not alarming. E is the expected state, not a problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is completing the pre-op checklist. The consent is signed, allergies are documented, and the client is NPO. The operative site is not marked. What should the PN do?
options: Proceed since the consent names the procedure
Report the missing site marking to the RN before the client goes to surgery
Mark the site personally to save time, before the end of the shift
Ask the family to mark the site, during the current shift, for now
explain: Correct: B - site marking is a Universal Protocol safety step; a missing mark must be reported and resolved before surgery. C is wrong - the PN does not mark the site; the provider does with the client involved. A is wrong - proceeding without the mark risks wrong-site surgery. D is wrong - family members do not perform site marking.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a lumbar puncture, the PN should position the client flat and monitor for which complication to report?
options: Severe headache that worsens when upright, or clear drainage from the puncture site
A small bandage over the site, for the duration of the patient's stay
Mild thirst, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Sleepiness that resolves with rest, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A - post-dural puncture headache and CSF leak (clear drainage) are complications needing RN/provider notification. C is routine. D is expected post-procedure rest. B is normal wound care.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is monitoring the groin site after a cardiac catheterization. Which finding requires immediate RN notification?
options: A palpable distal pulse, in this case
The client reporting mild groin soreness, on this occasion
A small bruise at the insertion site
Active bleeding or a rapidly expanding hematoma at the site
explain: Correct: D - active bleeding or expanding hematoma signals hemorrhage and needs immediate intervention. C is a common minor finding to document. B is expected post-procedure discomfort. A is the desired normal finding, not a problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A diabetic client is sweaty, shaky, and confused. The fingerstick reads 42 mg/dL. What should the PN do first?
options: Recheck the glucose in 2 hours, at the patient's bedside
Provide a fast-acting carbohydrate per protocol and report to the RN
Give the scheduled insulin dose, and record the intake and output for the shift
Encourage the client to go for a walk, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - 42 mg/dL with neuroglycopenic symptoms is severe hypoglycemia; fast carbs (juice, glucose tablets) per protocol plus RN notification. C is wrong - insulin would worsen hypoglycemia. D is wrong - activity lowers glucose further. A is wrong - waiting 2 hours with symptomatic hypoglycemia is dangerous.

q: Which findings suggest diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)? The PN should report:
options: Diaphoresis, tremors, and hunger, on this occasion
Bradycardia and hypothermia, in accordance with facility policy
Fruity breath odor, Kussmaul respirations, and dehydration
Weight gain and peripheral edema, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - fruity (acetone) breath, deep rapid Kussmaul respirations, and dehydration are classic DKA signs of severe hyperglycemia. A describes hypoglycemia. B is not characteristic of DKA. D suggests fluid overload, not DKA.

q: The PN is reinforcing heart failure teaching. Which client statement indicates a need for further teaching?
options: I will call if I need more pillows to breathe at night
I can stop my water pill when my swelling goes down
I will weigh myself daily and report a gain of 2 to 3 pounds in a day
I will limit sodium as instructed
explain: Correct: B - diuretics must not be stopped without provider direction; stopping leads to fluid reaccumulation. C, D, and A all show correct understanding: daily weights catch fluid gain early, sodium restriction reduces retention, and orthopnea (needing more pillows) is a warning sign to report.

q: A client clutches the chest and reports crushing pain radiating to the left arm. What is the PN's priority action?
options: Give the client a full meal to rule out indigestion, as documented in the plan of care
Have the client walk to the nurses' station, during the current shift
Document the pain and reassess in 30 minutes
Help the client rest, sit upright, and notify the RN immediately
explain: Correct: D - crushing radiating chest pain suggests MI; rest reduces cardiac workload while the RN is notified for emergency orders. B is wrong - exertion increases myocardial oxygen demand. A is wrong - feeding delays care and risks aspiration. C is wrong - waiting 30 minutes with possible MI is unsafe.

q: The PN is reinforcing breathing techniques for a client with COPD. Which technique should be reinforced?
options: Pursed-lip breathing with prolonged exhalation
Holding the breath for 30 seconds repeatedly
Rapid shallow panting
Breathing only through the mouth as fast as possible
explain: Correct: A - pursed-lip breathing slows exhalation, keeps airways open, and reduces air trapping. C is wrong - rapid shallow breathing worsens dyspnea. B is wrong - prolonged breath-holding is unsafe and unhelpful. D is wrong - fast mouth breathing increases air trapping.

q: A visitor reports that a client suddenly cannot speak clearly and the face looks droopy on one side. What should the PN do?
options: Give the client aspirin without an order, during the current shift
Wait to see if it resolves on its own
Note the exact time symptoms started and notify the RN immediately
Assume the client is tired and let them rest, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C - facial droop and aphasia suggest stroke; onset time determines treatment eligibility, so immediate RN notification is critical. D and B are wrong - stroke symptoms are never 'wait and see.' A is wrong - the PN cannot administer medication without an order, and not all strokes should receive aspirin.

q: A client vomits coffee-ground emesis and passes black tarry stools. The PN recognizes these as signs of:
options: Lower intestinal bleeding that can wait until morning, during the current shift
Upper GI bleeding requiring prompt reporting and monitoring of vital signs
Normal effects of iron supplements, before the end of the shift
Constipation that will resolve on its own
explain: Correct: B - coffee-ground emesis and melena indicate upper GI bleeding; the PN monitors vitals for shock and reports promptly. A is wrong - this is not a 'wait until morning' situation. C is wrong - while iron darkens stool, coffee-ground emesis is never normal. D is wrong - these are bleeding signs, not constipation.

q: A client's potassium is 6.2 mEq/L. Which cardiac change is most concerning and why must the PN report it immediately?
options: A slightly fast heart rate, which is always benign, for now
No ECG changes ever occur with potassium shifts, during the current shift
Peaked T waves, because hyperkalemia can cause lethal dysrhythmias
Flattened T waves, because they indicate low calcium
explain: Correct: C - hyperkalemia produces peaked T waves, widened QRS, and can progress to asystole; immediate reporting is essential. D is wrong - flattened T waves suggest hypokalemia, not hyperkalemia. A is wrong - tachycardia is not always benign and misses the point. B is wrong - potassium shifts classically alter the ECG.

q: An older adult client is confused, has poor skin turgor, and dark concentrated urine. The PN should:
options: Recognize probable dehydration, encourage fluids per orders, monitor I&O, and report to the RN
Assume confusion is normal aging and document only, based on the findings documented so far
Restrict fluids to prevent overload, before checking the patient's allergy status for the medication
Give an IV fluid bolus without an order, and report the findings to the healthcare provider
explain: Correct: A - these are classic dehydration signs in older adults; the PN promotes oral hydration per orders, tracks I&O, and reports. C is wrong - restricting fluids worsens dehydration. B is wrong - new confusion is never assumed to be normal aging. D is wrong - IV fluids require an order.

q: The PN is reinforcing pneumonia prevention teaching post-op. Which client statement shows correct understanding?
options: I should stay flat in bed and avoid moving, using the equipment available at the bedside
Coughing will reopen my surgical wound, so I will suppress coughs, for now
I only need to breathe deeply once a day, as documented in the plan of care
I will do my deep breathing and coughing exercises every hour while awake
explain: Correct: D - hourly deep breathing and coughing mobilizes secretions and prevents atelectasis/pneumonia. A is wrong - immobility increases pneumonia risk. B is wrong - splinting the incision with a pillow makes coughing safe. C is wrong - once daily is far too infrequent.

q: After a thyroidectomy, the PN notes the client has tingling around the mouth and a positive Chvostek sign. What should the PN do?
options: Reassure the client this is expected and will pass, during the current shift
Encourage the client to ambulate, and discard the documentation of the event afterwards
Give the client milk to drink, before the end of the shift
Report to the RN immediately; these suggest hypocalcemia from parathyroid injury
explain: Correct: D - perioral tingling and Chvostek sign indicate hypocalcemia, which can progress to laryngospasm; urgent reporting is needed. A is wrong - this is not a benign finding. C is wrong - milk is not a treatment for acute hypocalcemia and oral intake may be restricted. B is irrelevant to the problem.

q: A client with sickle cell disease reports sudden severe chest pain and has a fever. The PN should:
options: Treat it as routine pain and continue the care plan, as documented in the plan of care
Report immediately; chest pain with fever may indicate acute chest syndrome, a life-threatening complication
Apply heat to the chest and reassess tomorrow, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
Encourage the client to wait until the next pain medication dose, while disregarding the patient's reported symptoms
explain: Correct: B - acute chest syndrome is a leading cause of death in sickle cell disease and needs urgent evaluation. A is wrong - new chest pain with fever is never routine. D is wrong - waiting risks deterioration. C is wrong - heat does not treat acute chest syndrome.

q: A client with cirrhosis has a platelet count of 45,000/mm3. Which precaution should the PN follow and reinforce?
options: Use bleeding precautions: soft toothbrush, electric razor, report any bleeding or melena
Allow intramuscular injections without concern, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Avoid all activity, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
Encourage contact sports to build strength, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A - thrombocytopenia (normal 150,000-400,000) raises bleeding risk; gentle hygiene measures and bleeding surveillance are essential. D is wrong - contact sports risk hemorrhage. B is wrong - IM injections can cause hematomas with low platelets. C is wrong - total bed rest is unnecessary and harmful.

q: A client with major burns has a urine output of 20 mL/hr. The PN should:
options: Encourage the client to drink more water, at the patient's bedside
Remove the urinary catheter, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Report it to the RN immediately; output below 30 mL/hr suggests hypovolemia or renal compromise
Document it as adequate, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
explain: Correct: C - burn clients lose massive fluid volume; UO under 30 mL/hr signals inadequate resuscitation or kidney injury. D is wrong - 20 mL/hr is not adequate. A is wrong - oral fluids cannot correct burn shock and the client may be NPO. B is wrong - removing the catheter eliminates the monitoring tool.

q: Which findings suggest hypoglycemia rather than hyperglycemia? Select all that apply.
options: Fruity breath odor
Polyuria
Irritability and confusion
Tremors
Diaphoresis
Dry, flushed skin
explain: Correct: E, D, C - sweating, tremors, and neuroglycopenic symptoms (irritability, confusion) are hypoglycemia signs from sympathetic activation. A is wrong - fruity breath is ketoacidosis (hyperglycemia). F is wrong - dry flushed skin suggests hyperglycemia. B is wrong - polyuria is a hyperglycemia symptom.

q: Which findings are consistent with left-sided heart failure? Select all that apply.
options: Cough with frothy sputum
Dyspnea and orthopnea
Jugular vein distention
Dependent peripheral edema
Crackles in the lung bases
explain: Correct: B, E, A - left-sided failure backs blood into the lungs: dyspnea, crackles, and frothy sputum. C and D are wrong - JVD and peripheral edema reflect right-sided failure (systemic congestion), not left-sided.

q: Which findings suggest a deep vein thrombosis? Select all that apply.
options: Warmth and redness over one calf
Unilateral calf pain and swelling
Tenderness along one leg vein
Bilateral ankle edema that pits equally
A cool, pale foot with absent pulses
explain: Correct: B, A, C - unilateral pain, swelling, warmth, redness, and venous tenderness are classic DVT signs. D is wrong - bilateral symmetric edema suggests systemic causes like heart failure, not DVT. E is wrong - cool, pale, pulseless limb indicates arterial occlusion, not venous thrombosis.

q: The PN is monitoring a client with a head injury. Which findings suggest increased intracranial pressure and must be reported at once? Select all that apply.
options: Blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, stable from baseline
Clear fluid draining from the nose
Unequal or nonreactive pupils
Decreasing level of consciousness
Severe headache with vomiting
explain: Correct: D, E, C, B - declining LOC is the earliest and most sensitive sign; severe HA with vomiting, pupil changes, and CSF rhinorrhea (clear nasal drainage) all demand immediate reporting. A is wrong - stable normal vitals are not an ICP warning sign.

q: Which findings are consistent with Addison's disease (adrenal insufficiency)? Select all that apply.
options: Bronze-like hyperpigmentation of the skin
Hypertension
Hypotension
Moon face and truncal obesity
Hyponatremia and hyperkalemia
explain: Correct: C, A, E - Addison's causes hypotension, ACTH-driven hyperpigmentation, low sodium and high potassium from aldosterone deficiency. D is wrong - moon face and truncal obesity are Cushing syndrome (cortisol excess), the opposite. B is wrong - Addison's causes hypotension, not hypertension.

q: Which are early signs of shock the PN should report immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Restlessness and anxiety
Tachycardia
Bradycardia
Hypotension
Cool, clammy skin
Warm, dry, flushed skin
explain: Correct: B, A, E, D - compensatory tachycardia, restlessness from cerebral hypoperfusion, cool clammy skin from vasoconstriction, and hypotension are early shock signs. F is wrong - warm dry skin suggests the early distributive phase or is simply not the classic early sign pattern tested here; in early hypovolemic shock skin is cool and clammy. C is wrong - bradycardia is a late, pre-arrest sign, not early.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for a client with chronic pancreatitis. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I must avoid alcohol completely
I will eat small, low-fat meals
Smoking does not affect my pancreas
I should take my pancreatic enzyme replacements with meals as prescribed
A high-fat diet will help me gain weight
explain: Correct: A, B, D - alcohol abstinence, low-fat small meals, and enzymes with meals reduce pancreatic stimulation and aid digestion. E is wrong - high-fat meals trigger pain and flares. C is wrong - smoking worsens pancreatitis and raises pancreatic cancer risk.

q: Which measures help prevent COPD exacerbations? Select all that apply.
options: Ignoring mild increases in shortness of breath
Exercising vigorously outdoors on high-pollution days
Smoking cessation
Reporting increased sputum volume or color change promptly
Annual influenza and pneumococcal vaccines as recommended
explain: Correct: C, E, D - quitting smoking, recommended vaccines, and early reporting of sputum changes prevent and catch exacerbations early. B is wrong - exertion in polluted air can trigger bronchospasm. A is wrong - ignoring worsening dyspnea delays treatment.

q: Which PN responses demonstrate therapeutic communication? Select all that apply.
options: Tell me more about what you are experiencing
I think you should just stop worrying so much
Everything will turn out fine, do not worry
The nurse remains silent to give the client time to gather thoughts
You seem anxious about the test results
explain: Correct: A, E, D - open-ended exploration, reflecting observed feelings, and purposeful silence are therapeutic techniques. C is wrong - false reassurance dismisses the client's concern. B is wrong - giving advice ('you should') blocks the client's own problem-solving.

q: The PN is caring for a client with major depression. Which findings require immediate reporting to the RN? Select all that apply.
options: A sudden calm mood after a period of deep depression
The client is giving away personal possessions
The client talks about looking forward to a grandchild's visit
The client states, 'Everyone would be better off without me'
The client asks for a second helping at dinner
explain: Correct: D, B, A - direct statements of worthlessness/burden, giving away possessions, and sudden calm (which may signal a decided suicide plan) are all red flags requiring immediate reporting. E is wrong - improved appetite alone is not a danger signal. C is wrong - future-oriented statements are generally protective, not warning signs.

q: The charge RN is making assignments. Which client is the most appropriate assignment for the PN?
options: A client with multisystem failure needing ventilator management
A client being discharged after new colostomy surgery needing initial ostomy teaching
A stable client with diabetes needing routine insulin administration and glucose monitoring
A newly admitted client with undiagnosed abdominal pain needing an initial assessment, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - a stable diabetic client needing routine meds and monitoring fits PN scope. D is wrong - initial assessments belong to the RN. A is wrong - unstable multisystem clients need RN-level care. B is wrong - initial ostomy teaching is the RN's role; the PN reinforces later.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A provider gives a telephone order for pain medication. The facility policy states only RNs may accept telephone orders. The PN should:
options: Decline to accept it and ask the provider to give the order to the RN
Take the order anyway to avoid delaying pain relief, at the patient's bedside
Ignore the provider's call, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Take the order and have the UAP carry it out, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A - the PN follows scope and facility policy; telephone orders go to the RN. B is wrong - policy and scope exist for safety; violating them is not justified by urgency. D is wrong - UAPs cannot carry out medication orders. C is wrong - ignoring the provider abandons the client's pain need; redirecting is the professional action.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN disagrees with the RN's plan for a client's care. What is the PN's best first step?
options: Carry out the plan silently even though it seems wrong
Discuss the concern directly and respectfully with the RN
Complain to other staff about the RN, before the end of the shift
Change the plan without telling the RN, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - the chain of communication starts with direct, respectful discussion with the RN. A is wrong - silently carrying out a plan believed unsafe violates the PN's duty. C is wrong - gossip solves nothing and is unprofessional. D is wrong - unilaterally changing the plan breaks teamwork and accountability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: When documenting client care, the PN should chart:
options: At the end of the week from memory, in accordance with facility policy
Only abnormal findings, skipping routine care, as part of the routine care for this patient
Subjective opinions about the client's attitude, during the current shift
Objective observations, actions taken, and the client's response, promptly after care
explain: Correct: D - documentation must be objective, complete, and timely to support continuity and legal defense. C is wrong - opinions and judgments do not belong in the record. B is wrong - routine care also needs documenting to show it was done. A is wrong - delayed charting from memory is inaccurate and unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is giving a handoff report to the oncoming nurse. Which information is most important to include?
options: A detailed history of the client's childhood, in accordance with facility policy
The client's favorite television shows, while maintaining standard precautions throughout
Current status, recent changes, pending orders, and safety concerns such as fall risk
The PN's personal impressions of the client's family
explain: Correct: C - handoff must convey current status, changes, pending items, and safety risks for continuity. B and A are irrelevant to safe care. D is unprofessional and non-clinical.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with a do-not-resuscitate order goes into cardiac arrest. The family shouts, 'Do everything!' What should the PN do?
options: Follow the valid DNR order and immediately notify the RN and provider of the conflict
Ask the family to sign a new consent form first, as documented in the plan of care
Begin resuscitation because the family overrode the order, in accordance with facility policy
Leave the room to avoid the conflict, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A - a valid DNR order stands until the provider changes it; the PN follows the order and escalates the conflict. C is wrong - family demands do not override a valid order at the bedside. B is wrong - consent paperwork does not resolve an active arrest situation. D is wrong - leaving abandons both the client and the situation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which task is appropriate for the PN to assign to the UAP?
options: Deciding whether a client's pain requires medication
Interpreting a client's telemetry rhythm strip
Performing the admission skin assessment
Feeding a client who has no swallowing precautions
explain: Correct: D - feeding a client without dysphagia is a routine task delegable to UAP. A is wrong - pain assessment decisions require nursing judgment. B is wrong - rhythm interpretation is beyond both UAP and PN independent scope. C is wrong - admission assessments belong to the RN.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN notes the RN documented vital signs that the PN knows were never taken. What should the PN do?
options: Confront the RN angrily at the nurses' station
Report the falsification through the chain of command per facility policy
Ignore it; documentation is the RN's business, at the patient's bedside
Chart the same vital signs to match, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: B - falsified documentation endangers clients and is unethical; the PN reports through proper channels. C is wrong - ignoring fraud makes the PN complicit. A is wrong - public confrontation is unprofessional and unsafe. D is wrong - copying false data spreads the falsification.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client asks the PN to pray with them before surgery. The PN is comfortable doing so. What is the best action?
options: Call security because the request is inappropriate, as documented in the plan of care
Refuse, saying religion has no place in nursing, during the current shift
Respectfully participate or arrange for the client's spiritual support per their wishes
Tell the client to pray silently alone, while ensuring the call light is within the patient's reach
explain: Correct: C - supporting the client's spiritual needs is part of holistic care when the PN is comfortable. B is wrong - refusing abruptly dismisses a valid coping resource. D is wrong - it rejects the client's request for presence. A is wrong - a prayer request is not a security issue.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is reinforcing hospice teaching with a family. Which statement shows the family understands hospice?
options: Hospice means we can no longer visit
Hospice focuses on comfort and quality of life, not cure
Hospice will try experimental treatments to cure the cancer
Hospice is only for the last 24 hours of life
explain: Correct: B - hospice provides comfort-focused palliative care. C is wrong - hospice does not pursue curative or experimental treatment. A is wrong - family presence is encouraged. D is wrong - hospice can begin months before death when prognosis qualifies.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with limited English needs discharge instructions reinforced. What should the PN do?
options: Use a qualified medical interpreter to reinforce the teaching
Ask the client's 10-year-old child to interpret
Skip the teaching since it was already given once
Speak loudly and slowly in English until the client nods
explain: Correct: A - qualified interpreters ensure accurate, confidential communication. B is wrong - children should never interpret medical information. D is wrong - volume does not overcome a language barrier and nodding may just be politeness. C is wrong - understanding must be verified, not assumed.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN receives a report that a client fell but was not injured. The RN has assessed the client. What is the PN's responsibility now?
options: Decide the client needs no further observation, as documented in the plan of care
Tell the client the fall was their own fault, for now
Remove all fall precautions since there was no injury, at the patient's bedside
Document the PN's own objective observations and continue fall precautions and monitoring
explain: Correct: D - the PN documents objectively and maintains precautions; falls increase repeat-fall risk. A is wrong - post-fall monitoring is still required. B is wrong - blaming the client is nontherapeutic. C is wrong - precautions should be strengthened, not removed, after a fall.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which situations require the PN to advocate by reporting to the RN? Select all that apply.
options: A family member disagrees with the client's own treatment decision and pressures staff
A client is sleeping comfortably after pain medication
A provider has not responded to pages about a deteriorating client
A client's pain remains 8/10 after the maximum ordered PRN dose
A client's cultural dietary request is being ignored by food services
explain: Correct: D, C, E, A - uncontrolled pain, unresponsive provider, ignored cultural needs, and family pressure against client autonomy all require RN escalation and advocacy. B is wrong - comfortable sleep after effective pain relief is a good outcome needing no advocacy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care
