q: The PN is supervising a newly hired UAP. Which observations require the PN to intervene and re-educate? Select all that apply.
options: The UAP raises the bed to waist height before providing care
The UAP performs hand hygiene before client contact
The UAP tells a client the pain medication 'is not due yet' instead of reporting the request to the nurse
The UAP leaves a confused client's bed in the high position and walks away
The UAP reports a client's request for pain medication promptly
explain: Correct: D, C - leaving a confused client's bed high and unattended is a fall hazard, and the UAP must never make medication-timing decisions; pain medication requests must be reported to the nurse promptly. B, A, and E are correct UAP behaviors: hand hygiene, ergonomic bed height during care, and prompt reporting.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions protect client confidentiality? Select all that apply.
options: Shredding printed handoff sheets when no longer needed
Posting about an interesting case on social media without names
Logging off the computer when leaving the workstation
Discussing client information only in private areas with the care team
Sharing a client's diagnosis with the client's employer who calls to ask
explain: Correct: D, C, A - private discussions, logging off, and shredding handoff sheets protect PHI. E is wrong - employers have no right to client health information. B is wrong - even de-identified case posts risk re-identification and violate policy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN witnesses the signing of a consent form. Which statements about the PN's role are true? Select all that apply.
options: The PN signs as witness after consent is properly obtained
The PN confirms the provider explained the procedure and answered questions
The PN verifies the client signed voluntarily and appears competent
The PN explains the surgical risks to the client before witnessing
The PN may obtain consent if the provider is busy
explain: Correct: C, B, A - the witness confirms voluntary signature, apparent competence, and that explanation occurred, then signs. D is wrong - explaining risks is the provider's job, not the witness's. E is wrong - the PN never obtains informed consent independently.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which clients should the PN recognize as needing more frequent monitoring and possible RN reassignment? Select all that apply.
options: A stable client awaiting discharge tomorrow
A client reading quietly with stable vital signs
A newly admitted client whose assessment is incomplete
A client receiving a first dose of IV antibiotics
A client whose condition is deteriorating despite interventions
explain: Correct: E, C, D - deteriorating, newly admitted unassessed, and first-dose IV antibiotic clients (anaphylaxis risk) need RN-level vigilance. A and B describe stable clients appropriate for routine PN care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A fire extinguisher is needed for a small trash fire. The PN remembers PASS. What is the correct sequence?
options: Pull the pin, Aim at the base, Squeeze the handle, Sweep side to side
Point, Activate, Saturate, Stop, as documented in the plan of care
Push the alarm, Aim high, Spray widely, Stand back, in accordance with facility policy
Pull the pin, Aim at the flames' top, Shake, Spray, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: A - PASS: Pull pin, Aim at the base of the fire, Squeeze handle, Sweep side to side. C scrambles the steps and aims wrong. D aims at flame tops instead of the base. B is a fabricated acronym.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN notices a frayed electrical cord on a client's IV pump. What should the PN do?
options: Ignore it since the pump is still working, at the patient's bedside
Remove the pump from service, label it, and report it per policy
Wrap it with tape and keep using the pump, and wash hands before and after the procedure
Plug it into a different outlet and continue
explain: Correct: B - damaged cords are shock and fire hazards; the device must be tagged out and reported. C is wrong - tape does not make a frayed cord safe. D is wrong - changing outlets does not fix the cord. A is wrong - 'still working' does not mean safe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is receiving oxygen by nasal cannula. Which safety instruction should the PN reinforce?
options: It is safe to use an electric razor near oxygen, at the patient's bedside
Oxygen tubing can be draped over a space heater, on this occasion
No smoking, open flames, or petroleum-based products near oxygen
Smoking is allowed if the oxygen is turned off briefly
explain: Correct: C - oxygen supports combustion; smoking, flames, and petroleum products are fire hazards. D is wrong - smoking is never safe around oxygen, even briefly. B is wrong - heat sources near tubing are dangerous. A is a distractor; the key tested rule is the no-smoking/no-flame/no-petroleum trio.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing poison prevention teaching for parents of a toddler. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will induce vomiting first and call later if needed, as documented in the plan of care
Child-resistant caps mean the product is safe to leave out, before the end of the shift
Syrup of ipecac should be given for every swallowed poison, for now
I will keep the poison control number handy and store chemicals locked away
explain: Correct: D - locked storage plus the poison control number is the prevention standard. C is wrong - ipecac is no longer routinely recommended. B is wrong - child-resistant does not mean child-proof. A is wrong - call poison control first; vomiting is not always indicated and can cause harm.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing safe infant sleep teaching. Which statement by the parent indicates correct understanding?
options: The baby should sleep on the stomach with soft blankets
The baby sleeps on the back, on a firm mattress with nothing soft in the crib
The baby can share our bed if we are light sleepers, at the patient's bedside
Bumper pads make the crib safer, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - back to sleep, firm mattress, bare crib reduces SIDS risk. A is wrong - prone sleeping and soft bedding increase SIDS risk. C is wrong - bed-sharing raises suffocation and SIDS risk. D is wrong - bumpers are a suffocation hazard.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with a seizure disorder is being discharged. Which home safety point should the PN reinforce?
options: Avoid showers and take only tub baths and continue to monitor the patient closely for changes
Stop medication once seizures have not occurred for a month, then follow up with the laboratory for the pending results
Take showers rather than tub baths, avoid heights and unsupervised swimming, and take medication as prescribed
Swim alone to build independence, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, in this case
explain: Correct: C - showers reduce drowning risk, heights and solo swimming are hazards, and adherence prevents seizures. D is wrong - swimming alone risks drowning during a seizure. A is wrong - tub baths are the drowning hazard, not showers. B is wrong - stopping antiepileptics without provider direction invites rebound seizures.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is teaching about scald prevention for a family with young children. The PN should reinforce setting the water heater to:
options: 160 F for better dish sterilization
140 F to save energy
The maximum setting for faster hot water
No higher than 120 F
explain: Correct: D - 120 F or below prevents tap-water scalds in children. A, B, and C all risk serious burns; hotter settings scald small children in seconds.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with an implanted pacemaker is scheduled for an MRI. What should the PN do?
options: Report the pacemaker to the RN before the MRI; metal devices can be dangerous in the MRI scanner
Tell the client the pacemaker will improve the images, using the equipment available at the bedside
Remove the pacemaker at the bedside, in accordance with facility policy
Send the client to MRI as scheduled, before administering any further medication
explain: Correct: A - implanted metal/electronic devices are major MRI safety risks requiring screening and RN/provider review. D is wrong - proceeding without screening is dangerous. C is wrong - the PN never removes implanted devices. B is wrong and nonsensical.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client's restraint order was written 4 hours ago and the client remains agitated. The PN should:
options: Follow policy: reassess, ensure the order is still valid/renewed, monitor closely, and report to the RN
Continue the restraints indefinitely since the client is still agitated, using the equipment available at the bedside
Tighten the restraints for better control, while keeping the patient safe from injury at all times
Remove the restraints because 4 hours is too long and verify the result with a second measurement
explain: Correct: A - restraint orders are time-limited and require reassessment, renewal, monitoring, and reporting. B is wrong - restraints cannot continue indefinitely without valid orders. D is wrong - the PN does not unilaterally discontinue; RN/provider direction is needed. C is wrong - restraints must never impair circulation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is diagnosed with influenza. Which precautions should the PN follow? Select all that apply.
options: Wearing an N95 respirator for all routine care
Performing hand hygiene before and after contact
Placing the client in a private room or cohorting
Keeping the door sealed with negative pressure
Wearing a surgical mask when within 3 feet of the client
explain: Correct: E, C, B - influenza requires droplet precautions: surgical mask within 3 feet, private room/cohort, hand hygiene. A and D are wrong - N95 respirators and negative-pressure rooms are for airborne diseases like TB, not droplet-spread influenza.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which precautions are required? Select all that apply.
options: A surgical mask on the client during transport
A gown and gloves for all routine contact
Keeping the room door closed
A negative-pressure private room
Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator
explain: Correct: E, D, A, C - TB is airborne: N95 for staff, negative-pressure room, mask on the client during transport, door closed. B is wrong - gown and gloves for all routine contact is contact-precaution practice, not required for TB alone.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which interventions are appropriate seizure precautions in the hospital? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the bed in the lowest position
Padding the side rails
Placing a tongue blade at the bedside for use during a seizure
Having suction and oxygen equipment available
Restraining the client's arms at all times
explain: Correct: A, D, B - low bed, suction/oxygen ready, and padded rails protect during a seizure. E is wrong - routine arm restraints are inappropriate and harmful. C is wrong - nothing is ever placed in the mouth during a seizure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing toilet training teaching. Which statement indicates the parent understands readiness?
options: Training must be finished before age 2, before administering any further medication
Training should start at exactly 18 months for every child, for now
We will start when our child stays dry for longer periods and shows interest
Punishment speeds up toilet training, while maintaining standard precautions throughout
explain: Correct: C - readiness cues (longer dry periods, interest, communication) guide timing, not the calendar. B and A are wrong - rigid age deadlines ignore developmental variation. D is wrong - punishment causes anxiety and setbacks.

q: The PN reinforces dental health teaching for a young child. Which statement by the parent indicates correct understanding?
options: Dental visits can wait until adulthood, at the patient's bedside
Baby teeth do not matter since they fall out
We will put the baby to bed with a bottle of juice, during the current shift
We will brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and limit sugary drinks
explain: Correct: D - twice-daily fluoride brushing and limiting sugar prevent caries. C is wrong - bedtime juice bottles cause baby-bottle tooth decay. B is wrong - decayed baby teeth affect nutrition, speech, and permanent teeth. A is wrong - early dental visits establish prevention.

q: A pregnant client asks about exercise. The PN reinforces that she should:
options: Exercise only in the third trimester, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
Continue moderate exercise as approved by her provider, avoiding contact sports and overheating
Avoid all exercise during pregnancy, while encouraging the patient to ambulate as tolerated
Begin intense new training to prepare for labor, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - moderate provider-approved exercise is beneficial; contact sports and overheating are avoided. C is wrong - blanket avoidance is not recommended for uncomplicated pregnancies. D is wrong - starting intense new training is unsafe. A is wrong - there is no third-trimester-only rule.

q: The PN is reinforcing osteoporosis prevention teaching for a postmenopausal client. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: Only medication can prevent bone loss, during the current shift
High alcohol intake strengthens bones, using the equipment available at the bedside
I will get calcium, vitamin D, do weight-bearing exercise, and avoid smoking
Bed rest is the best way to protect my bones, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: C - calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, and not smoking all protect bone density. D is wrong - immobility accelerates bone loss. A is wrong - lifestyle measures are foundational. B is wrong - excess alcohol harms bone.

q: The PN reinforces skin cancer prevention teaching. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I only need sunscreen at the beach in summer, and check the patient's allergy band before proceeding
I will use broad-spectrum sunscreen, seek shade midday, and report new or changing moles
A base tan protects me from skin cancer, during the current shift
Tanning beds are safer than sunlight, and evaluate whether the patient's goals were met
explain: Correct: B - daily broad-spectrum protection, midday shade, and mole surveillance are the prevention standard. A is wrong - UV exposure is year-round. C is wrong - any tan is skin damage. D is wrong - tanning beds emit concentrated carcinogenic UV.

q: The PN reinforces testicular self-exam teaching for a young adult male. The key point to reinforce is:
options: Perform monthly self-exam and report any lump, swelling, or change to the provider
Self-exam replaces all provider visits, before administering any further medication
Exams are only needed after age 60, based on the findings documented so far
Only athletes need to do this, while keeping the patient safe from injury at all times
explain: Correct: A - monthly self-exam with prompt reporting of changes supports early detection. C is wrong - testicular cancer peaks in young men. B is wrong - self-exam supplements, not replaces, care. D is wrong - risk is not limited to athletes.

q: Which health promotion topics should the PN reinforce for a school-age child? Select all that apply.
options: Avoiding tobacco and alcohol
Skipping meals to stay thin
Playing unsupervised near busy streets
Using a seatbelt on every car ride
Wearing a helmet when bicycling
explain: Correct: E, D, A - helmets, seatbelts, and substance avoidance are core school-age safety topics. B is wrong - skipping meals risks disordered eating and poor growth. C is wrong - busy streets are a major injury risk.

q: The PN reinforces healthy-aging teaching for an older adult. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I should accept confusion as a normal part of aging
Isolation is fine as long as I am comfortable
I will stay physically active as my provider recommends
I will keep up with recommended vaccines
I will have regular vision and hearing checks
explain: Correct: C, D, E - activity, immunizations, and sensory screening support healthy aging. A is wrong - new confusion is never normal aging and must be evaluated. B is wrong - social isolation harms health; connection matters.

q: A client with a new colostomy says, 'My life is over; nobody will want to be near me.' The PN recognizes this as:
options: A sign the client is ready for discharge, as documented in the plan of care
A normal reaction that needs no response, before the end of the shift
Denial, requiring immediate confrontation, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
An expression of grief and body-image distress needing therapeutic listening and RN notification
explain: Correct: D - grief and altered body image are expected; the PN listens therapeutically and reports so the RN can arrange support resources. B is wrong - distress should never be ignored. C is wrong - this is grief, not denial, and confrontation is nontherapeutic. A is wrong - emotional distress does not signal discharge readiness.

q: A client who was just diagnosed with diabetes says, 'There is no way I have diabetes; the lab made a mistake.' This is an example of:
options: Denial
Rationalization
Projection
Compensation
explain: Correct: A - denial rejects an unwelcome reality. C is wrong - projection attributes one's own feelings to others. B is wrong - rationalization creates logical excuses, not outright rejection. D is wrong - compensation offsets a weakness with a strength.

q: A client with schizophrenia says, 'The voices are telling me the food is poisoned.' What is the PN's best response?
options: Agree that the food might be poisoned to build trust, as part of the patient's ongoing care
State that you do not hear the voices, the food is safe, and encourage eating while notifying the RN
Remove all food from the room permanently, as documented in the plan of care
Argue that voices are not real, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - do not reinforce the hallucination; present reality calmly, encourage nutrition, and report. A is wrong - agreeing validates the delusion. D is wrong - arguing increases agitation without helping. C is wrong - removing all food harms nutrition and does not treat psychosis.

q: The PN is caring for a client in a manic episode. Which approach is best?
options: Leave the client alone to rest
Provide stimulating group activities to burn energy
Reduce stimuli, offer finger foods, and set firm limits
Engage in lengthy debates about the client's grand plans
explain: Correct: C - low stimulation, portable nutrition, and clear limits match manic needs. B is wrong - stimulation worsens mania. D is wrong - debating grandiose ideas is fruitless and escalating. A is wrong - unsupervised manic clients may act impulsively and unsafely.

q: A client is having a panic attack. What should the PN do first?
options: Immediately give a PRN sedative without assessment
Leave the client alone to calm down, at the patient's bedside
Tell the client their fear is irrational, before the end of the shift
Stay with the client, speak calmly, and guide slow breathing
explain: Correct: D - presence, calm voice, and breathing guidance reduce panic; the PN stays and reports. B is wrong - leaving an acutely panicked client is unsafe. C is wrong - calling fear irrational is judgmental and escalating. A is wrong - medication requires assessment and follows orders, not reflex dosing.

q: A family reports their older parent suddenly became confused and agitated overnight. The PN should recognize this as most consistent with:
options: Delirium, an acute change needing prompt evaluation and RN notification
Dementia, which needs no urgent action, at the patient's bedside
Stubbornness, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Normal aging, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - sudden confusion is delirium until proven otherwise, often from infection, meds, or dehydration, and needs urgent workup. D is wrong - acute confusion is never normal aging. B is wrong - dementia is gradual; sudden change is delirium. C is dismissive and unsafe.

q: Which actions maintain a safe therapeutic milieu on a mental health unit? Select all that apply.
options: Ignoring a client's pacing to avoid confrontation
Allowing unrestricted access to sharps for independence
Removing or securing objects that could be used for self-harm
Monitoring clients for escalating behavior
Keeping emergency equipment and protocols accessible
explain: Correct: C, D, E - environmental safety, behavioral monitoring, and emergency readiness protect everyone. B is wrong - sharps access invites self-harm. A is wrong - pacing can signal escalating agitation that needs early intervention, not ignoring.

q: Which family behaviors are examples of enabling a client with alcohol use disorder? Select all that apply.
options: Taking over all household duties so the client faces no consequences
Calling the client's employer with excuses to cover absences
Setting clear boundaries about alcohol in the home
Bringing alcohol to the client during treatment
Encouraging the client to attend treatment sessions
Lending money the family knows will buy alcohol
explain: Correct: D, B, A, F - supplying alcohol, covering up, shielding from consequences, and funding drinking all enable continued use. E is wrong - encouraging treatment is supportive, not enabling. C is wrong - healthy boundaries oppose enabling.

q: The PN is assisting with range-of-motion exercises for a client on bed rest. The correct technique is:
options: Force joints past the point of pain to maintain flexibility
Perform ROM once a week, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Move each joint through its full range slowly and gently, stopping if pain occurs
Exercise only the arms since legs matter less, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - slow, gentle, full-range movement prevents contractures without injury. A is wrong - forcing past pain tears tissue. D is wrong - all joints need movement. B is wrong - ROM is typically done daily or per orders, not weekly.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing foot care teaching for a client with diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. Which statement indicates a need for further teaching?
options: I will cut my toenails straight across
I can walk barefoot at home since it toughens the skin
I will wear well-fitting shoes and clean socks, during the current shift
I will check my feet daily for cuts or blisters
explain: Correct: B - barefoot walking risks unnoticed injuries that become infected; this needs correction. D, A, and C all show correct understanding: daily inspection, straight-across nail trimming, and protective footwear.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is providing oral care for an unconscious client. What is the correct technique?
options: Skip oral care since the client is not eating, for the duration of the patient's stay
Place the client flat and pour water into the mouth, in accordance with facility policy
Brush aggressively to stimulate consciousness, before the end of the shift
Position the client on the side with head turned, use a swab, and keep suction nearby
explain: Correct: D - side-lying positioning with suction prevents aspiration during oral care. B is wrong - flat positioning with poured water risks aspiration. C is wrong - aggressive brushing injures tissue and does not restore consciousness. A is wrong - unconscious clients still need oral care to prevent infection.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN applies a warm compress as ordered. Which safety measure is most important?
options: Use the hottest temperature the client can tolerate, before the end of the shift
Leave it on indefinitely for maximum effect, based on the findings documented so far
Check the skin frequently and follow the ordered time limit to prevent burns
Apply it directly over an open wound without a barrier, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - heat applications require skin checks and time limits because burns can occur, especially with reduced sensation. B is wrong - indefinite application risks burns. D is wrong - open wounds need sterile technique per orders, not routine compresses. A is wrong - maximum tolerable heat is a burn waiting to happen.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing sleep hygiene teaching for a client with insomnia. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will keep a regular sleep schedule, limit naps, and avoid caffeine late in the day
I should exercise vigorously right before bed, before the end of the shift
Watching exciting shows in bed helps me fall asleep
I will drink coffee late in the evening to relax, using the equipment available at the bedside
explain: Correct: A - consistent schedule, limited naps, and no late caffeine promote sleep. D is wrong - evening caffeine disrupts sleep. B is wrong - vigorous late exercise is stimulating. C is wrong - exciting screen content delays sleep onset.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for a client with a hearing aid. Which action is correct?
options: Turn the volume to maximum for best hearing, for now
Remove the hearing aid before the client showers or sleeps, clean it, and store it safely
Leave the hearing aid in during an MRI, then file the incident report according to facility policy
Share the hearing aid with the roommate who also has hearing loss, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - hearing aids are removed for water exposure and sleep, cleaned, and stored safely. C is wrong - electronic devices are unsafe in MRI. D is wrong - hearing aids are fitted to the individual and never shared. A is wrong - maximum volume causes discomfort and feedback.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is providing perineal care for a female client with an indwelling catheter. The correct technique is:
options: Clean from back to front, while encouraging the patient to ambulate as tolerated
Scrub vigorously with strong soap, before the end of the shift
Skip perineal care since the catheter keeps the area clean
Clean from front to back, using a clean area of the cloth each stroke
explain: Correct: D - front-to-back cleaning prevents introducing rectal bacteria to the urethra; fresh cloth areas prevent cross-contamination. A is wrong - back-to-front spreads bacteria toward the urethra. B is wrong - vigorous scrubbing irritates tissue. C is wrong - catheters increase infection risk, making hygiene more important.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help prevent constipation in an immobile client? Select all that apply.
options: Encouraging activity as tolerated
Encouraging fluids as permitted
Administering prescribed stool softeners
Providing fiber-rich foods as ordered
Restricting all fluids to reduce toileting needs
explain: Correct: B, D, A, C - fluids, fiber, mobility, and ordered stool softeners all prevent constipation. E is wrong - fluid restriction worsens constipation and risks dehydration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for an incontinent client. Which actions protect skin integrity? Select all that apply.
options: Leaving the client in a wet brief overnight to promote sleep
Keeping the skin dry between changes
Cleansing gently and applying barrier cream per orders
Changing soiled briefs promptly
Using scented wipes aggressively for odor control
explain: Correct: D, C, B - prompt changes, gentle cleansing with barrier protection, and dry skin prevent moisture-associated breakdown. E is wrong - scented products and aggressive wiping irritate skin. A is wrong - prolonged moisture exposure damages skin; sleep never justifies it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which body mechanics should the PN use when moving clients? Select all that apply.
options: Widening the stance for a stable base
Keeping the load close to the body
Keeping the back straight and bending at the knees
Asking for help with heavy or unpredictable clients
Twisting at the waist to reposition quickly
explain: Correct: C, B, A, D - straight back, bent knees, close load, wide base, and getting help prevent staff injury. E is wrong - twisting while lifting injures the spine.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client takes NPH insulin at 8:00 AM. When should the PN be most alert for hypoglycemia?
options: Between 9:00 and 10:00 AM, during the current shift
At midnight, 16 hours later, for now
Hypoglycemia cannot occur with NPH
Between 12:00 PM and 8:00 PM, when NPH peaks
explain: Correct: D - NPH peaks 4 to 12 hours after injection, so midday to evening is the highest hypoglycemia risk window. A is too early for the peak. B is past the typical duration. C is wrong - all insulins can cause hypoglycemia.

q: A diabetic client takes metoprolol. What important teaching should the PN reinforce?
options: Metoprolol should be stopped before exercise, during the current shift
Beta blockers prevent all diabetic complications, as documented in the plan of care
Beta blockers can mask the warning signs of hypoglycemia, so monitor glucose closely
Beta blockers increase blood sugar to dangerous levels in everyone
explain: Correct: C - beta blockers blunt sympathetic symptoms like tremor and tachycardia, hiding hypoglycemia; sweating may remain. B is wrong - they do not prevent complications. A is wrong - stopping without orders is unsafe. D overstates - the masking effect is the key issue, not universal severe hyperglycemia.

q: A client takes hydrochlorothiazide. Which finding should the PN report to the RN?
options: Potassium 3.1 mEq/L
Potassium 4.2 mEq/L
Mild increase in urination
Blood pressure 132/84 mmHg
explain: Correct: A - thiazides waste potassium; 3.1 is below the 3.5-5.0 normal range and needs reporting. D is a reasonable BP. C is an expected diuretic effect. B is a normal potassium.

q: A client starting an opioid for post-op pain asks about side effects. The PN should reinforce that the client should:
options: Drink alcohol to boost pain relief, using the equipment available at the bedside
Expect constipation and use fluids, fiber, activity, and ordered laxatives to prevent it
Stop the opioid abruptly once pain lessens without telling anyone, as documented in the plan of care
Drive normally since opioids do not affect alertness, and wash hands before and after the procedure
explain: Correct: B - constipation is nearly universal with opioids and needs proactive prevention. D is wrong - opioids impair alertness; driving is unsafe. A is wrong - alcohol plus opioids risks fatal respiratory depression. C is wrong - changes to pain management need communication with the team.

q: Naloxone is prescribed for a client receiving opioids. The PN understands its purpose is to:
options: Treat opioid addiction permanently, on this occasion
Prevent constipation, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Increase the pain-relieving effect, before the end of the shift
Reverse opioid-induced respiratory depression in an emergency
explain: Correct: D - naloxone is the opioid antagonist used for overdose with respiratory depression. C is wrong - it blocks, not boosts, opioid effects. B is wrong - it does not treat constipation. A is wrong - it reverses acute overdose; it is not addiction treatment.

q: A male client with benign prostatic hyperplasia is prescribed an antihistamine for allergies. What should the PN monitor and report?
options: Urinary retention, since anticholinergic effects can worsen obstruction
Lower blood pressure, on this occasion
Improved allergy symptoms only, as documented in the plan of care
Increased appetite, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A - antihistamines have anticholinergic effects that can precipitate urinary retention in BPH; the PN monitors output and reports difficulty voiding. C ignores the interaction risk. B and D are not the priority concerns with this combination.

q: The PN is reinforcing nitroglycerin teaching for angina. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will keep the tablets in a clear bottle on the windowsill
I will take it while driving to the hospital, during the current shift
I will sit down, take one dose, and call emergency services if pain is not relieved in 5 minutes
Headache and flushing mean I am allergic and should never take it again
explain: Correct: C - sit to prevent syncope, one dose, and emergency help if unrelieved follows standard teaching. B is wrong - driving during angina is unsafe. A is wrong - nitroglycerin degrades in light and must stay in its dark container. D is wrong - headache and flushing are expected vasodilation effects, not allergy.

q: Which findings may indicate digoxin toxicity and must be reported? The PN should watch for:
options: Increased appetite and weight gain
Blurred or yellow-tinged vision, anorexia, nausea, and confusion
Warm, flushed skin, before the end of the shift
Excessive energy and rapid pulse, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: B - visual changes (including yellow-green halos), GI upset, and confusion are classic digoxin toxicity signs. A is wrong - anorexia, not increased appetite, occurs. C is unrelated to digoxin. D is wrong - toxicity more often causes bradycardia and dysrhythmias, not a rapid energetic pulse.

q: A client is starting a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI). Which foods must be avoided? Select all that apply.
options: Red wine and tap beer
Aged cheeses
Fresh vegetables
Plain rice
Cured or smoked meats
explain: Correct: B, E, A - aged, fermented, and cured foods contain tyramine, which with MAOIs can trigger hypertensive crisis. C and D are wrong - fresh vegetables and plain rice are low in tyramine and safe.

q: The PN is reinforcing warfarin teaching. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I need regular INR blood tests as ordered
I will avoid NSAIDs and excess alcohol
I will report unusual bleeding, bruising, or blood in urine or stool
I can start herbal supplements freely since they are natural
I will keep my intake of vitamin K foods consistent
explain: Correct: E, C, B, A - consistent vitamin K, bleeding surveillance, avoiding NSAIDs/alcohol, and INR monitoring are warfarin essentials. D is wrong - many herbals (ginkgo, garlic, ginseng) interact with warfarin; nothing is added 'freely.'

q: The PN is administering prescribed potassium chloride liquid. Which practices are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Diluting it in water or juice as directed and giving with food
Having the client sit upright while drinking it
Giving it on an empty stomach with no fluids
Giving it intravenously by rapid IV push for faster effect
Monitoring for signs of hyperkalemia
explain: Correct: A, E, B - oral potassium must be diluted to protect the GI tract, taken with food and fluids, upright to prevent irritation, with monitoring for excess. D is wrong - IV push potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrest; it is never given that way. C is wrong - undiluted potassium on an empty stomach causes severe GI irritation.

q: A client takes furosemide and gentamicin together. Which finding must the PN report promptly?
options: New tinnitus or hearing changes
Blood pressure 126/78 mmHg, in full
Urine output of 50 mL/hr
Mild thirst, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: A - both furosemide and aminoglycosides like gentamicin are ototoxic; combined use raises the risk, and tinnitus or hearing loss needs prompt reporting. D is an expected mild diuretic effect. C is adequate output. B is a normal BP.

q: Before surgery, the PN should ensure the client has:
options: Eaten a full meal for strength, at the patient's bedside
Removed dentures, jewelry, and nail polish, voided, and is wearing only the gown
Brought valuables into the operating room, as documented in the plan of care
Applied full makeup to look well, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - dentures and jewelry are removed for safety, voiding prevents bladder injury and incontinence under anesthesia, and polish interferes with pulse oximetry. A is wrong - pre-op clients are NPO. D is wrong - makeup interferes with skin assessment. C is wrong - valuables are secured, never taken to the OR.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client says something 'gave way' and the PN sees intestines protruding from the incision. What should the PN do?
options: Give the client water to prevent shock and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, in full
Push the organs back inside and apply pressure, before the patient is transferred to another unit
Stay with the client, cover the wound with a sterile saline-moistened dressing, keep the client NPO and still, and call for the RN immediately
Leave to find the surgeon alone, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: C - evisceration is an emergency: stay, cover with sterile saline dressing, keep NPO/still with knees slightly bent, and get help at once. B is wrong - never push organs back in. D is wrong - the client must never be left alone. A is wrong - oral intake is contraindicated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is reinforcing post-op leg exercises. The purpose the PN should explain is:
options: To build muscle mass quickly, during the current shift
To tire the client so they sleep
To replace the need for ambulation, at the patient's bedside
To promote venous return and help prevent blood clots
explain: Correct: D - ankle pumps and leg exercises promote venous return, reducing DVT risk. A is wrong - post-op exercises are not for muscle building. B is wrong - fatigue is not the goal. C is wrong - exercises supplement, never replace, early ambulation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client's hemoglobin is 7.2 g/dL (baseline 13.5). The PN should:
options: Document it as normal since the client looks fine
Encourage the client to eat red meat immediately, for now
Report it to the RN promptly; the sharp drop suggests bleeding
Recheck it next week, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C - a hemoglobin drop of this magnitude post-op signals possible hemorrhage and needs urgent evaluation. A is wrong - 7.2 is well below normal (12-16 female, 14-18 male). B is wrong - diet cannot correct acute blood loss. D is wrong - waiting a week with possible bleeding is unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest post-op hemorrhage that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: A single small spot of drainage on the dressing
Restlessness and cool, pale skin
Stable vital signs matching baseline
Tachycardia with narrowing pulse pressure
Increasingly saturated dressings
explain: Correct: E, D, B - expanding dressing saturation, compensatory tachycardia, and restlessness with pallor are hemorrhage/shock signs. A is wrong - minimal spotting is expected. C is wrong - stable baseline vitals are reassuring, not alarming.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which measures help prevent post-op deep vein thrombosis? Select all that apply.
options: Sequential compression devices as ordered
Early ambulation as ordered
Leg exercises and ankle pumps
Prolonged bed rest without movement
Keeping the legs crossed for comfort
explain: Correct: B, C, A - ambulation, leg exercises, and SCDs all promote venous return. E is wrong - crossed legs impede venous flow. D is wrong - immobility is the primary DVT risk factor.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which wound findings suggest surgical site infection that the PN should report? Select all that apply.
options: A clean, dry, well-approximated incision
Mild itching along a healing incision
Purulent drainage with a foul odor
Increasing redness, warmth, and swelling around the incision
Fever and increasing incisional pain
explain: Correct: D, C, E - spreading erythema, purulent foul drainage, and fever with worsening pain indicate infection. A is wrong - a clean dry incision is normal healing. B is wrong - mild itching is a common benign healing sensation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client has not voided 8 hours after surgery and reports lower abdominal discomfort. What should the PN do?
options: Insert an indwelling catheter without an order, for now
Assess for bladder distention, encourage fluids and toileting measures per orders, and report to the RN
Tell the client discomfort is expected and ignore it, before the end of the shift
Wait another 12 hours; this is always normal, while ensuring the call light is within the patient's reach
explain: Correct: B - 8 hours without voiding post-op suggests retention; the PN assesses, tries ordered measures, and reports. D is wrong - prolonged retention risks bladder injury. A is wrong - catheter insertion requires an order. C is wrong - dismissing the complaint misses a real complication.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client's white blood cell count is 18,000/mm3 (normal 4,500-11,000). The PN should:
options: Recognize possible infection and report it to the RN
Repeat the test personally in the room
Tell the client not to worry since WBCs fight infection
Document it as normal
explain: Correct: A - leukocytosis suggests infection or inflammation and needs RN/provider evaluation. D is wrong - 18,000 exceeds the normal range. C is wrong - reassurance without reporting misses the clinical significance. B is wrong - the PN does not run lab tests at the bedside.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A diabetic client's bedtime fingerstick reads 52 mg/dL and the client feels shaky. What should the PN do?
options: Put the client to bed and recheck in the morning, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Give the bedtime insulin first, then recheck
Give a large high-fat meal, as documented in the plan of care
Follow protocol: give fast-acting carbs, recheck in 15 minutes, and report to the RN
explain: Correct: D - symptomatic hypoglycemia at bedtime needs fast carbs, 15-minute recheck, and RN notification; overnight lows are dangerous. B is wrong - insulin would worsen the low. A is wrong - sleeping through hypoglycemia risks seizure or coma. C is wrong - fat slows glucose absorption; fast carbs come first.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: During an asthma attack, the PN notes audible wheezing and the client cannot complete sentences. What is the PN's priority?
options: Offer a large meal to calm the client, and confirm the patient's identity using two identifiers
Help the client sit upright, administer ordered rescue medication, and notify the RN
Encourage the client to lie flat and relax, and wash hands before and after the procedure
Document the wheezing and reassess in an hour, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: B - severe attack with speech limitation needs upright positioning, ordered bronchodilator, and urgent RN notification. C is wrong - flat positioning worsens breathing. A is wrong - eating during an attack risks aspiration. D is wrong - waiting an hour with severe distress is unsafe.

q: An older adult with pneumonia becomes newly confused and restless. The PN should:
options: Recognize confusion as a sign of hypoxia or worsening infection in older adults and report to the RN immediately
Restrain the client to prevent wandering, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, on this occasion
Orient the client once and leave, because the patient has tolerated the same intervention before
Assume it is normal aging, under the supervision of the registered nurse
explain: Correct: A - new confusion in an older adult with pneumonia often signals hypoxia or sepsis and needs urgent evaluation. D is wrong - acute confusion is never normal aging. C is wrong - a single orientation attempt does not address the cause. B is wrong - restraints do not treat hypoxia.

q: The PN is reinforcing TB medication teaching. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: One week of medicine cures tuberculosis, before the end of the shift
I only need medication when I cough, at the patient's bedside
I can stop the medications once I feel better, based on the findings documented so far
I must take the medications for the full 6 to 9 months even when I feel well
explain: Correct: D - full-course adherence prevents relapse and drug resistance. C is wrong - stopping early causes relapse and resistant TB. A is wrong - TB needs months of therapy. B is wrong - symptoms do not guide treatment duration.

q: A client is diagnosed with Clostridioides difficile. Which hygiene measure should the PN follow and reinforce?
options: No hand hygiene is needed with gloves on, during the current shift
Alcohol-based hand sanitizer is sufficient, before the end of the shift
Handwashing with soap and water, since alcohol does not kill C. difficile spores
Hand hygiene only before meals, because the patient has tolerated the same intervention before
explain: Correct: C - C. difficile forms spores resistant to alcohol sanitizers; soap-and-water washing physically removes them. B is wrong - sanitizer does not kill spores. A is wrong - hand hygiene is still required after glove removal. D is wrong - hygiene is needed before and after every contact.

q: An older adult client has new incontinence, foul-smelling urine, and increased confusion. The PN should suspect:
options: Normal aging changes, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
A urinary tract infection and report the findings to the RN
Dehydration only, needing no report, then reassess the patient's respiratory status
Medication side effects that will resolve alone, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - new incontinence with confusion and urinary changes in older adults classically signals UTI needing evaluation. A is wrong - these are not normal aging. C is wrong - the findings need reporting regardless. D is wrong - assuming self-resolution without assessment is unsafe.

q: The PN is caring for a client with chronic kidney disease. Which finding is most urgent to report?
options: Potassium 6.0 mEq/L
Blood pressure 138/86 mmHg
A 0.5 kg weight gain since yesterday
Mild ankle swelling
explain: Correct: A - hyperkalemia in kidney disease risks fatal dysrhythmia and needs immediate action. B is mildly elevated but not urgent. D and C are fluid-retention signs to monitor and report routinely, but potassium of 6.0 is the emergency.

q: A pregnant client at 34 weeks reports a severe headache, visual spots, and upper abdominal pain. What should the PN do?
options: Reassure her these are normal pregnancy discomforts
Suggest she lie flat on her back, in accordance with facility policy
Report to the RN immediately; these suggest preeclampsia
Tell her to wait for her appointment next week
explain: Correct: C - headache, visual changes, and epigastric/RUQ pain are preeclampsia warning signs needing urgent evaluation. A and D are wrong - these are never dismissed as normal. B is wrong - supine positioning can cause vena cava compression; left lateral is preferred.

q: A client with placenta previa begins painless bright-red vaginal bleeding. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client that bleeding is expected and needs no report, and proceed without confirming the order in the chart
Perform a vaginal exam to assess dilation and continue to monitor the patient closely for changes
Encourage ambulation to speed labor, while encouraging the patient to ambulate as tolerated
Keep the client on bed rest, monitor vitals and bleeding, avoid vaginal exams, and notify the RN immediately
explain: Correct: D - painless bright-red bleeding suggests placenta previa; vaginal exams can worsen bleeding, so the PN monitors and reports urgently. B is wrong - exams are contraindicated. C is wrong - ambulation is unsafe with active bleeding. A is wrong - this bleeding is an obstetric emergency.

q: The PN assesses a postpartum fundus and finds it boggy and displaced to the right. What should the PN do?
options: Tell the client to ignore it, in accordance with facility policy
Apply firm continuous pressure indefinitely, at the patient's bedside
Massage the fundus gently per protocol, assist the client to void, and report to the RN
Document it as normal, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: C - a boggy displaced fundus suggests bladder distention preventing contraction; gentle massage, voiding, and RN notification address hemorrhage risk. D is wrong - boggy fundus is not normal. B is wrong - rough prolonged pressure injures tissue. A is wrong - ignoring risks postpartum hemorrhage.

q: The PN is reinforcing newborn thermoregulation teaching. Which parent statement indicates correct understanding?
options: We will keep the baby dry, dressed warmly with a hat, and avoid drafts because newborns lose heat quickly
We will bathe the baby in cold water to toughen the skin, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
Newborns regulate temperature as well as adults, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Overheating the room prevents all heat loss, while maintaining standard precautions throughout
explain: Correct: A - newborns lose heat rapidly through a large surface area; drying, warm clothing, hats, and draft avoidance prevent cold stress. B is wrong - cold bathing causes dangerous heat loss. D is wrong - overheating risks hyperthermia. C is wrong - newborn thermoregulation is immature.

q: The PN observes a breastfeeding mother. Which observation indicates effective latch that the PN can reinforce positively?
options: The mother reports sharp pain throughout the feeding, on this occasion, for now
The baby's mouth covers most of the areola with rhythmic sucking and swallowing
Only the nipple tip is in the baby's mouth with clicking sounds, during the current shift
The baby falls asleep within 30 seconds without swallowing
explain: Correct: B - wide latch over the areola with rhythmic suck-swallow indicates effective feeding. C is wrong - nipple-only latch with clicking causes pain and poor transfer. A is wrong - persistent sharp pain signals poor latch needing help. D is wrong - no swallowing means no milk transfer.

q: A 2-day-old newborn is increasingly jaundiced with poor feeding. The PN should:
options: Place the baby in direct sunlight on a windowsill, during the current shift
Stop all feedings until the jaundice clears, on this occasion, for now
Assume jaundice is always normal, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Report to the RN promptly; worsening jaundice with poor feeding needs evaluation
explain: Correct: D - worsening jaundice with poor feeding can signal significant hyperbilirubinemia needing assessment. C is wrong - not all jaundice is benign. A is wrong - windowsill sunlight is ineffective and risks burns and temperature instability. B is wrong - frequent feeding helps clear bilirubin.

q: A client with appendicitis reports right lower quadrant pain. Which order should the PN question or report as concerning?
options: An order for a laxative or enema
IV fluids, on this occasion
NPO status, at the patient's bedside
Vital signs every 4 hours
explain: Correct: A - laxatives or enemas with appendicitis risk rupture; the PN should clarify/report this order. C is appropriate pre-op preparation. B supports hydration. D is routine monitoring.

q: The PN knows an APGAR score of 8 at 1 minute indicates:
options: A score that is never reassessed, and wash hands before and after the procedure
A generally healthy newborn with possibly minor adjustment issues
Severe distress needing resuscitation, on this occasion, for now
Fetal death, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B - APGAR 7-10 indicates good condition; 8 suggests a vigorous newborn with perhaps minor color or tone deductions. C describes scores 0-3. D is wrong - APGAR assesses live newborns. A is wrong - APGAR is repeated at 5 minutes and beyond as needed.

q: Which actions are appropriate when a client is having an asthma exacerbation? Select all that apply.
options: Notifying the RN of worsening distress
Administering the ordered rescue bronchodilator
Encouraging the client to lie flat and breathe into a paper bag
Positioning the client upright
Encouraging slow, controlled breathing
explain: Correct: D, B, E, A - upright positioning, ordered bronchodilator, controlled breathing, and RN notification are the correct response. C is wrong - lying flat worsens breathing and paper-bag breathing is for hyperventilation, not asthma.

q: Which findings suggest preeclampsia that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Severe headache unrelieved by rest
Visual disturbances such as spots or blurring
Blood pressure 158/104 mmHg
Mild ankle swelling at the end of the day
Protein in the urine
explain: Correct: C, A, B, E - hypertension, severe headache, visual changes, and proteinuria are preeclampsia hallmarks. D is wrong - mild dependent ankle edema can be normal in pregnancy; it is not a preeclampsia criterion alone.

q: Which signs indicate respiratory distress in a newborn that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Acrocyanosis in the first hours of life
Grunting with expiration
Intercostal retractions
Nasal flaring
Respiratory rate of 44 breaths/min
explain: Correct: D, C, B - flaring, retractions, and grunting are distress signs needing immediate reporting. E is wrong - 30-60 breaths/min is the normal newborn range. A is wrong - acrocyanosis (blue hands/feet) is normal in the first day.

q: The PN is reinforcing diet teaching for chronic kidney disease. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will follow protein limits set by my provider and dietitian
I will limit sodium, potassium, and phosphorus as instructed
High-sodium processed foods are fine in small amounts daily
I will restrict fluids if my provider orders it
I can eat unlimited bananas and oranges for energy
explain: Correct: B, A, D - CKD diets limit sodium, potassium, phosphorus, protein, and sometimes fluids to reduce kidney workload. E is wrong - bananas and oranges are high-potassium and dangerous in CKD. C is wrong - processed high-sodium foods worsen fluid retention and hypertension.

q: Which precautions should the PN follow for a client with hepatitis B? Select all that apply.
options: Wearing a respirator mask for all routine care
Double-bagging all linens as infectious waste
Reinforcing the importance of household contacts discussing vaccination with their provider
Advising the client not to share razors, toothbrushes, or needles
Standard precautions for blood and body fluids
explain: Correct: E, D, C - hepatitis B spreads through blood and body fluids: standard precautions, no sharing of blood-contaminated items, and vaccination discussion for contacts. A is wrong - hepatitis B is not airborne; no respirator is needed. B is wrong - routine linen handling with standard precautions suffices.

q: The PN is reinforcing GERD teaching. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will eat smaller, more frequent meals
I will avoid lying down for 2 to 3 hours after eating
I will avoid tobacco and excess alcohol
Tight belts and waistbands are fine
I should eat large spicy meals before bed
explain: Correct: B, A, C - staying upright after meals, smaller meals, and avoiding tobacco/alcohol reduce reflux. E is wrong - large spicy late meals worsen GERD. D is wrong - tight abdominal pressure promotes reflux.

q: Which findings suggest bowel obstruction that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: High-pitched bowel sounds early, then absent sounds
Soft, nondistended abdomen with normal bowel movements
Vomiting with inability to pass flatus
Crampy abdominal pain with distention
Increasing abdominal girth measurements
explain: Correct: D, C, A, E - crampy pain, distention, vomiting without flatus, hyperactive-then-absent bowel sounds, and increasing girth all signal obstruction. B is wrong - a soft abdomen with normal stools contradicts obstruction.

q: Which are risk factors for postpartum hemorrhage that the PN should monitor for? Select all that apply.
options: Multiple gestation
Prolonged or rapid labor
A firm, contracted fundus
Large baby (macrosomia)
Retained placental fragments
explain: Correct: B, A, D, E - prolonged/precipitate labor, multiples, macrosomia, and retained fragments all predispose to uterine atony and hemorrhage. C is wrong - a firm contracted fundus is protective, not a risk factor.

q: A client insists on leaving the hospital against medical advice (AMA). What is the PN's best action?
options: Sign the AMA form on the client's behalf and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Physically prevent the client from leaving, then report any change to the oncoming shift nurse
Have security remove the client's belongings and report any abnormal findings to the healthcare provider
Notify the RN and provider, document the client's statements and actions objectively, and reinforce the risks of leaving as the RN directs
explain: Correct: D - competent clients may leave AMA; the PN notifies the team, documents objectively, and reinforces risks without coercion. B is wrong - physically detaining a competent client is false imprisonment. C is wrong - security is not needed for a competent adult leaving. A is wrong - the client signs their own AMA form; the PN may witness.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is documenting a client's pain reassessment after medication. The most important elements to include are:
options: Only the medication name, for the duration of the patient's stay
A note that the client 'tolerated it well' with no details, during the current shift
The pain rating, what was done, and the client's response to the intervention
The PN's guess about why the client has pain, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - pain reassessment documentation needs the rating, intervention, and response to show effectiveness. D is wrong - guesses do not belong in the record. A is wrong - the name alone shows nothing about outcome. B is wrong - vague phrases without data are poor documentation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client's potassium result of 6.1 mEq/L appears in the chart. The PN should:
options: Wait for the provider to notice it, at the patient's bedside
Recheck it with a different lab machine personally
File the result and mention it at the next shift huddle
Report the critical value to the RN immediately per policy
explain: Correct: D - critical lab values require immediate reporting per policy; hyperkalemia can be lethal. C is wrong - waiting for a huddle delays urgent treatment. B is wrong - the PN does not rerun lab analyzers. A is wrong - the PN is responsible for communicating critical results, not waiting.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN believes a provider's order is unsafe for the client. What is the correct sequence?
options: Carry it out and document disagreement, during the current shift, for now
Clarify with the provider; if unresolved, escalate through the chain of command and do not carry out an unsafe order
Change the order to what seems safer, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
Ask the UAP to carry it out instead, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - the PN clarifies first, then escalates; an unsafe order is never carried out. A is wrong - carrying out a known unsafe order violates the duty to protect. D is wrong - delegating does not transfer accountability. C is wrong - the PN cannot rewrite provider orders.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A family member asks the PN for details about another client's condition. The PN should:
options: Decline politely, explaining that client information is confidential
Share only the diagnosis but not the treatment
Ask the other client for permission first, then share freely, during the current shift
Share the information since the families know each other, for now
explain: Correct: A - confidentiality applies to everyone; the PN declines politely. D is wrong - acquaintance does not authorize disclosure. B is wrong - partial disclosure is still a violation. C is wrong - putting the client on the spot is inappropriate; the default is non-disclosure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is contributing to a client's care plan. Which contribution is appropriate?
options: Writing the nursing diagnoses independently, then reassess the patient after the intervention
Ordering diagnostic tests, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Providing collected data such as vital sign trends and the client's reported symptoms
Setting the discharge date, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C - the PN contributes data; the RN synthesizes it into diagnoses and plans. A is wrong - nursing diagnosis is the RN's role. D is wrong - discharge timing is a provider/team decision. B is wrong - the PN does not order diagnostics.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client expresses interest in organ donation. The PN's best action is to:
options: Ignore the comment as unrelated to nursing care, as documented in the plan of care
Acknowledge the interest, document it, and report it to the RN so proper resources are provided
Complete the donor paperwork independently, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
Talk the client out of it, then report the outcome to the registered nurse
explain: Correct: B - the PN supports the expressed wish, documents, and refers to the RN for the formal process. D is wrong - discouraging donation imposes the PN's values. C is wrong - formal consent processes involve designated staff. A is wrong - the wish deserves a response and referral.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN almost administers the wrong dose but catches the error before giving it. What should the PN do?
options: Report the near miss per facility policy so systems can be improved
Only tell the client, on this occasion
Say nothing since no harm occurred, for now
Document that the medication was given, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: A - near-miss reporting drives system improvement and is protected quality activity. C is wrong - silence wastes a learning opportunity. B is wrong - telling only the client does not fix the system. D is wrong - documenting a false administration is fraud.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which action by the PN best demonstrates cost-effective care?
options: Reusing single-use items between clients, before administering any further medication
Opening extra supply kits just in case, and confirm the patient's identity using two identifiers
Using only the supplies needed, avoiding waste, and reporting malfunctioning equipment
Skipping ordered treatments to save money, using the equipment available at the bedside
explain: Correct: C - stewardship means using what is needed without waste. B is wrong - 'just in case' waste raises costs. D is wrong - skipping ordered care harms clients and is not stewardship. A is wrong - reusing single-use items spreads infection.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The RN delegates tracheostomy suctioning for a client with an established trach to the experienced PN. This is appropriate because:
options: The RN is too busy, as documented in the plan of care
UAPs refused to do it, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
Tracheostomies never need suctioning, for the duration of the patient's stay
Suctioning an established tracheostomy is within PN scope when competency is verified
explain: Correct: D - suctioning an established trach is a standard PN skill once competency is confirmed. A is wrong - busyness does not justify delegation; scope and competence do. B is wrong - UAP refusal is irrelevant to scope. C is factually wrong.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client refuses a bath. The PN's best response is to:
options: Have the UAP do it while the client sleeps, at the patient's bedside
Insist the bath is required and proceed anyway, as documented in the plan of care
Skip hygiene for the rest of the hospitalization
Respect the refusal, explore the reason, offer alternatives, and document
explain: Correct: D - clients may refuse care; the PN respects autonomy, problem-solves, and documents. B is wrong - forcing care violates autonomy and can be battery. A is wrong - doing it during sleep is deceptive. C is wrong - one refusal does not end all future hygiene offers.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is caring for a client in isolation for a contagious illness. The client's family is upset about visiting restrictions. The PN should:
options: Explain the reasons for precautions empathetically and reinforce the teaching about safe visiting
Ban the family from the unit, while observing the patient for any adverse reaction
Ignore the family's concerns, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
Let the family visit without precautions to keep them happy, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A - empathetic explanation plus reinforced teaching balances safety and family needs. D is wrong - waiving precautions endangers everyone. B is wrong - banning family is unnecessarily harsh. C is wrong - ignoring concerns damages trust.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A new PN asks what 'standard of care' means. The best explanation is:
options: Whatever the most senior nurse prefers, then notify the provider of any abnormal findings
Whatever the client requests, before the end of the shift, for now
The level of care a reasonably prudent nurse with similar training would provide in similar circumstances
The minimum needed to avoid complaints, based on the findings documented so far
explain: Correct: C - standard of care is the legal benchmark of prudent practice. A is wrong - seniority does not define the standard. D is wrong - complaint-avoidance is not the measure. B is wrong - client requests do not override professional standards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is asked to witness a client's advance directive. The PN should verify that the client:
options: Is over 65 years old, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
Appears to understand the document, is signing voluntarily, and has had questions answered by the appropriate person
Has a terminal diagnosis, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, on this occasion
Has already decided without any discussion, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, for now
explain: Correct: B - witnessing confirms apparent understanding and voluntariness after questions were addressed. D is wrong - some discussion is expected; the witness confirms it happened appropriately. A is wrong - age is not the criterion; competence is. C is wrong - advance directives are for any competent adult.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which tasks can the PN appropriately delegate to the UAP? Select all that apply.
options: Ambulating a stable client
Changing bed linens for a stable client
Deciding which clients need pain medication
Assessing lung sounds
Collecting a urine specimen
explain: Correct: A, E, B - ambulation, specimen collection, and linen changes for stable clients are routine delegable tasks. D is wrong - assessment requires nursing judgment. C is wrong - medication decisions are never delegated to UAPs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is preparing an end-of-shift report. Which items must be included? Select all that apply.
options: The PN's personal opinions about the provider
Pending labs, procedures, or consults
Abnormal vital signs and the actions taken
Fall risk status and safety precautions in place
New orders received during the shift
explain: Correct: C, B, D, E - abnormal vitals with actions, pending items, safety status, and new orders ensure continuity. A is wrong - personal opinions about providers are unprofessional and irrelevant to handoff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions by the PN support continuity of care? Select all that apply.
options: Following the established care plan
Reviewing the chart before providing care
Documenting care promptly and accurately
Making independent changes to the care plan without telling anyone
Communicating changes in condition to the RN
explain: Correct: C, E, A, B - timely documentation, change communication, plan adherence, and chart review all support continuity. D is wrong - silent independent changes fragment care and are outside PN scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with diabetes is NPO for surgery and the RN is titrating insulin per protocol. The PN's appropriate roles include: Select all that apply.
options: Checking fingerstick glucose as ordered
Monitoring for signs of hypoglycemia
Reporting abnormal glucose results to the RN promptly
Offering the client juice while NPO
Independently deciding the insulin dose
explain: Correct: B, A, C - monitoring, ordered glucose checks, and prompt reporting are PN roles. E is wrong - titration decisions belong to the RN per protocol. D is wrong - giving juice violates NPO status.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which statements reflect correct understanding of the PN's accountability? Select all that apply.
options: Accountability ends when the shift ends
The PN can be held liable for carrying out a known unsafe order
Only the RN is accountable for anything that happens on the unit
The PN is accountable for tasks performed, including those delegated to UAPs
The PN must practice within the scope defined by the state nurse practice act
explain: Correct: D, E, B - accountability follows the PN's own actions and delegations, is bounded by the practice act, and includes refusing unsafe orders. A is wrong - documentation and handoff extend responsibility beyond clock-out. C is wrong - every licensed nurse is accountable for their own practice.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Before administering any medication, the PN must verify the client's identity using:
options: The room number, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Asking the roommate to confirm, then notify the provider of any abnormal findings
Recognition of the client's face alone, and wash hands before and after the procedure
Two identifiers such as name and date of birth, checked against the armband
explain: Correct: D - two identifiers (name, DOB) matched to the armband and order is the safety standard. A is wrong - room numbers change and are not identifiers. C is wrong - familiarity is not a substitute for identifier checks. B is wrong - roommates cannot verify identity.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN notes a client's allergy band lists penicillin, but the MAR shows a newly ordered penicillin-type antibiotic. What should the PN do?
options: Hold the medication and report the discrepancy to the RN immediately
Give a smaller test dose, in accordance with facility policy
Give the first dose and watch for a reaction, for now
Remove the allergy band since it may be outdated, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A - an allergy-band versus order mismatch is a critical safety stop; the PN holds and reports. C is wrong - administering risks anaphylaxis. D is wrong - the PN never removes allergy identification. B is wrong - 'test doses' of allergens are dangerous and outside scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client at risk for suicide is admitted. Which environmental safety measures should the PN ensure?
options: Placing the client in a remote room with no observation, at the patient's bedside
Leaving sharps and cords within reach to promote independence
Removing harmful objects, checking the room for hazards, and following observation protocols
Allowing the client to keep all personal items uninspected, at this stage
explain: Correct: C - ligature and sharps removal plus prescribed observation levels protect the client. B is wrong - accessible sharps and cords enable self-harm. D is wrong - personal items must be screened per protocol. A is wrong - isolation without observation is the opposite of safe care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing home oxygen safety teaching. Which statement indicates the client needs further teaching?
options: I will not adjust the flow rate without direction, during the current shift
I can use petroleum jelly on my nose to prevent dryness
I will not smoke while using oxygen, at the patient's bedside
I will keep oxygen away from open flames
explain: Correct: B - petroleum products near oxygen are a fire hazard; water-based products should be used. C, D, and A all show correct understanding: no smoking, no flames, and no unsupervised flow changes.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A toddler is brought to the clinic after swallowing an unknown pill. The PN's first action is to:
options: Wait for symptoms before acting, in accordance with facility policy
Call poison control and report the child's age, weight, substance if known, and symptoms
Induce vomiting immediately, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Give milk to dilute the pill, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B - poison control gives substance-specific guidance; the PN gathers key data first. C is wrong - vomiting is not always indicated and can cause harm. D is wrong - milk is not a universal antidote. A is wrong - waiting wastes the early treatment window.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing car seat teaching for an infant. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: A forward-facing seat is safest for newborns, at the patient's bedside
Car seats are only needed for long trips
The infant should ride in a rear-facing seat in the back seat
The infant can ride in the front seat if held by an adult
explain: Correct: C - rear-facing in the back seat is the standard for infants. D is wrong - holding a baby is never a substitute for a car seat, and the front seat risks airbag injury. A is wrong - newborns must be rear-facing. B is wrong - restraints are needed on every ride.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A confused client keeps trying to leave the unit. Which is the best initial action?
options: Redirect and engage the client, ensure supervision, notify the RN, and consider elopement precautions per policy
Let the client leave since they want to go, in accordance with facility policy
Lock the client in the room alone, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, in practice
Apply restraints immediately, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: A - redirection, supervision, RN notification, and policy-based elopement precautions are the least restrictive safe response. D is wrong - restraints are a last resort with an order. B is wrong - an unsafe confused client must not wander off. C is wrong - locking a client in a room alone is unsafe and inappropriate.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN finds a client on the floor. After assessing for injury and notifying the RN, the PN should first:
options: Help the client up immediately to reduce embarrassment, at the patient's bedside
Tell the client to get up alone, before the end of the shift, for now
Move the client to a chair quickly, in accordance with facility policy
Keep the client still until assessed, then assist safely per the RN's direction
explain: Correct: D - a fallen client is kept still until injury is assessed to avoid worsening harm, then moved safely. A is wrong - rushing the client up risks spinal or fracture injury. B is wrong - an injured client should not get up alone. C is wrong - quick moves before assessment are unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which situation is a 'near miss' that the PN should report?
options: A client complimenting the staff, for now
A medication error that reached the client and caused harm
A wrong dose drawn up but caught and corrected before administration
A routine vital sign within normal limits, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: C - a caught-before-harm error is the classic near miss; reporting it improves systems. B is an actual adverse event, not a near miss. A and D are not safety events at all.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions reduce the risk of health care-associated infections? Select all that apply.
options: Disinfecting shared equipment between uses
Performing hand hygiene between clients
Wearing the same gown for all clients on the unit
Following isolation precautions as posted
Leaving urinary catheters in place for convenience
explain: Correct: B, A, D - hand hygiene, equipment disinfection, and isolation compliance prevent transmission. C is wrong - gowns are single-client use. E is wrong - catheters are removed as soon as unneeded to prevent CAUTI.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is caring for a client with varicella (chickenpox). Which precautions apply? Select all that apply.
options: A negative-pressure room if available
Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator
A surgical mask for routine entry
Placing the client with a roommate who never had chickenpox
Contact precautions for skin lesions
explain: Correct: B, E, A - varicella is airborne plus contact: N95, contact precautions for lesions, negative-pressure room. C is wrong - a surgical mask does not protect against airborne virus. D is wrong - a nonimmune roommate would be exposed.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control
