q: Which are correct steps for donning personal protective equipment? Select all that apply.
options: Putting on the gown first, then mask, then eye protection, then gloves
Donning PPE in the hallway after entering the room
Performing hand hygiene before donning
Putting gloves on over the gown cuffs
Securing the mask snugly over nose and mouth
explain: Correct: C, A, E, D - hand hygiene first, then gown, mask, eye protection, gloves over cuffs, with a snug mask seal. B is wrong - PPE is donned before entering the isolation room, not after.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching about colon cancer screening. The PN should reinforce that screening generally begins at age:
options: 65 regardless of history, as part of the patient's ongoing care
45 for average-risk adults, or earlier if high risk
Only when symptoms appear, on this occasion, for now
25 for everyone, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - average-risk screening starts at 45; high-risk clients start earlier per provider. D is too early for average risk. A misses the recommended start age. C defeats the purpose of screening, which finds disease before symptoms.

q: A parent asks when a child should first see a dentist. The PN reinforces:
options: Only when there is tooth pain, before the end of the shift
Dental visits are unnecessary for children
At age 10, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
By the first birthday or when the first tooth appears
explain: Correct: D - first dental visit by age 1 or first tooth establishes prevention early. A is wrong - waiting for pain means decay is advanced. C is far too late. B is wrong - children need dental care.

q: The PN reinforces shingles vaccine teaching for a 60-year-old. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: The recombinant shingles vaccine is recommended for adults 50 and older
One shingles episode means I never need the vaccine
Antibiotics prevent shingles, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
The vaccine is only for people who never had chickenpox, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A - shingles vaccine is recommended at 50+ even after prior shingles or chickenpox. D is wrong - prior chickenpox is the reason vaccination matters. B is wrong - recurrence is possible, so vaccination is still recommended. C is wrong - shingles is viral; antibiotics do not prevent it.

q: An older adult asks how to stay strong and prevent falls. The PN reinforces:
options: Regular provider-approved exercise including balance and strength activities
Only exercising when feeling unsteady, for now
Complete bed rest to avoid injury, based on the findings documented so far
Avoiding all physical activity after 70, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: A - balance and strength exercise reduce fall risk. C is wrong - bed rest weakens muscles and bones. D is wrong - inactivity accelerates decline. B is wrong - exercising only when unsteady is reactive, not preventive.

q: The PN is reinforcing HPV vaccine teaching for the parent of an 11-year-old. The key point is:
options: The vaccine is only for adults, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment
The vaccine treats existing infections, and confirm the patient's identity using two identifiers
One dose in childhood is never followed by anything else, as documented in the plan of care
Routine HPV vaccination is recommended starting at ages 11-12 to prevent HPV-related cancers
explain: Correct: D - routine HPV vaccination at 11-12 prevents cancer-causing HPV types. A is wrong - the target age is preteen. B is wrong - the vaccine is preventive, not therapeutic. C is wrong - the series involves multiple doses per schedule.

q: A pregnant client asks whether dental cleanings are safe during pregnancy. The PN reinforces that:
options: Dental X-rays are required at every prenatal visit, during the current shift
Routine dental care, including cleanings, is safe and important during pregnancy
All dental care must be avoided until after delivery, at the patient's bedside
Gum disease has no effect on pregnancy outcomes
explain: Correct: B - routine dental care is safe in pregnancy, and periodontal disease is associated with preterm birth, so care should not be postponed. C is wrong - avoiding all care allows disease to progress. D is wrong - gum disease is linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes. A is wrong - routine dental X-rays are not a prenatal requirement.

q: Which immunizations should the PN reinforce for adults 65 and older? Select all that apply.
options: Annual influenza vaccine
HPV vaccine as a first dose at 70
Pneumococcal vaccine as recommended
The full childhood vaccine series repeated yearly
Shingles (recombinant zoster) vaccine
explain: Correct: A, C, E - flu, pneumococcal, and shingles vaccines are recommended for older adults. D is wrong - childhood series are not repeated yearly. B is wrong - HPV vaccination is targeted to younger ages, not initiated at 70.

q: The PN reinforces injury prevention for an adolescent. Which topics are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Wearing helmets for bikes and sports
Seatbelt use on every ride
Trying risky dares to fit in
Avoiding alcohol and drugs, especially with driving
Texting while driving if experienced
explain: Correct: B, D, A - seatbelts, substance avoidance, and helmets prevent the leading causes of teen injury and death. C is wrong - dares risk serious injury. E is wrong - texting while driving is dangerous regardless of experience.

q: A client says, 'I do not need my antidepressant anymore; I feel fine.' What is the PN's best response?
options: Agree and tell the client to stop the medication, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment
Tell the client they will be depressed forever and document the outcome in the patient's medical record
Encourage the client to discuss it with the provider before making changes and report the statement to the RN
Hide the medication so the client cannot stop it, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - feeling better often means the drug is working; changes need provider direction, and the RN must know. A is wrong - the PN never advises stopping. B is wrong - hopeless predictions are nontherapeutic. D is wrong - deception violates trust and autonomy.

q: A client with anorexia nervosa is admitted. The PN's priority in the milieu is to:
options: Comment on the client's appearance to motivate eating, and assess the patient's understanding of the teaching provided
Allow the client to skip all meals to avoid conflict, and verify the order against the medication administration record, on this occasion, for now
Monitor meals and eating behaviors per the plan, provide a structured supportive environment, and report concerns to the RN
Weigh the client openly in front of peers, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, in full
explain: Correct: C - structured monitoring with therapeutic support and RN reporting is the PN's role. A is wrong - appearance comments worsen body image. B is wrong - allowing meal-skipping enables the disorder. D is wrong - public weigh-ins are shaming and nontherapeutic.

q: A client in alcohol withdrawal is tremulous and anxious 12 hours after the last drink. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client that withdrawal is harmless, based on the findings documented so far
Keep the client safe, monitor vital signs, and report to the RN immediately since withdrawal can progress to seizures
Give the client a drink to calm the tremors, while maintaining the patient's privacy and dignity
Leave the client alone to rest, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, at this stage
explain: Correct: B - alcohol withdrawal can escalate to seizures and delirium tremens; close monitoring and RN notification are essential. A is wrong - withdrawal can be life-threatening. C is wrong - giving alcohol is never therapeutic. D is wrong - the client needs observation, not isolation.

q: A client who lost a spouse 2 months ago says, 'I keep expecting him to walk through the door.' The PN recognizes this as:
options: A normal early grief response; the PN listens supportively and reports concerns per the plan
A sign of psychosis, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Abnormal prolonged grief requiring confrontation and notify the registered nurse of the patient's status
Denial that must be broken through immediately, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: A - sensing the deceased's presence is a common normal grief experience; supportive listening is therapeutic. C is wrong - 2 months is early grief, not prolonged disorder. D is wrong - grief is not 'broken through' by confrontation. B is wrong - this is not psychosis.

q: A client discloses intimate partner violence and asks the PN not to tell anyone. The PN's best action is to:
options: Tell the client to go home and work it out, in accordance with facility policy
Promise absolute secrecy, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Confront the partner in the waiting room, before the end of the shift
Explain limits of confidentiality, ensure immediate safety, and report per facility policy and law
explain: Correct: D - safety comes first; the PN cannot promise secrecy about abuse and must follow reporting laws and policy. B is wrong - promising secrecy the PN cannot keep destroys trust. A is wrong - sending the client back without resources endangers them. C is wrong - confronting the partner risks escalation and is unsafe.

q: A client with dementia becomes agitated at sundown. The PN's best initial approach is to:
options: Use a calm routine, reduce noise and shadows, redirect gently, and report patterns to the RN
Argue with the client about the time of day, using the equipment available at the bedside
Restrain the client until morning, while keeping the patient safe from injury at all times
Give a sedative without an order, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: A - sundowning responds to calm routines, environmental tweaks, and redirection; patterns are reported for plan adjustment. B is wrong - arguing with dementia increases agitation. C is wrong - restraints are a last resort. D is wrong - medicating without an order exceeds scope.

q: Which responses are therapeutic when a client expresses hopelessness? Select all that apply.
options: Tell me what is going through your mind
You seem to be feeling hopeless right now
I know exactly how you feel
I will stay with you for a while
Cheer up; things are not that bad
explain: Correct: B, A, D - reflecting feelings, open-ended exploration, and therapeutic presence are appropriate for hopelessness. E is wrong - minimizing dismisses the client's pain. C is wrong - the PN cannot know exactly how the client feels.

q: Which behaviors suggest a client may be experiencing a crisis needing urgent RN notification? Select all that apply.
options: Giving away prized possessions suddenly
Requesting an extra blanket
Extreme agitation with threatening behavior
Calmly reading a book
Stating a plan to harm self or others
explain: Correct: E, A, C - stated harm plans, giving away possessions, and threatening agitation are crisis indicators. D and B are ordinary comfort behaviors needing no urgent action.

q: The PN is teaching a client to use a cane. The correct instruction is:
options: Hold the cane on the weak side, in accordance with facility policy
Hold the cane on the strong side and move the cane with the weak leg
Hold the cane in the middle with both hands, during the current shift
The cane height does not matter, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: B - the cane goes on the strong side and advances with the weak leg for support. A is wrong - weak-side placement provides no support where needed. C is wrong - one-handed use on the strong side is correct. D is wrong - proper height (wrist crease level) prevents poor posture and falls.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for dentures. The correct procedure is:
options: Let the client sleep with them always without cleaning
Store them dry in a tissue, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Clean them over a sink full of water or a towel, using a brush and denture cleaner
Use hot water to sterilize them, as part of the routine care for this patient
explain: Correct: C - cleaning over water or a towel prevents breakage if dropped. D is wrong - hot water warps dentures. B is wrong - they should be stored in water or solution, labeled. A is wrong - dentures need daily cleaning and gums need rest.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with dyspnea is most comfortable in which position?
options: Prone without support, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Flat on the back, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Trendelenburg, on this occasion
High Fowler's or sitting upright leaning slightly forward
explain: Correct: D - upright positioning lets the diaphragm descend and expands lung capacity. B is wrong - flat positioning worsens dyspnea. C is wrong - Trendelenburg pushes abdominal contents against the diaphragm. A is wrong - unsupported prone restricts breathing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing Kegel exercise teaching for urinary incontinence. The correct instruction is:
options: Tighten the pelvic floor muscles as if stopping urine flow, hold, then relax, repeating several times daily
Bear down like having a bowel movement, while monitoring for signs of infection at the site
Hold the breath during the exercises, as documented in the plan of care
Do Kegels only once a month, and record the intake and output for the shift
explain: Correct: A - Kegels strengthen pelvic floor muscles through repeated contraction and relaxation. B is wrong - bearing down strains rather than strengthens. C is wrong - breath-holding raises intra-abdominal pressure. D is wrong - benefits require regular daily practice.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assisting a client with a walker. The correct technique is to:
options: Pull the walker behind while walking, based on the findings documented so far
Move the walker a short distance forward, then step into it while standing upright
Lean heavily over the walker with a hunched back
Push the walker far ahead and step into it, and encourage the patient to report any new symptoms
explain: Correct: B - short forward moves with upright posture keep the walker stable and the client balanced. D is wrong - pushing it far ahead causes overreaching and falls. A is wrong - a walker behind provides no support. C is wrong - hunching impairs balance and breathing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A post-op client needs to cough and deep breathe. The PN should instruct the client to:
options: Avoid coughing to protect the incision, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Take rapid shallow breaths only, before the end of the shift
Cough without any support to build strength, at the patient's bedside, for now
Splint the incision with a pillow, breathe deeply, and cough firmly
explain: Correct: D - splinting supports the incision while effective coughing clears secretions. C is wrong - unsupported coughing is painful and clients will avoid it. A is wrong - suppressing coughs invites atelectasis. B is wrong - shallow breaths do not expand alveoli.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client reports nausea after surgery. Which PN action is best?
options: Encourage the client to lie flat immediately after eating, in accordance with facility policy
Offer a large meal to settle the stomach, because the provider is expected to review the case later today
Provide small sips of clear fluids as ordered, reduce odors, and report persistent nausea to the RN
Give an antiemetic without an order, while disregarding the patient's reported symptoms
explain: Correct: C - small sips, odor control, and reporting follow post-op nausea management within PN scope. B is wrong - large meals worsen nausea. A is wrong - lying flat after intake increases aspiration risk with nausea. D is wrong - medication requires an order.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures promote regular bowel function in a hospitalized client? Select all that apply.
options: Administering prescribed bowel regimen medications
Promoting activity as tolerated
Encouraging fluids and fiber as ordered
Providing privacy and unhurried time for toileting
Encouraging the client to ignore the urge to defecate
explain: Correct: C, B, D, A - fluids, fiber, mobility, privacy, and ordered bowel medications all support regularity. E is wrong - ignoring the urge leads to constipation and impaction.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for a dyspneic client. Which comfort measures are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the environment calm and uncluttered
Placing the client flat with legs elevated
Encouraging slow, pursed-lip breathing
Administering oxygen as ordered
Positioning upright in high Fowler's
explain: Correct: E, D, A, C - upright positioning, ordered oxygen, calm environment, and pursed-lip breathing ease dyspnea. B is wrong - flat positioning worsens breathing difficulty.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which home safety measures help prevent falls in older adults? Select all that apply.
options: Removing throw rugs and clutter from walkways
Installing grab bars in the bathroom
Waxing floors to a high shine
Wearing sturdy, nonskid footwear
Improving lighting, especially at night
explain: Correct: A, B, E, D - clear walkways, grab bars, good lighting, and safe footwear prevent falls. C is wrong - highly waxed floors are slippery and dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is teaching a client to mix NPH and regular insulin. The correct order is:
options: Draw up the clear regular first, then the cloudy NPH
Mixing insulins is never done
Draw up the cloudy NPH first, then the clear regular
Shake the vial vigorously before drawing up
explain: Correct: A - 'clear before cloudy' prevents contaminating the regular insulin with NPH. C reverses the order and risks contamination. D is wrong - insulin is rolled gently, never shaken. B is wrong - NPH and regular are routinely mixed.

q: A client takes levothyroxine. The PN reinforces that it should be taken:
options: At bedtime with a large meal, at the patient's bedside
In the morning on an empty stomach, separate from calcium and iron
With antacids to prevent stomach upset
Only when feeling tired, based on the findings documented so far
explain: Correct: B - morning empty-stomach dosing maximizes absorption; calcium and iron bind the drug. A is wrong - food reduces absorption. D is wrong - it is daily therapy, not as-needed. C is wrong - antacids impair absorption.

q: A client asks why prednisone cannot be stopped suddenly. The PN's best explanation is:
options: Sudden stopping improves immunity, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Stopping suddenly is fine if you feel better, using the equipment available at the bedside
Tapering is only needed for injections, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
The body reduces its own steroid production during therapy, so the dose must be tapered as ordered to avoid adrenal crisis
explain: Correct: D - prolonged steroids suppress the adrenal axis; tapering lets it recover. B is wrong - abrupt stop risks adrenal crisis. C is wrong - tapering applies to oral steroids too. A is wrong - the opposite is true.

q: The PN is reinforcing NSAID teaching. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will take it on an empty stomach for faster relief, as part of the patient's ongoing care
NSAIDs have no effect on the stomach, for now
I will take it with food or milk and report stomach pain or black stools
I can safely double the dose if pain is severe, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - food protects the stomach lining, and pain or melena signals GI bleeding to report. A is wrong - empty-stomach NSAIDs irritate the mucosa. D is wrong - exceeding the dose raises bleeding and kidney risks. B is wrong - GI irritation and bleeding are major NSAID risks.

q: A client takes acetaminophen regularly for arthritis. What is the most important teaching point the PN should reinforce?
options: Do not exceed the maximum daily dose (generally 3,000-4,000 mg) because overdose causes liver damage, and check combination products for hidden acetaminophen
Acetaminophen is completely safe at any dose, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, in accordance with facility policy
It reduces inflammation like ibuprofen, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, on this occasion
Take it with alcohol to increase effect, and verify the order against the medication administration record, since the finding falls within the range documented previously, in practice
explain: Correct: A - liver toxicity is the critical risk, and many combination products hide acetaminophen. B is wrong - no drug is safe at any dose. D is wrong - alcohol plus acetaminophen greatly increases liver injury. C is wrong - acetaminophen is not an anti-inflammatory.

q: A client taking diphenhydramine for allergies drives for a living. What should the PN reinforce?
options: Take extra doses before driving to stay alert and continue to monitor the patient closely for changes
Drowsiness means the drug is not working, in full
It can cause significant drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until the effects are known
It never causes drowsiness, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
explain: Correct: C - first-generation antihistamines sedate; driving and alcohol are unsafe until response is known. D is wrong - drowsiness is common. A is wrong - extra doses worsen sedation. B is wrong - sedation is a side effect, not a sign of failure.

q: A client with hypertension asks about over-the-counter pseudoephedrine for congestion. The PN should:
options: Say nothing; it is the client's choice, in accordance with facility policy
Tell the client to double the blood pressure medication that day, before the end of the shift
Recommend it as completely safe, and ensure the side rails are raised before leaving the room
Advise the client to check with the provider or pharmacist first, since decongestants can raise blood pressure
explain: Correct: D - decongestants can elevate BP and interact with antihypertensives; provider/pharmacist guidance is needed. C is wrong - it is not risk-free in hypertension. B is wrong - the PN never advises dose changes. A is wrong - the PN has a duty to share safety information.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for a client starting an antihypertensive. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will stop the medication once my pressure is normal, before the end of the shift
I will rise slowly from sitting or lying to prevent dizziness
Dizziness when standing is a sign the drug is curing me, for now
I can drink heavily on weekends, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - rising slowly counters orthostatic hypotension. A is wrong - stopping without direction risks rebound hypertension. D is wrong - heavy alcohol raises BP and interacts with the drug. C is wrong - orthostatic dizziness is a side effect to manage and report, not a cure sign.

q: The PN is reinforcing antibiotic teaching. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I should stop the antibiotic if I develop severe watery diarrhea and call the provider
I will take it with a full glass of water as directed
I will take the full course even if I feel better
I will report rash, itching, or difficulty breathing immediately
I can share leftover antibiotics with family members
explain: Correct: C, D, B, A - full course prevents resistance, allergic signs need immediate reporting, proper administration matters, and severe diarrhea may signal C. difficile needing provider direction. E is wrong - antibiotics are never shared; different infections need different drugs.

q: Which are correct practices for safe medication administration? Select all that apply.
options: Checking the order against the MAR using the five rights
Administering a medication another nurse prepared without verifying it
Checking the expiration date
Verifying client identity with two identifiers
Documenting administration promptly after giving it
explain: Correct: A, D, C, E - five rights, two identifiers, expiry checks, and prompt documentation are safety fundamentals. B is wrong - the administering nurse verifies every medication personally.

q: The PN is caring for a client receiving IV potassium. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Verifying the infusion rate against the order and pump settings
Assessing cardiac rhythm per protocol
Giving the IV potassium by rapid bolus if the level is very low
Reporting signs of hyperkalemia such as muscle weakness or ECG changes
Monitoring the IV site for irritation or infiltration
explain: Correct: A, E, D, B - rate verification, site monitoring, hyperkalemia surveillance, and rhythm assessment are essential with IV potassium. C is wrong - IV push potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrest; it is infused at controlled rates only.

q: The order is for 2 g of a medication; available: 500 mg tablets. How many tablets should the PN administer?
options: 4 tablets
8 tablets
2 tablets
0.5 tablet
explain: Correct: A - convert grams to milligrams first: 2 g = 2000 mg; 2000 mg divided by 500 mg per tablet = 4 tablets. D gives 250 mg. C gives 1000 mg, half the dose. B gives 4000 mg, double the dose.

q: Before a thoracentesis, the PN positions the client:
options: Lying on the affected side
Sitting upright leaning forward over a bedside table
In Trendelenburg, on this occasion
Flat on the back, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: B - sitting and leaning forward spreads the ribs and exposes the pleural space. D is wrong - supine does not open the intercostal spaces. A is wrong - lying on the affected side compresses it. C is wrong - Trendelenburg is unrelated to thoracentesis positioning.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before a paracentesis, the PN should ensure the client has:
options: Eaten a full meal, on this occasion
Removed all clothing permanently, at this stage
Voided to empty the bladder and reduce injury risk
Drunk a large amount of water, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - an empty bladder reduces the risk of bladder puncture during paracentesis. A is wrong - clients are typically NPO or lightly restricted. D is wrong - filling the bladder increases injury risk. B is wrong - the client wears a gown, not no clothing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is scheduled for a CT scan with IV contrast and reports a prior severe reaction to contrast dye. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client that contrast reactions are harmless, for now
Proceed with the scan since reactions rarely recur, as documented in the plan of care
Give Benadryl without an order before the scan, at the patient's bedside
Report the history to the RN immediately; premedication or alternative imaging may be needed
explain: Correct: D - prior contrast reactions predict future ones; the team must decide on premedication or alternatives. B is wrong - reactions commonly recur and can be worse. A is wrong - severe reactions can be life-threatening. C is wrong - premedication requires orders.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After an upper endoscopy (EGD) with sedation, the PN should check which finding before offering fluids?
options: Bowel sounds, for now
Blood pressure only
Return of the gag reflex
Urine output, at this stage
explain: Correct: C - the gag reflex must return before oral intake to prevent aspiration after throat anesthesia. B alone is insufficient. A is unrelated to EGD recovery. D does not determine swallow safety.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which items must be verified before a client goes for an invasive procedure? Select all that apply.
options: Signed informed consent on the chart
Known allergies documented and communicated
Correct site marking when applicable
NPO status as ordered
The client's favorite music playing
explain: Correct: A, D, B, C - consent, NPO, allergies, and site marking are Universal Protocol safety checks. E is wrong - music preference is comfort, not a safety verification.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a lumbar puncture, which PN actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the client flat as ordered
Encouraging fluids as permitted
Monitoring the puncture site for drainage or bleeding
Encouraging the client to sit upright immediately
Reporting severe headache, numbness, or weakness to the RN
explain: Correct: A, B, C, E - flat positioning, hydration, site monitoring, and reporting neuro symptoms are correct post-LP care. D is wrong - sitting upright immediately can worsen post-dural puncture headache.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest IV infiltration that the PN should report? Select all that apply.
options: Taut, shiny skin over the area
Swelling around the IV site
Coolness and pallor of the surrounding skin
Blood return in the tubing with free flow
Pain or tenderness at the site
explain: Correct: B, C, E, A - swelling, cool pale skin, pain, and taut shiny skin indicate fluid entering tissue. D is wrong - blood return with free flow suggests a patent line, not infiltration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before a procedure requiring NPO, the PN learns the client drank juice 2 hours ago. What should the PN do?
options: Say nothing; a little juice will not matter, and assess the patient's understanding of the teaching provided
Report it to the RN immediately; the procedure may need to be delayed due to aspiration risk
Document that the client was NPO, and verify the order against the medication administration record, for now
Give the client more juice to settle the stomach, and confirm the patient's identity using two identifiers
explain: Correct: B - recent intake before anesthesia/sedation risks aspiration; the team must know. A is wrong - any intake matters. D is wrong - more intake worsens the problem. C is wrong - false documentation is fraud.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client reports new calf pain and the PN notes unilateral swelling. What should the PN do?
options: Keep the client on bed rest, avoid massaging the leg, and report to the RN promptly as possible DVT
Massage the calf to relieve the pain, while keeping the head of the bed elevated as tolerated
Encourage vigorous leg exercises, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Apply heat and reassess tomorrow, and report the findings to the healthcare provider
explain: Correct: A - unilateral calf pain with swelling suggests DVT; massage could dislodge a clot, so the leg is left alone and the RN notified. B is wrong - massage risks embolization. C is wrong - vigorous exercise is unsafe with suspected DVT. D is wrong - waiting delays diagnosis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is assisting the RN with a blood transfusion check. The PN's role includes:
options: Skipping the identity check to save time, at the patient's bedside
Deciding the transfusion rate independently, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, at this stage
Hanging the blood without any verification, then document the patient's response to the intervention
Verifying client identity with two identifiers and matching the blood product label with the RN per policy
explain: Correct: D - two-nurse verification of identity and product is the critical safety step. A is wrong - skipping checks risks fatal mismatch. C is wrong - unverified transfusion is never acceptable. B is wrong - the rate follows orders and protocol.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client reports leg pain that starts with walking and stops with rest. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Venous insufficiency, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Arthritis that requires no follow-up, and confirm the patient's identity using two identifiers
A muscle strain needing no report, and verify the order against the medication administration record, for now
Intermittent claudication from peripheral arterial disease, which should be reported to the RN
explain: Correct: D - reproducible exertional pain relieved by rest is classic arterial claudication and needs evaluation. A is wrong - venous disease causes aching with prolonged standing, relieved by elevation. C and B dismiss a vascular symptom that warrants workup.

q: The PN is caring for a client with Parkinson's disease. Which observation requires extra safety planning and RN notification?
options: Shuffling gait with freezing episodes and recent near-falls
Soft speech, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Taking medication on schedule, on this occasion
Mild hand tremor at rest, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - freezing gait with near-falls is a major injury risk needing plan adjustment. D and B are expected Parkinson's features to document and accommodate. C is good adherence, not a problem.

q: A client with hypothyroidism reports increasing fatigue, cold intolerance, and constipation. The PN should:
options: Suggest the client just needs more sleep, and verify the order against the medication administration record, in full
Document the symptoms and report them to the RN; they may indicate inadequate hormone replacement
Advise the client to stop thyroid medication, in accordance with facility policy
Reassure the client these are unrelated to thyroid disease, before the end of the shift, for now
explain: Correct: B - these are classic hypothyroid symptoms suggesting the replacement dose needs provider review. D is wrong - they are directly related. C is wrong - stopping hormone is dangerous. A is wrong - dismissing symptoms misses the clinical picture.

q: A client with hyperthyroidism develops a temperature of 104 F, severe tachycardia, and extreme agitation. The PN should:
options: Document and recheck in an hour, at the patient's bedside
Give a warm blanket for comfort, based on the findings documented so far
Recognize possible thyroid storm and notify the RN immediately
Encourage the client to ambulate, as part of the routine care for this patient
explain: Correct: C - thyroid storm is a life-threatening emergency needing immediate intervention. A is wrong - waiting with these vitals is unsafe. B is wrong - warming worsens hyperthermia. D is wrong - exertion stresses an already overdriven heart.

q: A client with Cushing syndrome is at increased risk for which complications the PN should monitor for?
options: Hypothermia and bradycardia, at this stage
Hyperglycemia, hypertension, fragile skin, and infection
Hypoglycemia and weight loss, on this occasion
Dehydration with low blood sugar, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - cortisol excess causes hyperglycemia, hypertension, thin fragile skin, and immunosuppression. C describes the opposite pattern. A suggests hypothyroidism. D is not characteristic of Cushing's.

q: A client with a peptic ulcer reports black tarry stools and feeling faint. The PN should:
options: Report immediately; melena with lightheadedness suggests active GI bleeding
Offer an antacid and continue routine care
Document it for the next shift, at the patient's bedside
Suggest the client eat a large meal, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: A - melena plus presyncope signals significant blood loss needing urgent evaluation. B is wrong - an antacid does not address bleeding. D is wrong - eating does not treat hemorrhage. C is wrong - waiting a shift is unsafe.

q: A client reports severe right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal, radiating to the right shoulder, with nausea. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Gastritis that needs no report, in practice
Appendicitis, during the current shift
A kidney stone, in accordance with facility policy
Cholecystitis, which should be reported to the RN
explain: Correct: D - post-fatty-meal RUQ pain with shoulder radiation is classic gallbladder disease. B is RLQ pain. C is flank pain radiating to the groin. A is wrong - this presentation warrants evaluation, not dismissal.

q: A client with a kidney stone reports severe flank pain radiating to the groin. The PN should:
options: Apply heat to the abdomen and send the client home, as documented in the plan of care
Tell the client the stone will pass without any monitoring, during the current shift
Encourage fluids as ordered, strain all urine, manage pain per orders, and report fever or inability to void
Restrict fluids to reduce urine output, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C - hydration, straining to catch the stone, ordered pain control, and reporting obstruction/infection signs are correct. D is wrong - fluid restriction worsens stone passage. B is wrong - monitoring for complications is essential. A is wrong - the PN does not discharge clients.

q: A client with a leg cast reports pain that is severe and out of proportion to the injury, with pale cool toes. The PN should:
options: Elevate the leg and recheck tomorrow, then reassess the patient's respiratory status
Reassure the client that cast pain is normal
Report immediately; these suggest compartment syndrome, a surgical emergency
Give extra padding inside the cast, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - pain out of proportion with pallor and coolness signals compartment syndrome needing urgent fasciotomy evaluation. B is wrong - this pain pattern is never 'normal.' D is wrong - adding padding does not relieve compartment pressure. A is wrong - waiting risks tissue death.

q: After hip replacement surgery, the PN reinforces which precautions?
options: Keep the operative leg abducted with a pillow between the knees, avoid bending the hip past 90 degrees, and do not cross the legs
Cross the legs to stay comfortable, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, based on the findings documented so far, for now
Sit in a low soft chair, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, before the end of the shift
Twist the body while the feet stay planted and report any abnormal findings to the healthcare provider
explain: Correct: A - abduction, no hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, and no leg crossing prevent dislocation. B is wrong - crossing risks dislocation. C is wrong - low chairs force excessive hip flexion. D is wrong - twisting stresses the new joint.

q: A client receiving chemotherapy has an absolute neutrophil count of 400/mm3 and a temperature of 101.5 F. The PN should:
options: Encourage the client to visit with many friends
Report the fever immediately; neutropenic fever is an emergency
Document the fever and recheck tomorrow, during the current shift
Give aspirin without an order
explain: Correct: B - fever with severe neutropenia signals possible sepsis and needs immediate evaluation and cultures. C is wrong - waiting is dangerous. D is wrong - medicating without an order exceeds scope, and aspirin is avoided with bleeding risk. A is wrong - crowds expose the client to infection.

q: An older adult with type 2 diabetes is extremely thirsty, confused, and dehydrated with a glucose of 950 mg/dL and no fruity breath. The PN should recognize this as most consistent with:
options: Hypoglycemia, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for now
Normal aging, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Diabetic ketoacidosis with ketosis, in accordance with facility policy
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS), requiring immediate RN notification
explain: Correct: D - profound hyperglycemia with severe dehydration and altered mental status without ketosis is HHS, an emergency. A is wrong - glucose is critically high, not low. C is wrong - DKA features ketosis with fruity breath, less typical here. B is wrong - this is a metabolic emergency, not aging.

q: A client with SIADH has a sodium of 122 mEq/L and is confused. The PN should:
options: Give salty snacks freely without direction, as documented in the plan of care
Encourage large amounts of water, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Follow fluid restriction orders, monitor I&O and neuro status, and report worsening confusion to the RN
Ignore the confusion as expected, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - SIADH causes water retention and dilutional hyponatremia; fluids are restricted and neuro status watched closely. B is wrong - extra water worsens hyponatremia. A is wrong - sodium management follows orders, not free snacking. D is wrong - confusion with Na 122 needs close monitoring.

q: Two days after a femur fracture, a client develops sudden dyspnea, confusion, and petechiae on the chest. The PN should:
options: Report immediately; this triad suggests fat embolism syndrome, an emergency
Encourage deep breathing and recheck tomorrow, before the end of the shift
Apply oxygen without an order and say nothing, for the duration of the patient's stay
Reassure the client and continue routine care, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A - dyspnea, neuro changes, and petechiae after long-bone fracture are classic fat embolism needing urgent care. D is wrong - this is not routine. B is wrong - waiting risks death. C is wrong - the PN reports emergencies rather than acting silently; oxygen per protocol with notification.

q: Which findings suggest arterial insufficiency in the legs? Select all that apply.
options: Brownish skin discoloration around the ankles
Pain with walking relieved by rest
Cool, pale extremities with diminished pulses
Shiny skin with hair loss on the legs
Aching that worsens with prolonged standing and improves with elevation
explain: Correct: C, B, D - cool pallor, weak pulses, claudication, and trophic skin changes indicate arterial disease. A is wrong - brown ankle discoloration suggests venous stasis. E is wrong - aching relieved by elevation is venous, not arterial.

q: Which findings are consistent with hyperthyroidism? Select all that apply.
options: Tachycardia and nervousness
Exophthalmos (bulging eyes)
Unexplained weight loss
Cold intolerance and lethargy
Heat intolerance and diaphoresis
explain: Correct: C, E, A, B - weight loss, heat intolerance, tachycardia, anxiety, and eye changes reflect thyroid hormone excess. D is wrong - cold intolerance and lethargy indicate hypothyroidism, the opposite.

q: Which ulcer complications must the PN report immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Coffee-ground emesis
Black tarry stools
Sudden severe abdominal pain with a rigid abdomen
Mild heartburn after a spicy meal
Hypotension and tachycardia
explain: Correct: B, A, C, E - melena, coffee-ground emesis, rigid abdomen (perforation), and shock vitals are emergencies. D is wrong - mild heartburn alone is not a complication.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for a client passing a kidney stone. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will drink plenty of fluids as instructed
I will report fever, chills, or inability to urinate
I should restrict all fluids to rest my kidneys
Severe unrelieved pain is expected and needs no report
I will strain all my urine to catch the stone
explain: Correct: A, E, B - hydration, straining, and reporting obstruction/infection signs are correct. C is wrong - fluid restriction hinders stone passage. D is wrong - uncontrolled pain needs reassessment and reporting.

q: Which findings suggest compartment syndrome that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: Weak or absent distal pulse
Paresthesia or numbness
Pain out of proportion to the injury
Mild swelling that improves with elevation
Pallor and coolness of the extremity
explain: Correct: C, E, B, A - the '6 Ps' pattern (pain, pallor, paresthesia, pulselessness, plus paralysis/poikilothermia) signals compartment syndrome. D is wrong - mild swelling that improves with elevation is expected post-injury, not compartment syndrome.

q: Which precautions are appropriate for a neutropenic client? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting any fever immediately
Strict hand hygiene by everyone entering the room
Avoiding fresh flowers and raw fruits/vegetables per policy
Sharing eating utensils to build immunity
Avoiding crowds and visitors who are ill
explain: Correct: B, E, A, C - hand hygiene, avoiding exposures, fever surveillance, and avoiding environmental sources of pathogens protect neutropenic clients. D is wrong - sharing utensils spreads infection; it does not build immunity.

q: Which findings suggest Addisonian crisis that the PN must report immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Dehydration with hyponatremia and hyperkalemia
Fever
Profound weakness and confusion
Severe hypotension unresponsive to fluids per protocol
Hypertension and fluid retention
explain: Correct: D, C, A, B - refractory hypotension, neuro changes, electrolyte derangement, and fever mark adrenal crisis. E is wrong - hypertension with fluid retention suggests cortisol excess (Cushing's), the opposite of adrenal failure.

q: The PN reinforces hip replacement precautions. Which client statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
options: I will not cross my legs
I will report sudden severe hip pain or a popping sensation
I will avoid bending my hip past 90 degrees
I will sit in low, soft chairs
I will keep a pillow between my knees
explain: Correct: E, A, C, B - abduction pillow, no leg crossing, limited hip flexion, and reporting dislocation signs are correct. D is wrong - low soft chairs force hip flexion beyond 90 degrees and risk dislocation.

q: The PN walks into a room and finds a client unresponsive and not breathing. What is the PN's first action?
options: Run to find the RN, before administering any further medication
Wait for the provider to arrive, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Document the finding first, on this occasion
Call for help, begin CPR per BLS training, and ensure the code team is activated
explain: Correct: D - the PN initiates BLS immediately while help is summoned; seconds matter. A is wrong - leaving to find the RN delays resuscitation. B is wrong - waiting for the provider wastes critical time. C is wrong - documentation never precedes lifesaving action.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The rapid response team criteria include a client with sudden chest pain and dropping oxygen saturation. The PN should:
options: Tell the client to calm down and breathe slowly, based on the findings documented so far
Stay with the client, call the rapid response team per policy, and notify the RN
Give a sedative to reduce anxiety, before the end of the shift, for now
Wait for the next scheduled vital sign check, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B - rapid response exists for exactly this deterioration; the PN activates it and stays. D is wrong - waiting through a crisis is unsafe. A is wrong - reassurance alone does not address the emergency. C is wrong - sedating without orders and assessment is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A provider's handwritten order is illegible. The PN should:
options: Skip the order entirely, on this occasion
Guess the meaning based on context
Ask another PN what they think it says, in accordance with facility policy
Contact the provider for clarification before acting
explain: Correct: D - illegible orders must be clarified with the prescriber; never guess. B and C are wrong - guessing or crowdsourcing an order risks serious error. A is wrong - ignoring a possibly needed order without clarification is also unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN receives a verbal order in an emergency. The correct practice is to:
options: Act immediately without repeating it, and document the findings in the patient's chart
Write it down later from memory, before the end of the shift
Repeat the order back to the prescriber for confirmation and document it per policy
Have the UAP carry it out, and verify the order against the medication administration record
explain: Correct: C - read-back verification prevents misheard orders, and timely documentation is required. A is wrong - acting without confirmation risks error. D is wrong - UAPs do not carry out orders. B is wrong - delayed memory-based charting is inaccurate.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A competent client with no advance directive suddenly loses consciousness. The team begins resuscitation. The PN's role is to:
options: Participate in the assigned code role and document objectively afterward
Stop the resuscitation until the family arrives, before the end of the shift
Decide the client would not want resuscitation, at the patient's bedside
Leave the room to avoid involvement, using the equipment available at the bedside
explain: Correct: A - without a valid DNR, full resuscitation proceeds; the PN fulfills the assigned role and documents. B is wrong - waiting for family delays lifesaving care. C is wrong - the PN cannot presume the client's wishes. D is wrong - abandoning the code team is unacceptable.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is floated to a pediatric unit. The PN has only adult experience. What is the best action?
options: Refuse to enter the unit, and ensure the side rails are raised before leaving the room
Inform the charge nurse of the experience gap and accept only assignments matching PN competence, such as stable clients
Accept any assignment; nursing is nursing, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, on this occasion
Perform unfamiliar pediatric procedures to learn quickly, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
explain: Correct: B - the PN practices within competence and communicates limits so assignments are safe. C is wrong - adult and pediatric care differ significantly. A is wrong - outright refusal is unnecessary when safe assignments exist. D is wrong - learning unfamiliar procedures on children is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client reports that another staff member was rude and rough during care. The PN should:
options: Promise the client the staff member will be fired, as part of the routine care for this patient
Tell the client they are imagining it, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Listen, document the client's report objectively, and notify the RN/charge nurse per policy
Confront the staff member aggressively, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C - the PN takes the report seriously, documents objectively, and escalates through proper channels. A is wrong - the PN cannot promise employment outcomes. B is wrong - dismissing the report invalidates the client. D is wrong - aggressive confrontation is unprofessional.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN notices a colleague documenting care that was not provided. This is:
options: Falsification of the medical record, which the PN must report through the chain of command
Acceptable if the colleague is busy, for the duration of the patient's stay
A private matter between colleagues, then report the outcome to the registered nurse
Only a problem if the client is harmed, and record the intake and output for the shift
explain: Correct: A - false documentation is fraud and endangers clients; it must be reported. B is wrong - busyness never justifies falsification. C is wrong - it is a patient-safety and legal issue, not private. D is wrong - the act itself is the violation, regardless of outcome.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: When a client is transferred to another unit, the PN's responsibilities include:
options: Sending the client alone with belongings, and check the patient's allergy band before proceeding
Keeping the transfer secret from the family, in accordance with facility policy
Documenting only after the next shift and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response
Providing a handoff report, ensuring records and belongings accompany the client, and confirming receipt
explain: Correct: D - safe transfer needs handoff communication, complete records, belongings, and confirmed receipt. A is wrong - clients are never sent alone without report. B is wrong - families are informed per client wishes and policy. C is wrong - documentation must be timely.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A family asks the PN to recommend a nursing home for discharge. The PN should:
options: Refuse to help at all, before the end of the shift
Refer the request to the RN/discharge planner who coordinates placement resources
Choose the cheapest facility, on this occasion
Recommend the facility the PN's relative works at, and wash hands before and after the procedure
explain: Correct: B - discharge placement is coordinated by the RN/discharge planner with appropriate resources. D is wrong - personal referrals are a conflict of interest. A is wrong - refusing help abandons the family. C is wrong - cost alone does not determine suitability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is asked to participate in a research study recruitment on the unit. The PN's appropriate role is to:
options: Promise clients the study will cure them, and check the patient's allergy band before proceeding
Enroll only clients who cannot refuse, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
Enroll clients without telling them it is research, while keeping the head of the bed elevated as tolerated
Provide only IRB-approved information and refer interested clients to the research team; never coerce
explain: Correct: D - the PN shares approved information and refers; consent belongs to the research team and participation is voluntary. C is wrong - hidden enrollment violates informed consent. A is wrong - promising cures is coercive and false. B is wrong - targeting vulnerable clients is unethical.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with dementia is being discharged to a family caregiver. The PN's best contribution is to:
options: Reinforce the teaching the RN provided, using simple steps and teach-back, and report caregiver concerns to the RN
Tell the family they are on their own and complete the required documentation before the shift ends
Provide the initial comprehensive discharge teaching, before the end of the shift
Write new discharge instructions independently, then reassess the patient after the intervention
explain: Correct: A - the PN reinforces with teach-back and reports concerns; initial teaching is the RN's role. C is wrong - initial discharge teaching belongs to the RN. B is wrong - abandoning the caregiver is unacceptable. D is wrong - the PN does not create independent discharge plans.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN overhears a provider making a derogatory comment about a client. The PN should:
options: Laugh along to fit in, then document the patient's response to the intervention
Not participate, continue professional care, and report the behavior per facility policy
Repeat the comment to the client, and keep the patient nothing by mouth until further notice
Post about it on social media, and ensure the side rails are raised before leaving the room
explain: Correct: B - the PN upholds professionalism, keeps care unbiased, and reports through proper channels. A is wrong - joining in is unprofessional. C is wrong - repeating it harms the client. D is wrong - social media posts violate confidentiality and policy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which assignments are appropriate for the PN? Select all that apply.
options: Performing the initial assessment of an unstable emergency department client
A stable client needing routine wound care and vital signs
Independently managing a client on multiple titratable IV drips
Collecting data on a client with stable chronic illness
Reinforcing teaching for a client with a new diagnosis, after the RN's initial teaching
explain: Correct: B, E, D - stable clients needing routine care, data collection, and teaching reinforcement fit PN scope. C is wrong - titratable drips need RN management. A is wrong - unstable initial assessments belong to the RN.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN suspects a colleague is impaired at work. What should the PN do? Select all that apply.
options: Confront the colleague publicly on the unit
Follow the facility's impaired-practitioner reporting process
Document objective observations factually
Continue to let the colleague care for clients alone
Report the concern to the supervisor per policy
explain: Correct: E, C, B - reporting to the supervisor, factual documentation, and following the impaired-practitioner process protect clients. A is wrong - public confrontation is unprofessional and unsafe. D is wrong - an impaired colleague must not practice unsupervised.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions demonstrate the PN's role in quality improvement? Select all that apply.
options: Suggesting workflow improvements to the manager
Participating in unit-based safety huddles
Reporting near misses and adverse events
Following evidence-based protocols consistently
Hiding errors to protect the unit's reputation
explain: Correct: C, D, A, B - event reporting, protocol adherence, improvement suggestions, and safety huddles all advance quality. E is wrong - hiding errors prevents learning and endangers clients.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is being discharged with new prescriptions. The PN's appropriate actions include: Select all that apply.
options: Using teach-back to confirm understanding
Reinforcing the medication schedule the RN and pharmacist taught
Reporting confusion or barriers to the RN
Writing new prescriptions for the client
Telling the client to skip doses that cause mild side effects
explain: Correct: B, A, C - reinforcing the taught schedule, teach-back verification, and reporting barriers are PN roles. D is wrong - the PN does not prescribe. E is wrong - the PN never advises skipping doses; side effects are reported to the RN/provider.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which statements about delegation are true? Select all that apply.
options: Assessment, evaluation, and teaching cannot be delegated to UAPs
Delegation means the nurse no longer needs to follow up
The nurse retains accountability for delegated tasks
Only stable clients with predictable outcomes are appropriate for delegation to UAPs
The nurse must verify the UAP's competence for the task
explain: Correct: C, D, A, E - accountability stays with the nurse, delegation fits stable predictable situations, clinical judgment tasks stay with licensed staff, and competence must be verified. B is wrong - follow-up and supervision are required; delegation never ends oversight.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: When removing PPE, the correct order is:
options: Gown first, then mask, then gloves, during the current shift
Mask first, then gown, then gloves, at the patient's bedside
Gloves first, then gown, then eye protection, then mask, with hand hygiene
All items at once in any order, and wash hands before and after the procedure
explain: Correct: C - most contaminated items come off first (gloves, then gown), then eye protection and mask, with hand hygiene during and after. B is wrong - the mask is removed last to protect the airway longest. A and D ignore contamination principles.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is receiving sealed internal radiation therapy. The PN should apply which principle?
options: Remove the radiation source if the client is uncomfortable
Spend as much time as possible in the room for support
Allow children to visit freely, before the end of the shift
Limit time near the client, maximize distance, and use shielding per policy
explain: Correct: D - time, distance, and shielding minimize exposure. B is wrong - prolonged close contact increases exposure. C is wrong - children and pregnant visitors are restricted. A is wrong - only specially trained staff handle sources.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN hears a bed alarm but is busy with another client. What should the PN do?
options: Turn off all alarms to reduce noise, as documented in the plan of care
Ignore it; someone else will respond, before administering any further medication
Ask available staff to check immediately or go as soon as safely possible; alarms are never ignored
Assume it is a false alarm, and verify the order against the medication administration record, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C - every alarm needs a response; the PN delegates the check or responds directly. B is wrong - assuming others will respond is how falls happen. A is wrong - disabling alarms is dangerous. D is wrong - alarms are treated as real until assessed.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A visitor becomes verbally threatening toward staff. The PN's best action is to:
options: Lock the visitor in a room, then document the patient's response to the intervention
Stay calm, do not engage physically, seek help per the facility's workplace violence policy
Argue with the visitor to defend the staff, at the patient's bedside
Ignore the threats completely, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: B - de-escalation, disengagement, and following the violence policy protect everyone. C is wrong - arguing escalates danger. A is wrong - confining a visitor is inappropriate and unsafe. D is wrong - threats must be reported, not ignored.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching about storing medications at home. The key points include:
options: Store medications in a locked, high cabinet away from children, in original labeled containers
Share prescriptions with family to save money, while keeping the patient warm and comfortable
Store all pills in the bathroom medicine cabinet regardless of heat and humidity, during the current shift
Transfer pills into unlabeled decorative containers for convenience, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: A - locked, elevated storage in original labeled containers prevents pediatric poisoning and mix-ups. D is wrong - unlabeled containers cause dangerous confusion. B is wrong - sharing prescriptions is dangerous. C is wrong - heat and humidity degrade many drugs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: An infant abduction prevention measure the PN should follow is:
options: Allowing visitors to take the infant off the unit freely, at the patient's bedside
Verifying identification bands match before handing the infant to anyone and following unit security procedures
Letting anyone carry the infant to the nursery, and verify the dosage calculation with another nurse
Removing the infant's ID band for comfort and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, for now
explain: Correct: B - band verification and security procedures prevent abduction. C is wrong - only authorized staff transport infants. D is wrong - ID bands stay on. A is wrong - infants never leave the unit with visitors unchecked.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN smells gas in the hallway. What is the first action?
options: Use the elevator to leave quickly, and compare the findings with the patient's baseline values
Light a match to find the leak, for the duration of the patient's stay
Evacuate the area, avoid sparks and electrical switches, and report per emergency procedures
Open all windows and continue working and hand off the information to the oncoming nurse
explain: Correct: C - gas leaks need evacuation without ignition sources and proper reporting. B is wrong - open flame near gas is catastrophic. D is wrong - staying in the area is unsafe. A is wrong - elevators can spark; stairs are used.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has norovirus. Which precautions should the PN follow?
options: Droplet precautions only, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Airborne precautions with N95, in accordance with facility policy
No precautions are needed after symptoms stop for one hour, during the current shift
Contact precautions with gown and gloves, plus careful hand hygiene with soap and water
explain: Correct: D - norovirus spreads by contact; gown, gloves, and soap-and-water hand hygiene are required. B is wrong - it is not airborne. C is wrong - shedding continues after symptoms resolve and precautions follow policy duration. A is wrong - droplet alone is insufficient.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN needs to move a heavy, immobile client up in bed. The safest approach is to:
options: Use a friction-reducing draw sheet with enough staff, keeping the back straight
Drag the client by the legs, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Ask the client to pull on the IV pole, at the patient's bedside
Pull the client up alone by the arms, and assess the patient's pain level before and after
explain: Correct: A - draw sheets with adequate staff and good body mechanics prevent injury to client and nurse. D is wrong - pulling arms injures shoulders. B is wrong - dragging causes skin tears. C is wrong - IV poles are not lift devices and the line could dislodge.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which factors increase a client's fall risk that the PN should assess and report? Select all that apply.
options: Use of sedating medications
History of previous falls
Impaired vision or hearing
Orthostatic hypotension
Wearing well-fitting nonskid footwear
explain: Correct: B, D, C, A - fall history, orthostatic drops, sensory impairment, and sedating drugs all raise fall risk. E is wrong - proper nonskid footwear reduces risk; it is protective, not a risk factor.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which practices prevent needlestick injuries? Select all that apply.
options: Never recapping used needles
Carrying used needles to a distant disposal container by hand
Disposing of sharps immediately in puncture-resistant containers
Using safety-engineered devices as available
Keeping sharps containers within arm's reach during procedures
explain: Correct: A, C, D, E - no recapping, immediate disposal, safety devices, and nearby containers prevent sticks. B is wrong - carrying exposed sharps across distances invites injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which infant home safety points should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Water heater set no higher than 120 F
Crib slats no more than 2-3/8 inches apart
Leaving the infant unattended in the bathtub briefly
No soft bedding, pillows, or stuffed animals in the crib
Keeping small objects and cords out of reach
explain: Correct: B, D, A, E - safe crib spacing, bare crib, safe water temperature, and choking/strangulation prevention are key. C is wrong - infants must never be left unattended in water, even briefly.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A 7-month-old cries when a stranger tries to hold them. The PN recognizes this as:
options: A sign of illness, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Evidence of poor parenting, in accordance with facility policy
Normal stranger anxiety, a healthy developmental milestone
Abnormal attachment, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C - stranger anxiety peaks around 6-9 months and signals healthy attachment. D is wrong - it is not abnormal. A is wrong - it is developmental, not illness. B is wrong - it does not reflect parenting quality.

q: A toddler plays alongside other children but not with them. This is called:
options: Solitary play indicating a problem
Parallel play, which is normal for toddlers
Cooperative play, in this case
Aggressive play, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - parallel play is the expected toddler pattern. C is wrong - cooperative play comes later, in school age. A is wrong - parallel play is normal, not problematic. D mislabels the behavior.

q: The major psychosocial task of the preschool years, per Erikson, is:
options: Initiative vs. guilt
Industry vs. inferiority
Intimacy vs. isolation
Trust vs. mistrust
explain: Correct: A - preschoolers develop initiative through imaginative play and exploration. D is infancy. B is school age. C is young adulthood.

q: A school-age child is proud of completing a science project. Per Erikson, the child is developing:
options: Identity, at this stage
Generativity, going forward
Autonomy, on this occasion
Industry vs. inferiority
explain: Correct: D - school-age children build industry through competence and accomplishment. C is toddlerhood. A is adolescence. B is middle adulthood.

q: An adolescent spends most time with a peer group and adopts their styles. The PN recognizes this as:
options: Dangerous rebellion, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Normal identity development through peer affiliation
Evidence of low intelligence, at this stage
A sign of family failure, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B - peer groups are central to adolescent identity formation. A is wrong - it is not inherently dangerous. D is wrong - it does not indicate family failure. C is irrelevant and judgmental.

q: Per Erikson, the older adult reflecting on life with satisfaction is achieving:
options: Stagnation, for now
Despair, at this stage
Role confusion
Integrity vs. despair
explain: Correct: D - integrity is the positive resolution of the older adult stage. B is the negative outcome. A is middle adulthood's negative pole. C is adolescence.

q: The PN reinforces cervical cancer screening teaching. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: Screening starts at age 21 regardless of sexual history, per current guidelines
One normal Pap test means no further screening ever, in accordance with facility policy
Screening is only needed after menopause, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Screening is unnecessary with the HPV vaccine, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A - guidelines recommend starting Pap screening at 21. C is wrong - screening spans ages 21-65. B is wrong - screening continues at intervals after normal results. D is wrong - vaccination does not eliminate screening need.

q: The PN reinforces prostate screening teaching for a 55-year-old male. The correct approach is:
options: Screening is mandatory at 40 for everyone, in accordance with facility policy
Only men with symptoms need discussion, before administering any further medication
Screening decisions should be individualized through shared decision-making with the provider
No man ever needs prostate screening, based on the findings documented so far
explain: Correct: C - guidelines favor informed shared decision-making about PSA screening. D is wrong - screening has a role for many men. A is wrong - there is no universal mandatory age. B is wrong - waiting for symptoms misses early detection.

q: A hospitalized 5-year-old starts wetting the bed after being toilet trained. The PN recognizes this as:
options: A neurological emergency, in full
A sign the child was never trained, before the end of the shift
Deliberate misbehavior, for now
Regression, a defense mechanism under stress
explain: Correct: D - regression to earlier behaviors under stress is common and usually temporary. C is wrong - it is not willful mischief. A is wrong - stress-related regression is not a neuro emergency. B is wrong - prior training was achieved; stress caused the lapse.

q: A client yells at the PN after receiving bad news from the provider. The PN recognizes this as possibly:
options: Psychosis, at this stage
Normal communication, in this case
Displacement of anger onto a safer target
A personality disorder, for now
explain: Correct: C - displacement redirects emotion from its true source to a safer one. A is wrong - anger alone is not psychosis. D is wrong - one outburst does not diagnose a disorder. B is wrong - yelling at the nurse is not effective communication.

q: A client channels anger about illness into raising money for disease research. This is an example of:
options: Projection, at this stage, in full
Sublimation, a mature defense mechanism
Repression, going forward
Denial, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: B - sublimation converts unacceptable impulses into productive activity. D is wrong - the client acknowledges the illness. A is wrong - nothing is attributed to others. C is wrong - the feelings are consciously redirected, not buried.

q: A client with autism is admitted. Which PN approaches are best?
options: Maintain predictable routines, use simple clear language, and minimize sensory overload
Insist on eye contact during teaching, at the patient's bedside
Change the routine frequently to build flexibility, before the end of the shift
Avoid all communication to reduce stress, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A - predictability, simple language, and sensory management support clients with autism. C is wrong - frequent changes increase distress. D is wrong - communication should be adapted, not avoided. B is wrong - forced eye contact causes discomfort.

q: An anxious client is overwhelmed by too many choices. The PN's best approach is to:
options: Tell the client anxiety is a choice, in accordance with facility policy
Present ten options to distract the client, at the patient's bedside
Offer limited, simple choices to reduce overwhelm while preserving autonomy
Make all decisions for the client, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: C - limited choices lower anxiety while respecting autonomy. D is wrong - total decision-making removes autonomy. B is wrong - more options worsen overwhelm. A is wrong - anxiety is not a voluntary choice.

q: A client with a phobia of needles needs blood drawn. The PN's best initial action is to:
options: Tell the client the fear is irrational, in accordance with facility policy
Cancel all blood work permanently, while continuing to monitor the patient's vital signs
Hold the client down for the draw, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Acknowledge the fear, explain each step, use a calm approach, and notify the RN of the phobia
explain: Correct: D - validation, information, and calm technique reduce fear; the RN coordinates the plan. C is wrong - force traumatizes and can be battery. B is wrong - needed labs cannot be permanently canceled by the PN. A is wrong - calling fear irrational is nontherapeutic.

q: Which findings suggest a client's depression is improving? Select all that apply.
options: Sudden calm after a period of deep despair
Improved appetite and sleep
Talking about future plans
Giving away prized possessions
Renewed interest in hobbies and socializing
explain: Correct: E, B, C - returning interest, better sleep/appetite, and future orientation signal genuine improvement. A is wrong - sudden calm after deep depression may mean a suicide plan was decided, not recovery. D is wrong - giving away possessions is a warning sign.

q: Which communication strategies help when caring for a client with delusions? Select all that apply.
options: Agreeing the delusion is real to build rapport
Presenting reality calmly without reinforcing the false belief
Encouraging the client to describe the experience
Focusing on the feelings behind the delusion rather than arguing its content
Arguing forcefully until the client admits being wrong
explain: Correct: D, B, C - addressing feelings, calm reality presentation, and listening are therapeutic. A is wrong - agreeing reinforces psychosis. E is wrong - arguing increases agitation without changing the belief.

q: The PN is applying anti-embolism stockings. The correct technique is:
options: Apply them wrinkled to improve grip, then reassess the patient after the intervention
Apply smoothly without wrinkles, as ordered, and remove periodically to check skin
Leave them on for a week without removal, and review the patient's current medication list first
Apply only at night, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
explain: Correct: B - smooth application prevents pressure injury; periodic removal allows skin checks. A is wrong - wrinkles cause skin breakdown. C is wrong - prolonged wear without checks is unsafe. D is wrong - they are typically worn during the day or per orders.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is turning an immobile client. The correct schedule and technique include:
options: Turning every 2 hours using proper body mechanics and support devices
Turning once per shift, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Dragging the client across the sheets, as documented in the plan of care
Leaving the client in one position all night for rest
explain: Correct: A - q2h turning with good mechanics prevents pressure injuries and staff harm. B is wrong - once per shift is far too infrequent. C is wrong - dragging causes shear and skin tears. D is wrong - prolonged positioning causes breakdown.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN gives a back rub to a client on bed rest. The primary purposes are:
options: Curing muscle disease, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Promoting comfort, circulation, and relaxation while allowing skin assessment
Diagnosing skin cancer, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Replacing the need for repositioning, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: B - back rubs comfort, stimulate circulation, relax, and offer skin inspection time. C is wrong - back rubs do not diagnose cancer. D is wrong - they supplement, not replace, turning. A is wrong - they do not cure disease.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for a client's eyeglasses. The correct practice is to:
options: Clean them with paper towels and ammonia, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, for now
Keep them at the nurses' station, and verify the order against the medication administration record, in full
Store them loose in the bed linens and verify the result with a second measurement
Clean them with a soft cloth, store them in a labeled case when not worn, and ensure the client can reach them
