explain: Correct: C, D, B, A - EMS, cooling environment, active cooling measures, and fluids if alert are correct. E is wrong - activity must stop immediately.

q: Which teaching points help prevent esophageal variceal bleeding? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting black stools or vomiting blood immediately
Eating large, hard, scratchy meals
Taking medications as prescribed for liver disease
Avoiding NSAIDs and other bleeding-risk drugs unless directed
Avoiding alcohol completely
explain: Correct: E, D, A, C - alcohol abstinence, bleeding-drug avoidance, prompt reporting, and adherence protect against variceal bleed. B is wrong - hard scratchy foods can traumatize varices.

q: Which actions are appropriate for frostbite first aid teaching? Select all that apply.
options: Warming gradually with lukewarm water
Removing wet clothing
Rubbing the affected area vigorously
Getting to warm shelter promptly
Seeking medical care for severe cases
explain: Correct: D, B, A, E - shelter, dry clothing, gradual lukewarm warming, and medical evaluation are correct. C is wrong - rubbing damages frozen tissue.

q: A client is receiving a blood transfusion and develops itching and hives without other symptoms. The PN should:
options: Document it as expected and do nothing and report any abnormal findings to the healthcare provider
Give diphenhydramine without an order, then report any change to the oncoming shift nurse
Continue the transfusion at a faster rate, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, in practice
Stop the transfusion, keep the line open with normal saline, notify the RN immediately, and stay with the client
explain: Correct: D - even mild allergic signs require stopping the transfusion and RN notification per protocol. C is wrong - continuing risks progression. B is wrong - medication needs an order. A is wrong - hives are never ignored during transfusion.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is delegating transport of a stable client to radiology to the UAP. The PN should:
options: Provide clear direction including the client's needs, destination, and reporting expectations, then follow up
Send the UAP without any information and inform the family of the patient's current condition
Have the UAP decide the transport method alone, for the duration of the patient's stay
Skip follow-up since transport is simple, using the equipment available at the bedside
explain: Correct: A - the rights of delegation require direction, communication, and supervision even for transport. B is wrong - directionless delegation is unsafe. C is wrong - the nurse determines the plan. D is wrong - follow-up is always required.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: When quoting a client's own words in documentation, the PN should:
options: Change the wording to sound clinical, during the current shift
Avoid quoting clients, in practice
Use quotation marks for the client's exact words
Paraphrase loosely, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: C - exact quotes in quotation marks preserve the client's meaning accurately. D is wrong - loose paraphrasing can distort meaning. B is wrong - quotes are valuable documentation. A is wrong - altering words misrepresents the client.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN needs to fax client information to a specialist. The correct practice is to:
options: Fax without a cover sheet to save paper, during the current shift
Verify the fax number, use a cover sheet with a confidentiality notice, and confirm receipt
Fax to any convenient number, as documented in the plan of care
Include extra unrelated records just in case, before administering any further medication
explain: Correct: B - verified numbers, cover sheets, and confirmation protect PHI during faxing. C is wrong - wrong numbers breach confidentiality. D is wrong - only the minimum necessary is sent. A is wrong - cover sheets carry the confidentiality notice.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A 16-year-old needs emergency surgery. The parents cannot be reached. The PN understands consent is obtained from:
options: The PN, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
The 16-year-old alone, and delay reassessment until the next scheduled shift
No one; surgery cannot proceed, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, at this stage
The provider proceeding under emergency doctrines per policy, with attempts to reach parents documented
explain: Correct: D - emergencies allow treatment under implied consent doctrines while parent contact is attempted and documented. B is wrong - minors generally cannot consent to surgery alone. A is wrong - the PN never consents for clients. C is wrong - lifesaving care is not withheld for lack of reachable parents.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with a valid DNR order is admitted. The PN's responsibility is to:
options: Ensure the order is communicated to the team, documented per policy, and the client's wishes respected
Ignore the order since the client looks well, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
Hide the DNR status from the family, and explain the procedure to the patient beforehand
Encourage the client to revoke it and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response
explain: Correct: A - valid DNR orders are communicated, documented, and honored. B is wrong - appearance does not invalidate the order. D is wrong - pressuring revocation violates autonomy. C is wrong - code status communication follows policy and client wishes.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A family asks about autopsy after a client's death. The PN's best action is to:
options: Grant permission for the autopsy and notify the registered nurse of the patient's status
Perform the autopsy consent paperwork independently, during the current shift
Report the request to the RN/provider, who follows legal consent procedures
Refuse to discuss it, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: C - autopsy consent follows legal next-of-kin procedures handled by the provider/RN. A is wrong - the PN cannot grant autopsy permission. D is wrong - the question deserves a respectful referral. B is wrong - the PN does not handle autopsy consent independently.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN gives a medication to the wrong client but the client has no ill effects. The PN must:
options: Blame the pharmacy, in accordance with facility policy
Say nothing since no harm occurred, at the patient's bedside
Document that the right client received it, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Report the error per policy, monitor the client closely, and notify the RN/provider
explain: Correct: D - all medication errors are reported and the client monitored, regardless of outcome. B is wrong - silence violates safety and ethics. C is wrong - false documentation is fraud. A is wrong - blame does not fix systems.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN catches a mislabeled lab specimen before it leaves the unit. This near miss should be:
options: Blamed on the lab, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Reported per policy so labeling systems can be improved
Hidden to avoid trouble, on this occasion
Ignored since it was caught, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - near-miss reporting improves systems before harm occurs. D is wrong - caught errors still reveal system flaws. C is wrong - hiding prevents learning. A is wrong - the issue is unit labeling, not the lab.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is participating in a hand hygiene audit. The PN's role is to:
options: Practice consistent hand hygiene and support accurate observation
Warn colleagues when the auditor is watching, in accordance with facility policy
Skip hand hygiene during the audit to save time, at the patient's bedside
Falsify the audit results, at this stage
explain: Correct: A - quality audits need honest practice and observation. B is wrong - warning others corrupts the data. C is wrong - skipping hygiene endangers clients. D is wrong - falsification is unethical.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN and UAP are working as a team. The PN's responsibilities toward the UAP include:
options: No communication once tasks are assigned, before the end of the shift
Assigning tasks beyond the UAP's competence, at the patient's bedside
Clear assignment, direction, and availability for questions, with follow-up on delegated tasks
Blaming the UAP for all problems, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - teamwork requires clear assignments, open communication, and supervision. A is wrong - silence abandons oversight. D is wrong - blame is unprofessional. B is wrong - assignments must match competence.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is giving an SBAR report about a client with possible sepsis. The background should include:
options: A guess about the diagnosis and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, for now
The client's favorite foods, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Relevant history: admitting diagnosis, baseline vitals, recent changes, and current antibiotics
The PN's weekend plans, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C - background gives the clinical context: history, baseline, changes, and treatments. D and B are irrelevant. A is wrong - the PN reports data, not diagnostic guesses.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client observing Ramadan wishes to fast from dawn to sunset. The PN's best action is to:
options: Forbid fasting for medical reasons without discussion, then reassess the patient after the intervention
Ignore the request, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, in practice
Tell the client religion does not matter in the hospital
Respect the practice, coordinate medication and meal timing with the RN/provider and dietitian as needed
explain: Correct: D - cultural accommodation with clinical coordination respects beliefs while maintaining safety. A is wrong - blanket forbidding without assessment is disrespectful. B is wrong - ignoring the request is nontherapeutic. C is wrong - spirituality matters to many clients.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A deaf client needs discharge teaching reinforced. The PN should:
options: Use a qualified sign language interpreter and written materials as appropriate
Have a family member guess the signs, based on the findings documented so far
Shout the instructions, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Skip the teaching since it is too difficult, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: A - qualified interpreters plus written reinforcement ensure understanding. C is wrong - shouting does not help deaf clients. B is wrong - guessing at signs risks dangerous miscommunication. D is wrong - difficulty never justifies skipping teaching.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is reinforcing home wound care teaching at discharge. The PN should ensure the client has:
options: Instructions in a language the client does not read, and ensure the side rails are raised before leaving the room
Necessary supplies or a plan to obtain them, plus clear written instructions reinforced with teach-back
No supplies; they can improvise, while monitoring for signs of infection at the site
Only verbal instructions, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: B - supplies, written instructions, and teach-back enable safe home care. C is wrong - improvisation risks infection. D is wrong - verbal-only instructions are forgotten. A is wrong - instructions must be in the client's language.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The provider orders home health nursing for a client. The PN's role is to:
options: Cancel the referral if the client seems unsure, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, at this stage, for now
Arrange the agency independently, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion
Reinforce the teaching about the referral and report the client's questions or concerns to the RN/discharge planner
Tell the client home health is unnecessary, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - the PN reinforces and reports; coordination belongs to the discharge team. B is wrong - the PN does not arrange referrals independently. A is wrong - the PN does not cancel orders. D is wrong - discouraging needed services harms the client.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A family asks about the difference between palliative care and hospice. The PN's best response is to:
options: Say they are exactly the same and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
Make the decision for the family, before checking the patient's allergy status for the medication, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time
Tell them neither is available, and assess the patient's understanding of the teaching provided, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment
Explain that palliative care can accompany curative treatment at any stage, while hospice focuses on comfort when cure is no longer pursued, and refer detailed questions to the RN
explain: Correct: D - accurate basic explanation with referral for details respects the PN's teaching role. A is wrong - they differ in goals and timing. C is wrong - both are real options. B is wrong - the family decides with the team.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which clients should the PN assess first when starting the shift? The PN should prioritize:
options: The client closest to the nurses' station, during the current shift
The client with the most acute change or highest instability
The client who is most talkative, in accordance with facility policy
The client who arrived first, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - acuity, not arrival order or location, drives prioritization. D, C, and A use irrelevant criteria.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions are appropriate when the PN suspects a client is being trafficked? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting per facility policy and law
Ensuring the client's immediate safety
Documenting objective observations
Confronting the suspected trafficker aggressively
Separating the client from the suspected trafficker when safe to do so
explain: Correct: B, E, A, C - safety, separation when safe, reporting, and objective documentation are required. D is wrong - aggressive confrontation endangers the client and the PN.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which statements about informed consent are true? Select all that apply.
options: Consent once signed can never be withdrawn
Consent must be voluntary and informed
The PN may witness the signature after consent is obtained
The provider explains the procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives
The client must be competent to consent
explain: Correct: B, E, D, C - voluntary, competent, provider-explained, and PN-witnessed are the consent elements. A is wrong - clients may withdraw consent at any time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which are appropriate PN responses to a client's pain report? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting unrelieved pain to the RN
Documenting the assessment and interventions
Believing the client's report
Assessing pain characteristics thoroughly
Telling the client the pain is exaggerated
explain: Correct: C, D, A, B - pain is what the client says it is; thorough assessment, reporting, and documentation are required. E is wrong - dismissing pain is nontherapeutic and unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions demonstrate accountability in PN practice? Select all that apply.
options: Seeking help when unsure
Following up on delegated tasks
Admitting and reporting errors promptly
Blaming others for mistakes
Practicing within competence
explain: Correct: C, A, B, E - owning errors, seeking help, supervising delegation, and staying within competence are accountability. D is wrong - blame-shifting is the opposite of accountability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is being transferred to long-term care. The PN should ensure the transfer includes: Select all that apply.
options: Current medications and orders
A complete handoff report
Advance directive status
Contact information for family
The client's valuables left unsecured
explain: Correct: B, A, C, D - handoff, meds, advance directives, and contacts ensure continuity. E is wrong - valuables must be secured per policy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which situations require the PN to use the chain of command? Select all that apply.
options: A conflict with a colleague that affects client care
An unresolved concern about a provider's order
A disagreement about lunch break timing
A safety issue the immediate supervisor has not addressed
A routine request for extra blankets
explain: Correct: B, D, A - unresolved order concerns, unaddressed safety issues, and care-affecting conflicts all warrant escalation. E and C are routine matters handled through normal channels.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is reinforcing trampoline safety. The key teaching includes:
options: One person at a time, with safety netting and padding, and adult supervision
Multiple children jumping together is safest, at the patient's bedside
Flips are safe for beginners, during the current shift
Trampolines need no safety equipment, for now
explain: Correct: A - single users, netting, padding, and supervision reduce injuries. B is wrong - multiple jumpers cause collisions. C is wrong - flips risk spinal injuries. D is wrong - safety equipment is essential.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces ATV safety for teens. The teaching includes:
options: Riding on paved roads is safest, as documented in the plan of care
No helmet is needed for short rides, before checking the patient's allergy status for the medication
Helmet use, no passengers on single-rider ATVs, adult supervision, and age-appropriate vehicle size
Doubling passengers is fine, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
explain: Correct: C - helmets, single riders, supervision, and proper sizing prevent ATV deaths. B is wrong - helmets are always needed. A is wrong - ATVs are designed for off-road use. D is wrong - passengers destabilize single-rider ATVs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces lawn mower safety. The key points include:
options: Removing safety guards for better cutting, while keeping the patient warm and comfortable
Keeping children indoors during mowing, wearing sturdy shoes, and never reaching under the deck
Letting young children ride on the mower, using the equipment available at the bedside
Mowing in the dark to avoid heat, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: B - children away, protective footwear, and respecting the deck prevent amputations. C is wrong - riders fall under mowers. A is wrong - guards prevent contact with blades. D is wrong - darkness hides hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces mouthguard use for a teen in contact sports. The reason is:
options: Mouthguards are just for appearance, during the current shift
Only professionals need them, for now
They make breathing impossible, in accordance with facility policy
Mouthguards prevent dental injuries and reduce concussion risk
explain: Correct: D - mouthguards protect teeth and jaws. A is wrong - they are protective equipment. B is wrong - all contact-sport athletes benefit. C is wrong - fitted guards allow breathing.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces safe diving teaching. The key point is:
options: Never dive into shallow or unknown water; enter feet first
Dive into shallow water headfirst, during the current shift
Diving is safe anywhere, based on the findings documented so far
Alcohol improves diving safety, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A - shallow-water diving causes spinal cord injuries; feet-first entry in known deep water is the rule. B is wrong - headfirst shallow diving paralyzes. C is wrong - unknown water hides hazards. D is wrong - alcohol impairs judgment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces boating safety. The teaching includes:
options: Children do not need life jackets, while keeping the patient warm and comfortable
Overloading the boat is fine, and encourage the patient to report any new symptoms
Everyone wears a properly fitted life jacket, and boating under the influence is avoided
Life jackets are optional for good swimmers, while keeping the patient safe from injury at all times
explain: Correct: C - universal life jacket use and sober operation prevent drowning. D is wrong - even strong swimmers drown. A is wrong - children need jackets most. B is wrong - overloading capsizes boats.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces backpack safety for school children. The teaching includes:
options: Keep the load under 10-15% of body weight, use both straps, and pack heaviest items closest to the back
Carry the backpack on one shoulder always, before administering any further medication
Weight does not matter for children and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, for now
Carry as much weight as possible, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A - light loads, two straps, and proper packing prevent back injury. D is wrong - heavy loads injure growing spines. B is wrong - single-strap carrying strains the back. C is wrong - weight matters greatly.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces internet safety for teens. The teaching includes:
options: Privacy settings do not matter, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change, based on the findings documented so far
Keep personal details private, never meet online contacts alone, and tell a trusted adult about uncomfortable interactions
Share personal information freely online, and verify the order against the medication administration record, on this occasion
Online friends are always safe, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: B - privacy, no solo meetups, and reporting uncomfortable contacts protect teens. C is wrong - oversharing enables predators. D is wrong - online identities can be faked. A is wrong - privacy settings are a key defense.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A teen tells the PN about being bullied at school. The PN's best action is to:
options: Ignore it as normal teen behavior, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, on this occasion
Tell the teen bullying builds character, then evaluate the patient's response within the hour
Tell the teen to fight back, and encourage the patient to report any new symptoms
Take it seriously, ensure safety, and report per school and facility policy, connecting the teen with resources
explain: Correct: D - bullying is taken seriously with safety planning, reporting, and resources. C is wrong - fighting back escalates danger. B is wrong - bullying causes real harm. A is wrong - it is not normal or acceptable.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which stranger safety points should the PN reinforce for school-age children? Select all that apply.
options: Yelling and running to a trusted adult if grabbed
Never going with a stranger, even with offered treats
Accepting rides from friendly strangers
Keeping secrets for a stranger who asks
Knowing their full name, address, and phone number
explain: Correct: B, E, A - refusal, self-identification knowledge, and yelling/running are protective. C is wrong - rides from strangers are never accepted. D is wrong - secret-keeping enables abuse.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces healthy dating relationships for teens. Warning signs of dating violence include: Select all that apply.
options: Pressuring for unwanted sexual activity
Insults and put-downs
Threats or physical aggression
Controlling behavior and jealousy
Respecting boundaries and opinions
explain: Correct: D, B, C, A - control, verbal abuse, threats/violence, and sexual pressure are dating violence signs. E is wrong - respect is healthy, not a warning sign.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which vaping risks should the PN reinforce for teens? Select all that apply.
options: That vaping is completely safe
Nicotine addiction
That vaping helps athletic performance
Exposure to harmful chemicals
Lung injury
explain: Correct: B, E, D - addiction, lung injury (EVALI), and toxic chemicals are real vaping risks. A is wrong - vaping is not safe. C is wrong - vaping harms lung function and performance.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces COVID-19 vaccine teaching. Which statement is correct?
options: Vaccines are only for the elderly, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
The vaccine helps prevent severe illness and follows current public health recommendations
Natural infection is always safer than vaccination, during the current shift
The vaccine gives you COVID-19, and verify the order against the medication administration record, for now
explain: Correct: B - COVID vaccines reduce severe disease per public health guidance. D is wrong - vaccines do not cause COVID-19. A is wrong - recommendations span age groups. C is wrong - natural infection carries higher risks.

q: A parent asks how much a newborn should sleep. The PN reinforces:
options: Sleep needs are the same at all ages, at the patient's bedside
Newborns should stay awake all day, during the current shift
Newborns sleep about 14-17 hours daily in short stretches
Newborns need only 4 hours a day, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C - 14-17 hours in short cycles is normal newborn sleep. D is far too little. B is wrong - newborns cannot stay awake all day. A is wrong - sleep needs change with age.

q: A parent asks about teen sleep needs. The PN reinforces:
options: Sleep needs decrease to adult levels at 13
Teens need only 5 hours
Teens function best on no sleep, as documented in the plan of care
Teens need about 8-10 hours of sleep nightly
explain: Correct: D - 8-10 hours supports teen growth, learning, and mood. B is insufficient. C is dangerous nonsense. A is wrong - teens need more than adults.

q: The PN reinforces screen time guidance for toddlers. The correct teaching is:
options: Limit screen time, prioritize interactive play, and avoid screens during meals and before bed
Screens are the best babysitter, then report the outcome to the registered nurse
Unlimited screen time is fine and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response
Toddlers learn best from screens alone, then evaluate the patient's response within the hour
explain: Correct: A - limited, purposeful screen use with play priority supports development. C is wrong - excessive screens displace active play. B is wrong - screens are not caregivers. D is wrong - toddlers learn through interaction, not screens.

q: The PN reinforces reading to young children. The benefit to emphasize is:
options: Reading is only for school-age children, during the current shift
Daily reading builds language, bonding, and school readiness
Television teaches language better, on this occasion
Reading should be avoided until age 5, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - reading aloud from infancy builds vocabulary and attachment. A is wrong - benefits start in infancy. C is wrong - interactive reading outperforms passive TV. D is wrong - early reading is encouraged.

q: A parent asks about dental sealants. The PN reinforces that sealants:
options: Protect molars from decay and are recommended for children at risk
Are never recommended, in accordance with facility policy
Are only for adults, based on the findings documented so far
Replace brushing, before the end of the shift, for now
explain: Correct: A - sealants shield molar grooves where decay starts. B is wrong - they are evidence-based prevention. D is wrong - they supplement, not replace, brushing. C is wrong - they are primarily pediatric.

q: Which are expected milestones for a 2-month-old? Select all that apply.
options: Brief head lift when prone
Cooing sounds
Walking
Sitting without support
Social smile
explain: Correct: E, B, A - smiling, cooing, and head control are 2-month milestones. D is wrong - independent sitting comes around 6 months. C is wrong - walking comes around 12 months.

q: Which are expected milestones for a 4-month-old? Select all that apply.
options: Reaching and grasping
Riding a bicycle
Tying shoes
Rolling from front to back
Laughing aloud
explain: Correct: E, D, A - laughter, rolling, and grasping are 4-month milestones. B and C are years away.

q: A client rambles through a long story. The PN responds, 'What I hear you saying is that you feel overwhelmed.' This is an example of:
options: Changing the subject, for now
Giving advice, on this occasion, in full
False reassurance, in this case
Summarizing to clarify and focus
explain: Correct: D - summarizing distills the message and checks understanding. A is wrong - the PN stayed with the client's theme. B is wrong - no advice was given. C is wrong - no reassurance was offered.

q: A client insists they have no problem with alcohol despite daily heavy drinking. The PN gently notes the discrepancy between the client's words and missed workdays. This is an example of:
options: Changing the subject, on this occasion
Arguing, based on the findings documented so far
Therapeutic confrontation of a discrepancy
Agreement, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - gentle confrontation highlights the gap between words and behavior to promote insight. B is wrong - the tone is nonjudgmental, not argumentative. D is wrong - the PN did not agree. A is wrong - the topic was addressed directly.

q: After yelling at a coworker, a client apologizes excessively and brings gifts. The PN recognizes this as possibly:
options: Denial, based on the findings documented so far
Projection, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Sublimation, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Undoing, an attempt to cancel out the behavior
explain: Correct: D - undoing tries to 'take back' an act through reparative behavior. C is wrong - nothing productive is created from the impulse. B is wrong - feelings are not attributed to others. A is wrong - the act is acknowledged, not denied.

q: A client with bulimia nervosa is admitted. The PN's priority is to:
options: Monitor for purging behaviors per the plan, provide a structured supportive environment, and report concerns to the RN
Weigh the client publicly, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, before the end of the shift
Allow unrestricted bathroom access immediately after meals, before administering any further medication
Comment on the client's weight, while keeping the head of the bed elevated as tolerated
explain: Correct: A - structured monitoring with therapeutic support and reporting is the PN's role. D is wrong - weight comments worsen the disorder. C is wrong - post-meal bathroom monitoring is part of the plan. B is wrong - public weigh-ins are shaming.

q: A client on long-term opioids is being tapered and develops agitation, sweating, and muscle aches. The PN should:
options: Discharge the client immediately, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Keep the client safe and comfortable, monitor vital signs, and report withdrawal symptoms to the RN
Tell the client withdrawal is imaginary, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Give the client extra opioids from another client's supply
explain: Correct: B - opioid withdrawal needs supportive monitoring and RN/provider management. C is wrong - withdrawal is real and distressing. D is wrong - diverting another client's medication is illegal. A is wrong - abandonment during withdrawal is unsafe.

q: Which approaches help a client with generalized anxiety? Select all that apply.
options: Teaching slow breathing and relaxation techniques
Staying with the client during high anxiety
Encouraging the client to describe feelings
Reducing overwhelming stimuli
Telling the client to just stop worrying
explain: Correct: B, A, D, C - presence, breathing techniques, low stimulation, and feeling exploration all reduce anxiety. E is wrong - 'just stop worrying' is dismissive and nontherapeutic.

q: A client's spouse is dying. Which signs suggest anticipatory grief that the PN should support? Select all that apply.
options: Sadness and tearfulness before the death
Discussing funeral plans
Anger about the situation
Withdrawing from the dying spouse
Complete absence of any emotion forever
explain: Correct: A, D, C, B - sadness, withdrawal, anger, and planning are all part of anticipatory grief. E is wrong - total permanent absence of emotion is not the expected pattern.

q: Which elements belong in a client's safety plan that the PN reinforces? Select all that apply.
options: Trusted people to contact
A promise that crises will never happen
Coping strategies that have helped before
Professional resources and crisis numbers
Warning signs that a crisis is developing
explain: Correct: E, C, A, D - warning signs, coping tools, supports, and resources make a workable safety plan. B is wrong - guaranteeing no future crises is impossible and false.

q: The PN is caring for a client with an ileal conduit (urostomy). The PN should:
options: Remove the pouch permanently to let the stoma air out, at the patient's bedside
Irrigate the stoma daily, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, in full
Monitor stoma color, pouch output, and peristomal skin, emptying the pouch regularly and reporting changes to the RN
Expect the pouch to stay dry, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: C - pink stoma, continuous urine output, and intact skin are monitored with regular emptying. D is wrong - the pouch fills continuously with urine. B is wrong - routine stoma irrigation is not done. A is wrong - the pouch must stay in place.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client has a nephrostomy tube. The PN's priority is to:
options: Remove it when output looks clear, in accordance with facility policy
Clamp the tube to test tolerance, while observing the patient for any adverse reaction
Keep the tube patent and secured, monitor output, and report decreased output, fever, or dislodgement to the RN
Irrigate it forcefully daily, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - patency, securement, output monitoring, and reporting are the PN's roles. B is wrong - clamping needs orders. D is wrong - forceful irrigation is dangerous. A is wrong - removal needs an order.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assisting with a client's morning care. The client can do partial tasks. The PN should:
options: Encourage the client to do what they can, assisting only as needed
Skip morning care to save time, during the current shift
Refuse to help with any tasks and verify the result with a second measurement
Do everything quickly, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A - promoting self-care preserves function and dignity. D is wrong - doing everything fosters dependence. B is wrong - hygiene is not skipped. C is wrong - refusing help is neglectful.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with a new suprapubic catheter asks about care. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Ignore cloudy urine, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Keep the insertion site clean and dry, secure the tubing, and report fever, blockage, or leakage to the RN
Pull on the catheter to test it, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Remove it for showers permanently, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time
explain: Correct: B - site hygiene, securement, and reporting complications are correct. C is wrong - pulling traumatizes the tract. D is wrong - removal needs an order. A is wrong - cloudy urine may signal infection needing evaluation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is reinforcing sitz bath teaching after perineal surgery. The correct instructions are:
options: Take sitz baths only once a week, in accordance with facility policy
Add strong disinfectants to the water, during the current shift
Use very hot water for 30 minutes, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Use warm water for about 15-20 minutes, then pat dry gently
explain: Correct: D - warm (not hot) water for 15-20 minutes soothes and promotes healing. C is wrong - very hot water burns and 30 minutes is excessive. B is wrong - harsh chemicals irritate healing tissue. A is wrong - frequency follows orders, typically more often.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with a colostomy is concerned about odor. The PN can reinforce:
options: There is nothing that helps, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
Remove the pouch in public, and verify the order against the medication administration record
Pouch deodorants, proper pouch seal, diet adjustments, and regular emptying help control odor
Stop eating to prevent odor, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C - deodorants, good seals, diet tweaks, and emptying manage odor effectively. A is wrong - many strategies help. D is wrong - starving is dangerous. B is wrong - removing the pouch is unsanitary.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN reinforces nighttime incontinence management. The teaching includes:
options: Drink large amounts of fluid before bed, then reassess the patient after the intervention
Limit evening fluids, void before bed, and keep a clear path to the bathroom
Avoid all daytime fluids, on this occasion
Wear heavy diapers and ignore the issue, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - evening fluid limits, bedtime voiding, and safe bathroom access reduce nighttime episodes. A is wrong - bedtime fluids worsen nocturia. D is wrong - containment alone ignores management. C is wrong - daytime fluids are still needed.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help promote bowel continence? Select all that apply.
options: Adequate fiber and fluids as ordered
Responding promptly to the urge to defecate
Scheduled toileting after meals to use the gastrocolic reflex
Ignoring bowel urges
Prolonged bed rest
explain: Correct: C, A, B - timed toileting, fiber/fluids, and prompt response build bowel control. D is wrong - ignoring urges causes incontinence and impaction. E is wrong - immobility worsens bowel function.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help relieve dry mouth? Select all that apply.
options: Drinking alcohol to stimulate saliva
Using a humidifier at night
Using sugarless gum or candy
Sipping water frequently
Avoiding alcohol-based mouthwashes
explain: Correct: D, C, E, B - hydration, sugarless stimulants, avoiding drying mouthwashes, and humid air all help. A is wrong - alcohol dries the mouth further.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which nonpharmacologic strategies help manage chronic pain? Select all that apply.
options: Relaxation and deep breathing
Heat or cold as ordered
Gentle activity as tolerated
Distraction techniques
Complete bed rest indefinitely
explain: Correct: A, C, B, D - relaxation, activity, thermal therapies, and distraction are evidence-based pain strategies. E is wrong - indefinite bed rest worsens chronic pain and function.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client takes pioglitazone. Which finding must the PN report to the RN?
options: Rapid weight gain with edema and shortness of breath
Occasional nausea, for the duration of the patient's stay
Mild headache, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Mild fatigue, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A - rapid weight gain, edema, and dyspnea suggest heart failure, a pioglitazone risk. C, B, and D are not the critical warning signs.

q: A client takes empagliflozin. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Double the dose when glucose is high, in accordance with facility policy
Stop drinking water, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Ignore urinary symptoms, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Report burning urination, fever, or genital itching; maintain good hygiene and hydration
explain: Correct: D - SGLT2 inhibitors raise genital mycotic and UTI risk; hygiene, hydration, and reporting matter. C is wrong - urinary symptoms need evaluation. B is wrong - dehydration worsens risks. A is wrong - dose changes need orders.

q: A client with hyperthyroidism takes propranolol. The PN should monitor and report:
options: Increased appetite, on this occasion
Warm skin, going forward
Weight gain, at this stage, for now
Bradycardia, hypotension, or wheezing
explain: Correct: D - beta blockers can cause excessive slowing, low pressure, and bronchospasm. A, C, and B are not beta-blocker warning signs.

q: A client takes diltiazem. Which finding should the PN report?
options: Mild flushing
Blood pressure 128/80 mmHg
Heart rate 48 beats/min
Occasional headache
explain: Correct: C - calcium channel blockers can cause significant bradycardia needing evaluation. B is a good BP. A and D are common mild effects.

q: A client takes verapamil and reports constipation. The PN's best response is to:
options: Tell the client to stop the drug, based on the findings documented so far
Reinforce fluids, fiber, and activity as ordered, and report severe or persistent constipation to the RN
Ignore the complaint, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Recommend harsh laxatives freely, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
explain: Correct: B - constipation is a common verapamil effect managed with lifestyle measures and reporting. A is wrong - the PN does not stop drugs. D is wrong - laxatives need direction. C is wrong - the complaint deserves a response.

q: A client starts isosorbide dinitrate for angina. The PN reinforces that:
options: Headache and flushing are common at first; sit or lie down if dizzy and report severe symptoms
It can be stopped abruptly without issue, and make sure the patient understands the instructions given
The drug works instantly like nitroglycerin, because the patient has tolerated the same intervention before
Headache is unexpected and alarming, using the equipment available at the bedside
explain: Correct: A - headaches from vasodilation are common initially; positional caution and reporting are correct. D is wrong - headache is expected. C is wrong - isosorbide is longer-acting, not sublingual rescue. B is wrong - abrupt stop can worsen angina.

q: A client takes clonidine. The most important teaching point the PN should reinforce is:
options: Do not stop abruptly; rebound hypertension can occur, so taper only as directed
Double the dose if blood pressure is high one day, during the current shift
It never causes drowsiness, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
It can be stopped suddenly without problems, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - abrupt clonidine withdrawal causes dangerous rebound hypertension. D is wrong - sudden stop is hazardous. C is wrong - drowsiness is common. B is wrong - dose changes need orders.

q: A client takes hydralazine and reports joint pain and fever. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client it is harmless, during the current shift
Tell the client to double the dose, as documented in the plan of care
Suggest the client stop eating salt, based on the findings documented so far
Report to the RN; hydralazine can rarely cause a lupus-like syndrome
explain: Correct: D - drug-induced lupus-like syndrome needs provider evaluation. A is wrong - it needs assessment. B is wrong - dose changes need orders. C is irrelevant to the symptoms.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching about tetracycline. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Take it with milk to improve absorption
Take it on an empty stomach as directed, separate from dairy and antacids
Share it with family for similar symptoms
Avoid excessive sun exposure; it causes photosensitivity
Report severe headache or vision changes
explain: Correct: D, B, E - sun protection, proper timing away from calcium, and reporting intracranial hypertension signs are correct. A is wrong - dairy impairs absorption. C is wrong - antibiotics are never shared.

q: Which medications can harm the kidneys that the PN should monitor for? Select all that apply.
options: Penicillin in normal doses for most clients
NSAIDs with prolonged use
Aminoglycoside antibiotics
Normal saline in small amounts
IV contrast dye
explain: Correct: B, C, E - NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and contrast are nephrotoxic; the PN monitors output and labs. A is wrong - penicillin is not typically nephrotoxic at normal doses. D is wrong - small saline amounts are not nephrotoxic.

q: The PN is reinforcing lithium teaching (in addition to toxicity signs). Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Have blood levels monitored as ordered
NSAIDs can raise lithium levels; report new medications
Report increased thirst with very large urine volumes
Maintain consistent salt and fluid intake
Stop the drug abruptly when feeling well
explain: Correct: D, A, C, B - consistent sodium/fluids, level monitoring, reporting polyuria, and NSAID interactions are lithium essentials. E is wrong - abrupt stop risks relapse.

q: Which are correct about PRN pain medication administration? Select all that apply.
options: Giving the maximum dose every time regardless of pain level
Documenting the dose, time, and response
Assessing pain before administration
Checking when the last dose was given
Reassessing pain after the medication takes effect
explain: Correct: C, D, B, E - assessment, timing checks, documentation, and reassessment are required. A is wrong - dosing follows the order parameters and the client's pain level.

q: A client's lactate is 4.5 mmol/L with hypotension. The PN should:
options: Recheck next week, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission, in practice
Encourage exercise, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, in accordance with facility policy
Report to the RN immediately; elevated lactate with hypotension suggests tissue hypoperfusion and possible sepsis
Document it as normal, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, for now
explain: Correct: C - lactate above 2 with hypotension signals shock needing urgent care. D is wrong - 4.5 is critically high. B is wrong - exercise is contraindicated. A is wrong - waiting is unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a kidney biopsy, the PN should monitor and report which finding?
options: The client wanting to rest, using the equipment available at the bedside
Hematuria that increases or does not clear, or dropping blood pressure
A small bandage, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Mild back soreness, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B - worsening hematuria or hypotension suggests post-biopsy bleeding. D is expected discomfort. C is normal care. A is expected recovery behavior.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before surgery, the PN reinforces chlorhexidine shower teaching. The correct instruction is:
options: Apply chlorhexidine and leave it on for days, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change, in practice
Shower with regular soap only, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, on this occasion
Shower with chlorhexidine as instructed the night before and morning of surgery, avoiding the face and rinsing well
Skip showering to save the antiseptic, and verify the order against the medication administration record, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - timed chlorhexidine showers reduce skin bacteria and surgical site infection. B is wrong - regular soap is less effective for this purpose. D is wrong - skipping defeats the purpose. A is wrong - it is rinsed off per instructions.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN is reinforcing VTE prophylaxis teaching. The PN explains that prevention includes:
options: Prolonged bed rest, as documented in the plan of care
Early ambulation, leg exercises, sequential compression devices, and ordered anticoagulants
Crossing the legs, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, at this stage
Avoiding all movement, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
explain: Correct: B - mobility, SCDs, and ordered anticoagulants prevent clots. A is wrong - bed rest causes clots. C is wrong - crossing impedes flow. D is wrong - immobility is the risk.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a kidney biopsy, which PN actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Encouraging strenuous activity immediately
Reporting severe flank pain or hypotension to the RN
Checking urine for blood
Monitoring vital signs closely
Keeping the client on bed rest as ordered
explain: Correct: D, C, E, B - vital signs, hematuria checks, bed rest, and bleeding-sign reporting are correct. A is wrong - rest, not exertion, follows kidney biopsy.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which measures are part of the surgical site infection prevention bundle? Select all that apply.
options: Maintaining normal body temperature
Appropriate hair removal with clippers
Chlorhexidine skin preparation
Shaving the site with a razor the night before
Timely prophylactic antibiotics per orders
explain: Correct: E, C, A, B - timely antibiotics, chlorhexidine prep, normothermia, and clipper hair removal prevent SSI. D is wrong - razor shaving increases infection risk.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which VTE prophylaxis measures can the PN reinforce or perform? Select all that apply.
options: Applying sequential compression devices as ordered
Administering ordered anticoagulants
Teaching leg exercises
Encouraging prolonged sitting with legs crossed
Encouraging early ambulation as ordered
explain: Correct: E, A, C, B - ambulation, SCDs, exercises, and ordered anticoagulants are the prophylaxis pillars. D is wrong - crossed-leg sitting impedes venous return.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client's surgical drain falls out. The PN's first actions are to:
options: Cover the site with a sterile dressing, note the time and drainage characteristics, and report to the RN immediately
Ignore it since drains fall out often, without first verifying the patient's identity at the bedside
Pull the rest of the tubing out forcefully, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, at this stage
Push it back in, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, in this case
explain: Correct: A - dislodged drains need sterile coverage, documentation, and RN notification. D is wrong - never reinsert dislodged drains. B is wrong - it needs assessment and reporting. C is wrong - forceful pulling injures tissue.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The PN finds a client picking at the surgical dressing with the wound exposed. The PN should:
options: Remove the rest of the dressing, as documented in the plan of care
Leave the wound open to air, based on the findings documented so far
Scold the client, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion
Apply clean gloves, cover the wound, assess, reinforce the need to keep it covered, and report to the RN
explain: Correct: D - protect the wound, assess contamination, educate, and report. C is wrong - scolding is nontherapeutic. B is wrong - open surgical wounds risk infection. A is wrong - the RN determines dressing needs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A pre-op client's hemoglobin is 8.5 g/dL. The PN should:
options: Document it as normal, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Cancel the surgery independently, before the end of the shift
Tell the client to eat spinach right before surgery, at the patient's bedside
Report it to the RN; anemia increases surgical risk and may need correction
explain: Correct: D - preoperative anemia needs provider evaluation and possible treatment. A is wrong - 8.5 is below normal. C is wrong - spinach does not fix acute anemia. B is wrong - the PN does not cancel surgeries.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After cardiac surgery, the PN notes hypotension, distended neck veins, and muffled heart sounds. The PN should:
options: Give fluids rapidly without an order, and proceed without confirming the order in the chart
Encourage the client to cough forcefully, as documented in the plan of care
Recognize Beck's triad suggesting cardiac tamponade and notify the RN immediately
Document and recheck in an hour, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: C - hypotension, JVD, and muffled sounds are tamponade's classic triad, a surgical emergency. D is wrong - waiting is fatal. B is wrong - coughing does not treat tamponade. A is wrong - fluid boluses need orders.

q: A client with a heart valve replacement develops fever, chills, and a new murmur. The PN should:
options: Report to the RN promptly; fever with a new murmur suggests endocarditis
Reassure the client it is a cold, during the current shift
Encourage vigorous exercise, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Tell the client to wait a week, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - endocarditis is a feared complication of valve replacement needing urgent workup. B is wrong - this is not a cold. C is wrong - exercise is unsafe. D is wrong - waiting risks valve destruction.

q: A client's heart rate is 38 beats/min with dizziness. The PN should:
options: Give caffeine without an order and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response
Report to the RN immediately; symptomatic bradycardia may indicate heart block needing urgent evaluation
Document it as normal, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, in accordance with facility policy
Encourage the client to run in place and notify the registered nurse of the patient's status
explain: Correct: B - bradycardia with symptoms suggests conduction disease needing prompt care. C is wrong - 38 with dizziness is not normal. D is wrong - exertion is dangerous. A is wrong - medicating without orders exceeds scope.

q: A pregnant client with preeclampsia develops hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets. The PN recognizes this as:
options: A reason to encourage labor at home, before the end of the shift, in full
HELLP syndrome, an obstetric emergency needing immediate RN notification
Normal pregnancy labs, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Mild anemia, during the current shift, for now
explain: Correct: B - HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets) threatens mother and fetus. C is wrong - these labs are critically abnormal. D is wrong - this is far more than mild anemia. A is wrong - home labor with HELLP is dangerous.

q: During labor, a client suddenly becomes severely dyspneic, hypotensive, and seizes. The PN should:
options: Call for help and notify the RN immediately; this suggests amniotic fluid embolism, a catastrophic emergency
Offer oral fluids, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Continue routine labor support, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
Encourage pushing, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - sudden cardiopulmonary collapse in labor suggests amniotic fluid embolism needing full emergency response. C is wrong - routine care is inappropriate. D is wrong - pushing is irrelevant. B is wrong - fluids do not treat embolism.

q: After membrane rupture, the PN sees the umbilical cord protruding from the vagina. The PN's first action is to:
options: Push the cord back inside, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, because the provider is expected to review the case later today, in this case
Clamp and cut the cord, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, since no change has been reported in the patient's condition, in practice
Encourage the client to walk, and verify the order against the medication administration record, with the patient's safety as the stated priority
Position the client knee-chest or Trendelenburg, gloved hand to relieve cord pressure if trained per protocol, call for help, and notify the RN immediately
explain: Correct: D - cord prolapse compresses the fetal lifeline; positioning reduces pressure while help arrives. A is wrong - pushing the cord in is not done. B is wrong - cutting the cord before delivery kills the fetus. C is wrong - walking worsens compression.

q: During delivery, the head delivers but the shoulders do not follow with gentle traction. The PN should:
options: Push on the fundus forcefully, before the end of the shift
Pull forcefully on the head, while disregarding the patient's reported symptoms
Call for help immediately and assist as directed; this suggests shoulder dystocia
Tell the mother to stop pushing forever, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - shoulder dystocia is an obstetric emergency needing the team and specific maneuvers. B is wrong - forceful pulling injures the baby. A is wrong - fundal pressure worsens impaction. D is wrong - pushing efforts are managed, not abandoned.

q: A 5-day-old has temperature instability, poor feeding, and lethargy. The PN should:
options: Swaddle tighter and wait, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Report to the RN promptly; these suggest neonatal sepsis
Give honey for energy, before the end of the shift
Assume newborns are always sleepy, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - temperature instability with poor feeding and lethargy are neonatal sepsis red flags. D is wrong - this exceeds normal sleepiness. A is wrong - waiting risks death. C is wrong - honey risks botulism and does not treat sepsis.

q: A newborn's umbilical stump shows spreading redness onto the abdomen with foul odor. The PN should:
options: Pull the stump off, as documented in the plan of care
Apply more alcohol and wait, with the patient's safety as the stated priority
Report to the RN promptly; this suggests omphalitis, a serious infection
Cover it with a dirty diaper, and record the intake and output for the shift
explain: Correct: C - spreading periumbilical redness is omphalitis needing urgent treatment. B is wrong - alcohol does not treat spreading infection. A is wrong - pulling the stump injures tissue. D is wrong - dirty diapers worsen infection.

q: A premature infant develops abdominal distention, bloody stools, and feeding intolerance. The PN should:
options: Massage the abdomen vigorously, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Continue feedings as usual, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Give extra formula, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, in accordance with facility policy
Stop feedings per protocol, keep NPO, and notify the RN immediately; this suggests necrotizing enterocolitis
explain: Correct: D - NEC is a neonatal emergency; feedings stop and the team is notified. B is wrong - continuing feeds worsens NEC. C is wrong - more formula is contraindicated. A is wrong - vigorous massage risks perforation.

q: A newborn with cleft palate is having difficulty feeding. The PN reinforces that the parents should:
options: Use special bottles and upright positioning as taught, feed slowly, and report poor weight gain
Force rapid feeding, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Give up on feeding, before the end of the shift, for now
Feed lying flat, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
explain: Correct: A - specialized bottles, upright slow feeding, and weight monitoring manage cleft feeding. C is wrong - feeding is achievable with techniques. D is wrong - flat feeding risks aspiration. B is wrong - rapid feeding causes choking.

q: A newborn has excessive drooling with coughing and choking during feeds. The PN should:
options: Pat the baby's back harder, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
Give thicker formula, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Stop oral feeding, keep NPO, and notify the RN immediately; this suggests tracheoesophageal fistula
Continue feeding normally, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: C - the drooling-choking triad suggests TEF; oral feeds risk aspiration pneumonia. D is wrong - continuing feeds is dangerous. B is wrong - thicker formula does not fix a fistula. A is wrong - harder patting does not help.

q: A newborn has a scaphoid (sunken) abdomen with respiratory distress. The PN should:
options: Place the baby prone, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Keep NPO, position to ease breathing, and notify the RN immediately; this suggests diaphragmatic hernia
Feed the baby to calm them, then reassess the patient's respiratory status
Give oxygen without reporting, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B - scaphoid abdomen with distress suggests abdominal organs in the chest; NPO and urgent evaluation are needed. C is wrong - feeding is contraindicated. A is wrong - positioning follows protocol, not routine prone. D is wrong - the RN must be notified.

q: A newborn's intestines are exposed through an abdominal wall defect covered by a membrane. The PN's priority is to:
options: Keep the infant NPO, cover the defect with sterile saline moistened dressing per protocol, keep warm, and notify the RN immediately
Feed the infant, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Touch the exposed bowel to assess, and verify the order against the medication administration record, on this occasion
Push the intestines back in, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change, at this stage
explain: Correct: A - gastroschisis/omphalocele needs sterile moist coverage, warmth, NPO, and urgent surgical evaluation. C is wrong - touching risks infection. D is wrong - never push bowel back. B is wrong - feeding is contraindicated.

q: A 2-day-old has not passed stool, has a distended abdomen, and vomits bile. The PN should:
options: Give a rectal thermometer to stimulate stool, as part of the routine care for this patient
Wait another week, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, in practice
Offer more formula, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Keep NPO and notify the RN immediately; this suggests Hirschsprung disease or intestinal obstruction
explain: Correct: D - delayed stool with distention and bilious vomiting signals obstruction needing urgent workup. A is wrong - rectal stimulation is not the intervention. C is wrong - more formula worsens obstruction. B is wrong - waiting risks perforation.

q: Which findings suggest cardiac tamponade that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: Hypotension
Distended neck veins
Clear lung sounds with normal blood pressure
Pulsus paradoxus
Muffled heart sounds
explain: Correct: A, B, E, D - hypotension, JVD, muffled sounds, and pulsus paradoxus are tamponade signs. C is wrong - normal vitals with clear lungs do not suggest tamponade.

q: Which findings suggest infective endocarditis that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: New heart murmur
Normal temperature with good energy
Fatigue
Fever and chills
Petechiae or Osler nodes
explain: Correct: D, A, E, C - fever, new murmur, embolic skin signs, and fatigue suggest endocarditis. B is wrong - normal vitals with energy do not suggest infection.

q: Which findings define HELLP syndrome that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Elevated liver enzymes
Low platelets
Right upper quadrant or epigastric pain
Hemolysis
Normal labs with mild swelling
explain: Correct: D, A, B, C - hemolysis, elevated LFTs, thrombocytopenia, and RUQ pain define HELLP. E is wrong - normal labs contradict HELLP.

q: Which actions are correct for umbilical cord prolapse? Select all that apply.
options: Relieving cord pressure with a gloved hand per protocol
Pushing the cord back into the uterus
Keeping the client from pushing the cord
Calling for help and notifying the RN immediately
Positioning knee-chest or Trendelenburg
explain: Correct: E, A, D, C - positioning, pressure relief, emergency notification, and preventing further cord handling are correct. B is wrong - the cord is never pushed back in.

q: Which findings suggest neonatal sepsis that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Irritability or seizures
Vigorous crying with good tone and feeding
Temperature instability
Poor feeding and lethargy
Apnea or respiratory distress
explain: Correct: C, D, E, A - temperature instability, poor feeding, apnea, and neuro changes are neonatal sepsis signs. B is wrong - vigorous feeding with good tone describes a well newborn.

q: Which findings suggest tracheoesophageal fistula in a newborn? Select all that apply.
options: Abdominal distention
Coughing and choking with feeds
Cyanosis during feeding
Excessive drooling
Quiet, comfortable feeding
explain: Correct: D, B, C, A - drooling, choking, cyanosis with feeds, and distention (air in stomach) suggest TEF. E is wrong - comfortable feeding contradicts TEF.

q: Which feeding strategies help a newborn with cleft palate? Select all that apply.
options: Feeding lying flat to speed up the process
Monitoring weight gain closely
Using special cleft bottles or nipples
Feeding slowly with frequent burping
Feeding in an upright position
explain: Correct: C, E, D, B - special bottles, upright slow feeding, burping, and weight monitoring manage cleft feeding. A is wrong - flat positioning risks aspiration.

q: The PN is caring for a client with a new prescription for a high-risk medication. Before the first dose, the PN should verify the order and also check:
options: Allergies, relevant labs, vital signs, and the client's understanding
Only the medication name, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
The client's favorite color, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
The pharmacy's phone number, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - high-risk medications need allergy, lab, vital sign, and understanding checks before the first dose. C is irrelevant. B is incomplete. D is not a client safety check.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A provider writes an order the PN believes is contraindicated for the client. After the provider insists, the PN should:
options: Administer it since the provider insisted, then follow up with the laboratory for the pending results
Have the UAP administer it, and verify the order against the medication administration record, at this stage
Alter the dose to make it safer, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
Refuse to administer, document the concern objectively, and escalate through the chain of command
explain: Correct: D - the PN never administers a believed-contraindicated order; refusal, documentation, and escalation are required. A is wrong - insistence does not make it safe. B is wrong - delegating does not remove accountability. C is wrong - the PN cannot rewrite orders.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is orienting a new UAP to the unit. The PN should explain that the UAP must:
options: Administer medications when nurses are busy, as documented in the plan of care
Report changes in client condition to the nurse promptly and never perform tasks beyond their role
Perform assessments independently, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Change care plans as needed, and verify the dosage calculation with another nurse
explain: Correct: B - UAPs report changes and stay within their role. C is wrong - assessment is a nursing function. A is wrong - UAPs do not administer medications. D is wrong - care plans are not changed by UAPs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client asks the PN about the risks of refusing a recommended surgery. The PN's best response is to:
options: Make the decision for the client, and verify the order against the medication administration record, on this occasion, for now
Tell the client surgery is always the right choice, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Encourage discussion with the provider, reinforce the provider's teaching, and report the client's concerns to the RN
Refuse to discuss it, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, within the scope of the practical nurse's role
explain: Correct: C - the PN facilitates informed decision-making and communicates concerns. A is wrong - decisions belong to the client. B is wrong - the PN does not direct the choice. D is wrong - the concern deserves a response.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN notices a spill on the unit floor. The PN should:
options: Cover it with a rug, before administering any further medication
Wait for housekeeping without warning anyone, before the end of the shift
Walk around it and leave it, while maintaining the patient's privacy and dignity
Clean it promptly or arrange for cleaning and warn others until it is safe
explain: Correct: D - immediate action or arranged cleanup with warnings prevents falls. C is wrong - leaving it endangers others. B is wrong - unwarned spills cause falls. A is wrong - rugs over spills create trip hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with limited vision needs medication teaching reinforced. The PN should:
options: Speak very quietly, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, at this stage, in full
Use large-print materials, verbal explanation, teach-back, and involve a trusted support person as the client wishes
Provide only written pamphlets, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
Skip the teaching, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion
explain: Correct: B - multimodal teaching adapted to vision loss ensures understanding. C is wrong - pamphlets alone are inaccessible. D is wrong - teaching cannot be skipped. A is wrong - quiet speech hinders hearing.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is asked to float to a unit with a higher acuity than the PN's experience. The PN should:
options: Perform advanced procedures to learn quickly, at the patient's bedside
Refuse to work entirely, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, in practice
Communicate limitations to the charge nurse and accept only appropriate assignments
Accept the sickest clients to prove competence, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - communicating limits allows safe assignment matching. D is wrong - overreaching endangers clients. B is wrong - refusal is unnecessary when safe assignments exist. A is wrong - learning advanced procedures on clients is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A family member is recording the PN without permission in a two-party consent state. The PN's best action is to:
options: Politely explain the concern, continue professional care, and report per facility policy
Stop all care until the phone is surrendered
Grab the phone, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Record the family member back, before administering any further medication
explain: Correct: A - calm professionalism with policy-based reporting is correct. C is wrong - grabbing property is inappropriate. B is wrong - care cannot be withheld. D is wrong - retaliation is unprofessional.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is documenting wound care. The most important details include:
options: Location, size, tissue type, drainage, odor, pain, and the client's response
A drawing without measurements, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
The PN's opinion of the wound, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Only the dressing type, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A - objective wound characteristics track healing or deterioration. C is wrong - opinions do not belong. D is incomplete. B lacks measurable data.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is anxious about an upcoming MRI. The PN's best action is to:
options: Cancel the MRI, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion
Explain what to expect in plain language, reinforce the RN's teaching, and report severe anxiety to the RN
Tell the client there is nothing to worry about, and wash hands before and after the procedure
Sedate the client without an order, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
explain: Correct: B - information reduces anxiety; severe cases are reported for possible intervention. C is wrong - dismissing anxiety is nontherapeutic. A is wrong - the PN does not cancel orders. D is wrong - sedation needs orders.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which delegation decisions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Delegating bathing of a stable client to the UAP
Delegating vital signs on a stable client to an experienced UAP
Delegating assessment of a new admission to the UAP
Delegating medication administration to the UAP
Delegating ambulation of a stable client to a competent UAP
explain: Correct: B, E, A - vitals, ambulation, and bathing for stable clients are delegable. C is wrong - assessment cannot be delegated. D is wrong - medication administration requires a licensed nurse.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions follow the PN's duty to report? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting a deteriorating client to the RN promptly
Keeping concerns to oneself to avoid conflict
Reporting suspected abuse per law
Reporting a malfunctioning device per policy
Reporting a near miss per policy
explain: Correct: A, D, C, E - deterioration, equipment, abuse, and near misses all trigger reporting duties. B is wrong - silence violates the duty to protect.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which are appropriate PN roles in client teaching? Select all that apply.
options: Reinforcing teaching the RN initiated
Using teach-back to verify understanding
Documenting teaching and the client's response
Providing initial teaching for complex new diagnoses
Adapting materials to the client's needs
explain: Correct: A, B, E, C - reinforcing, teach-back, adaptation, and documentation are PN teaching roles. D is wrong - initial complex teaching belongs to the RN.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which situations require incident reports? Select all that apply.
options: A client complimenting the food
Equipment malfunction affecting care
A client fall
A medication error
A near miss with no harm
explain: Correct: C, D, E, B - falls, errors, near misses, and equipment failures are all reportable safety events. A is wrong - compliments are not incidents.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which protect client privacy in electronic records? Select all that apply.
options: Viewing a celebrity client's chart out of curiosity
Logging off when leaving the workstation
Using strong passwords and not sharing them
Accessing only the records needed for assigned clients
Sharing login credentials with trusted colleagues
explain: Correct: B, C, D - logoff, password protection, and minimum-necessary access protect PHI. E is wrong - credential sharing is prohibited. A is wrong - curiosity access is a privacy violation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which are essential in a handoff for a client with diabetes? Select all that apply.
options: Recent glucose readings and trends
The client's favorite hobbies
Insulin or medication schedule
Meal intake
Signs of hypo- or hyperglycemia to watch for
explain: Correct: A, C, E, D - glucose trends, meds, warning signs, and intake ensure safe diabetes handoff. B is wrong - hobbies are irrelevant to the clinical handoff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN reinforces school bus safety. The teaching includes:
options: Stand in the road while waiting, and ensure the side rails are raised before leaving the room
Stick arms out the window, then report any change to the oncoming shift nurse
Run in front of the bus to board quickly, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, for now
Wait for the bus to stop fully, board in line, stay seated, and cross in front where the driver can see
explain: Correct: D - orderly boarding, seated riding, and visible crossing prevent bus injuries. C is wrong - running near buses is dangerous. A is wrong - waiting off the road is the rule. B is wrong - limbs stay inside.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces pedestrian safety for children. The teaching includes:
options: Run across busy streets, before the end of the shift, for now
Walk behind parked cars, for the duration of the patient's stay
Stop, look left-right-left, use crosswalks, and make eye contact with drivers
Cross streets without looking, based on the findings documented so far
explain: Correct: C - stop-look-crosswalk-eye contact is the safe crossing method. D is wrong - looking is essential. A is wrong - running reduces driver reaction time. B is wrong - parked cars hide children from drivers.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces skateboard and scooter safety. The teaching includes:
options: No helmet is needed for scooters, in accordance with facility policy
Riding in traffic to build skills, based on the findings documented so far
