Holding onto moving cars, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Helmet, wrist guards, and knee pads, riding in safe areas away from traffic
explain: Correct: D - protective gear and traffic-free areas prevent serious injuries. A is wrong - helmets are needed for both. B is wrong - traffic riding is dangerous. C is wrong - skitching causes severe injuries.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces sledding safety. The teaching includes:
options: Sit upright facing forward, sled in clear areas away from roads and trees, with adult supervision
Sled headfirst down steep hills, at the patient's bedside
Build jumps for excitement, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, on this occasion
Sled toward roads for a longer run, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A - upright, feet-first, clear runs, and supervision prevent sledding injuries. B is wrong - headfirst sledding risks head and spine injury. D is wrong - roads mean traffic danger. C is wrong - jumps cause crashes.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces hiking safety. The teaching includes:
options: Hike alone without telling anyone, then reassess the patient's respiratory status
Tell someone the plan, bring water and supplies, stay on trails, and watch the weather
Drink from any stream, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Ignore trail markers, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: B - communication, supplies, trails, and weather awareness keep hikers safe. A is wrong - solo unannounced hiking risks delayed rescue. C is wrong - stream water can carry pathogens. D is wrong - markers prevent getting lost.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces lab safety for a student. The teaching includes:
options: Tasting chemicals to identify them, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Mixing unknown chemicals for fun, at the patient's bedside
Wearing goggles, tying back hair, and knowing eyewash locations
Goggles are optional, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C - eye protection, hair control, and eyewash knowledge are lab safety basics. D is wrong - goggles are required. B is wrong - unknown mixtures can explode. A is wrong - tasting chemicals is never safe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces alcohol poisoning awareness for college students. The warning signs include:
options: Confusion, vomiting, slow or irregular breathing, and unresponsiveness, needing emergency help
Normal behavior after heavy drinking, then report any change to the oncoming shift nurse
Improved coordination, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Slight buzz, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A - these are alcohol poisoning signs requiring emergency care. B is wrong - heavy drinking is never risk-free. D understates the danger. C is the opposite of alcohol's effects.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which campfire safety points should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Clearing flammable material around the fire
Leaving fires smoldering overnight
Building fires under low tree branches
Fully extinguishing fires before leaving
Keeping fires small and attended
explain: Correct: E, A, D - small attended fires, cleared perimeters, and full extinguishing prevent wildfires. B is wrong - smoldering fires reignite. C is wrong - branches ignite easily.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces winter sports safety. The teaching includes:
options: Ignoring boundary signs, in accordance with facility policy
Helmet use, staying on marked trails, and skiing within ability
Skiing alone off-trail, during the current shift
No helmet for skiing, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B - helmets, marked trails, and ability-matched terrain prevent injuries. D is wrong - helmets are essential. C is wrong - solo off-trail skiing risks delayed rescue. A is wrong - boundaries mark hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces hunting safety. The teaching includes:
options: Wear camouflage only, before the end of the shift
Climb with a loaded gun, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Wear blaze orange, treat every gun as loaded, and know the target and beyond
Hunt alone without telling anyone, then report any change to the oncoming shift nurse
explain: Correct: C - visibility, muzzle discipline, and target awareness prevent hunting tragedies. A is wrong - orange is required for visibility. D is wrong - solo unannounced hunting delays rescue. B is wrong - climbing with a loaded gun risks accidental discharge.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces ice safety in winter. The teaching includes:
options: Cars can drive on any frozen lake, then reassess the patient's respiratory status
Ice thickness does not matter, before administering any further medication
All ice is safe to walk on, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment
Never go on unfamiliar ice; ice must be thick, tested, and supervised activities only
explain: Correct: D - unfamiliar ice is never trusted; thickness and supervision matter. C is wrong - thin ice drowns people yearly. A is wrong - vehicles need very thick, tested ice. B is wrong - thickness is the key safety factor.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which bicycle night safety measures should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Riding against traffic for better visibility
Wearing dark clothing to be stylish
Front white light and rear red reflector
Reflective clothing
Riding with traffic
explain: Correct: C, D, E - lights, reflectors, reflective gear, and with-traffic riding keep night cyclists visible and safe. B is wrong - dark clothing hides the rider. A is wrong - cyclists ride with traffic, not against it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces polio vaccine teaching. Which statement is correct?
options: Polio vaccine is part of routine childhood immunization and prevents paralytic polio
Polio was never serious, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Polio vaccine treats active polio, based on the findings documented so far
Only travelers need polio vaccine, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A - routine polio immunization prevents a crippling disease. B is wrong - polio paralyzed thousands. D is wrong - it is universal, not travel-only. C is wrong - vaccines prevent, not treat.

q: A parent asks what DTaP protects against. The PN reinforces:
options: Dengue, tuberculosis, and pneumonia
Diabetes, thyroid, and anemia
Diarrhea, typhoid, and parasites
Diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis
explain: Correct: D - DTaP covers diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis. The other options list unrelated conditions.

q: An adult asks how much aerobic exercise is recommended. The PN reinforces:
options: No exercise is needed, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Exercise once a month is enough, then evaluate the patient's response within the hour
About 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly, or 75 minutes vigorous, plus muscle strengthening
Only professional athletes need exercise, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - 150 moderate or 75 vigorous minutes weekly plus strengthening is the guideline. A is wrong - inactivity harms health. B is far too little. D is wrong - everyone benefits.

q: An adult asks about healthy sleep. The PN reinforces:
options: Sleep needs are identical for everyone
About 7-9 hours nightly for most adults
5 hours is plenty, on this occasion
12 hours is required, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: B - 7-9 hours supports adult health. C is insufficient for most. D is excessive for most adults. A is wrong - needs vary.

q: A parent asks about time-out for a 4-year-old. The PN reinforces that time-out should be:
options: Brief (about a minute per year of age), calm, and followed by reconnection
Done in a scary isolated place, at the patient's bedside
Accompanied by yelling, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Last for hours, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - brief, calm time-outs with reconnection teach without traumatizing. D is wrong - hours are excessive. B is wrong - frightening isolation harms. C is wrong - yelling undermines the lesson.

q: The PN reinforces positive discipline. The most effective approach the PN should emphasize is:
options: Harsh punishment for every mistake, at the patient's bedside
Praising desired behaviors specifically and consistently
Comparing the child negatively to siblings
Ignoring all behavior, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B - specific consistent praise shapes behavior positively. A is wrong - harsh punishment harms. D is wrong - ignoring everything teaches nothing. C is wrong - comparisons damage self-esteem.

q: Which are expected milestones for a 9-month-old? Select all that apply.
options: Stranger anxiety
Writing their name
Riding a bicycle
Pulling to stand
Pincer grasp
explain: Correct: E, A, D - pincer grasp, stranger anxiety, and pulling to stand are 9-month milestones. B and C are years away.

q: Which are expected language milestones for a 2-year-old? Select all that apply.
options: Speaking in complex sentences
Having a vocabulary of 50 or more words
Following simple instructions
Using two-word phrases
Using several thousand words
explain: Correct: D, B, C - two-word phrases, growing vocabulary, and following directions are 2-year-old milestones. A is wrong - complex sentences come later. E is wrong - thousands of words come in later childhood.

q: A client consciously decides not to think about an upcoming surgery until the day before. This is an example of:
options: Denial, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Projection, at the patient's bedside
Repression, as documented in the plan of care
Suppression, a conscious coping choice
explain: Correct: D - suppression is the conscious, deliberate postponement of attention. C is wrong - repression is unconscious. A is wrong - the surgery is acknowledged, not denied. B is wrong - nothing is attributed to others.

q: A client who lost a child volunteers with grieving parents. The PN recognizes this as:
options: Projection, for now
Regression, at this stage
Altruism, a mature defense mechanism
Denial, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C - altruism channels personal pain into helping others. D is wrong - the loss is acknowledged. A is wrong - feelings are not attributed to others. B is wrong - there is no return to earlier behavior.

q: A client with bipolar disorder is now sleeping 14 hours daily, withdrawn, and hopeless. The PN should:
options: Reduce monitoring since the client is quiet, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Encourage the client to cheer up, as documented in the plan of care
Assume the mania is cured, without first verifying the patient's identity at the bedside
Report to the RN; the depressive phase of bipolar disorder carries suicide risk and needs evaluation
explain: Correct: D - bipolar depression needs assessment and suicide precautions. C is wrong - the illness cycles; depression is part of it. B is wrong - 'cheer up' is nontherapeutic. A is wrong - withdrawn depressed clients need closer monitoring, not less.

q: A client hoards newspapers until the room is unsafe. The PN's best action is to:
options: Shame the client into cleaning, while keeping the head of the bed elevated as tolerated
Ignore the fire hazard, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, on this occasion
Report the safety hazard to the RN, work with the team on a gradual plan, and ensure fire and fall safety
Throw everything away while the client is out, then teach the patient how to perform the procedure at home
explain: Correct: C - safety hazards are reported and addressed through a therapeutic team plan. D is wrong - discarding belongings without consent violates trust. B is wrong - fire hazards cannot be ignored. A is wrong - shaming worsens hoarding.

q: A client is struggling to adjust after a job loss. The PN recognizes this as possibly:
options: A character flaw, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
An adjustment disorder, a stress-related response needing supportive listening and RN notification
Schizophrenia, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, on this occasion, for now
Malingering, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B - disproportionate stress responses to life changes fit adjustment disorders; support and referral help. C is wrong - there is no psychosis. A is wrong - it is not a character flaw. D is wrong - distress is genuine, not faked.

q: Which de-escalation techniques should the PN use with an agitated client? Select all that apply.
options: Speaking calmly with a nonthreatening posture
Crowding the client with multiple staff immediately
Listening to the client's concerns
Giving the client space
Offering choices to restore control
explain: Correct: A, D, E, C - calm voice, space, choices, and listening defuse agitation. B is wrong - crowding escalates aggression; staff presence is staged as needed.

q: Which actions support the family of a client with mental illness? Select all that apply.
options: Providing information about the illness and treatment
Connecting the family with support resources
Listening to the family's concerns
Encouraging the family's involvement as the client wishes
Blaming the family for the illness
explain: Correct: A, B, D, C - education, resources, involvement, and listening support families. E is wrong - blame is harmful and inaccurate.

q: Which are therapeutic responses to a client expressing anger? Select all that apply.
options: Maintaining safety for everyone
Exploring the source: 'Tell me what happened'
Acknowledging the feeling: 'You seem angry'
Setting limits on aggressive behavior
Telling the client anger is wrong
explain: Correct: C, B, D, A - validation, exploration, limit-setting, and safety are therapeutic. E is wrong - judging anger as wrong shuts down communication.

q: The PN is helping a client with adaptive utensils. The PN's role is to:
options: Encourage use of the utensils as the occupational therapist taught, allowing independence
Do everything for the client and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response
Feed the client to save time, and verify the order against the medication administration record, for now
Remove the utensils as too complicated, and verify the dosage calculation with another nurse
explain: Correct: A - reinforcing OT-taught adaptive equipment builds independence. C is wrong - feeding fosters dependence. D is wrong - removing tools harms function. B is wrong - doing everything reverses progress.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is positioning a client for meals. The correct position is:
options: Flat in bed, on this occasion
Upright at 90 degrees as tolerated
Trendelenburg, at this stage, for now
On the stomach, going forward
explain: Correct: B - upright positioning prevents aspiration during meals. A is wrong - flat eating risks aspiration. C and D are inappropriate for meals.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assisting a client to stand from a chair. The correct technique includes:
options: Having the client scoot forward, feet flat, lean forward, and push up using armrests with the PN guarding
Lifting under the armpits quickly, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, for now
Pulling the client up by the arms and hand off the information to the oncoming nurse
Tipping the chair backward, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A - forward scoot, flat feet, nose-over-toes lean, and armrest push with guarding is safe. C is wrong - arm pulling injures shoulders. B is wrong - armpit lifting is unsafe. D is wrong - tipping chairs causes falls.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client is dying and the family asks how to provide comfort. The PN can reinforce:
options: Force fluids and food, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Leave the client alone, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Gentle presence, moistening lips, repositioning for comfort, and quiet environment per the care plan
Keep the room bright and noisy, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C - presence, mouth care, positioning, and calm environment comfort the dying. B is wrong - abandonment is not comfort. A is wrong - forcing intake causes distress. D is wrong - stimulation disturbs rest.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which comfort measures are appropriate at the end of life? Select all that apply.
options: Insisting the client eat full meals
Managing pain per the plan and reporting changes
Moistening the mouth and lips
Repositioning for comfort
Keeping the environment calm and quiet
explain: Correct: D, C, E, B - positioning, mouth care, calm environment, and pain management are end-of-life comfort essentials. A is wrong - forcing food causes suffering.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client in a wheelchair is at risk for pressure injuries. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Sit still all day to avoid friction, in accordance with facility policy
Slide across surfaces for transfers, based on the findings documented so far
Avoid all movement, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Shift weight every 15-30 minutes and use pressure-relieving cushions as recommended
explain: Correct: D - regular weight shifts and cushions prevent ischial pressure injuries. A is wrong - immobility causes breakdown. B is wrong - sliding causes shear. C is wrong - movement is protective.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A post-op client reports painful gas. The PN can reinforce:
options: Staying in bed without moving, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment
Walking as ordered, avoiding straws and carbonated drinks, and reporting severe distention
Taking laxatives without an order, before the end of the shift
Eating large gas-producing meals, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: B - ambulation moves gas; straws and carbonation add air; severe distention is reported. A is wrong - immobility worsens gas. C is wrong - laxatives need orders. D is wrong - gas-producing foods worsen discomfort.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help prevent contractures in an immobile client? Select all that apply.
options: Proper positioning with support devices
Foot boots or splints as ordered
Encouraging active movement as tolerated
Range-of-motion exercises as ordered
Keeping joints immobile in one position
explain: Correct: D, A, C, B - ROM, positioning, activity, and splints prevent contractures. E is wrong - prolonged immobility causes contractures.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures promote venous return in the legs? Select all that apply.
options: Avoiding crossing the legs
Wearing anti-embolism stockings as ordered
Elevating the legs periodically
Standing still for long periods
Ankle pumps and leg exercises
explain: Correct: E, A, C, B - exercises, uncrossed legs, elevation, and stockings all promote venous return. D is wrong - prolonged standing pools blood in the legs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which hygiene measures are important for a client with a urinary catheter? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping the catheter secured to prevent pulling
Maintaining a closed drainage system
Daily perineal cleansing
Disconnecting the bag daily for cleaning
Keeping the drainage bag below bladder level
explain: Correct: C, E, B, A - hygiene, gravity drainage, closed systems, and securement prevent CAUTI. D is wrong - disconnection breaks the closed system and invites infection.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client takes niacin for cholesterol. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Take extra doses to lower cholesterol faster, then report the outcome to the registered nurse
Stop it at the first flush and verify the result with a second measurement
Expect flushing and itching; taking it with food and avoiding alcohol can help, and severe symptoms should be reported
Take it on an empty stomach for best effect, before checking the patient's allergy status for the medication
explain: Correct: C - flushing is expected; food and alcohol avoidance minimize it. D is wrong - empty stomach worsens flushing. B is wrong - mild flushing is managed, not a reason to stop without direction. A is wrong - extra doses increase harm.

q: A client takes cholestyramine. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Mix it with fluids as directed and take other medications at different times, since it binds drugs
Swallow the dry powder, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Expect immediate cholesterol lowering, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Take it with no fluids, and wash hands before and after the procedure
explain: Correct: A - the powder must be mixed with fluids, and separation from other drugs preserves their absorption. B is wrong - dry powder risks esophageal obstruction. D is wrong - fluids are required. C is wrong - effect takes weeks.

q: A client takes finasteride. The PN reinforces which safety point?
options: It works immediately, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
It is safe for everyone to handle, and assess the patient's understanding of the teaching provided
Women should take it for hair loss without direction, during the current shift
Pregnant women should not handle broken or crushed tablets due to risk to a male fetus
explain: Correct: D - finasteride can cause genital abnormalities in male fetuses; handling precautions matter. B is wrong - handling restrictions exist. A is wrong - effect takes months. C is wrong - use in women needs provider direction.

q: A client takes allopurinol for gout. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Take it only when joints hurt, for now
Drink plenty of fluids and report rash, fever, or decreased urine
Restrict all fluids, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Stop it during a flare without direction
explain: Correct: B - hydration prevents kidney stones; rash or fever may signal hypersensitivity. C is wrong - fluids are protective. D is wrong - stopping needs direction. A is wrong - allopurinol is daily prevention, not as-needed.

q: A client takes colchicine for gout flares. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Share it with family members, before administering any further medication
Continue it despite severe diarrhea, with the patient's safety as the stated priority
Double the dose for faster relief, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Report severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or muscle weakness, since these suggest toxicity
explain: Correct: D - GI symptoms and weakness signal colchicine toxicity needing evaluation. B is wrong - severe diarrhea needs reporting. C is wrong - extra doses cause toxicity. A is wrong - prescriptions are never shared.

q: The order is for 0.25 g of a medication; available: 125 mg tablets. How many tablets should the PN give?
options: 2 tablets
0.5 tablet
4 tablets
1 tablet
explain: Correct: A - 0.25 g = 250 mg; 250 divided by 125 = 2 tablets. B gives 62.5 mg. D gives 125 mg. C gives 500 mg.

q: An IV of 1000 mL is ordered over 10 hours. What is the rate in mL/hr?
options: 200 mL/hr
150 mL/hr
100 mL/hr
50 mL/hr
explain: Correct: C - 1000 mL divided by 10 hours = 100 mL/hr. D, B, and A reflect arithmetic errors.

q: A child weighs 20 kg. The order is for a single dose of 5 mg/kg. How much should the PN give?
options: 50 mg
200 mg
100 mg
25 mg
explain: Correct: C - 20 kg x 5 mg/kg = 100 mg. D, A, and B reflect calculation errors.

q: The PN is reinforcing allopurinol teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Take it as prescribed, even between flares
Report rash, fever, or painful urination
Avoid excessive alcohol
Drink plenty of fluids daily
Stop it abruptly once feeling better
explain: Correct: D, B, A, C - hydration, hypersensitivity surveillance, adherence, and alcohol limits are allopurinol essentials. E is wrong - stopping without direction invites flares.

q: Which drugs commonly cause orthostatic hypotension that the PN should monitor for? Select all that apply.
options: Topical moisturizers
Daily multivitamins
Tricyclic antidepressants
High-dose diuretics
Alpha blockers such as tamsulosin
explain: Correct: E, D, C - alpha blockers, diuretics, and TCAs all lower standing blood pressure. A and B do not cause orthostatic hypotension.

q: Which anticholinergic effects should the PN monitor for and report? Select all that apply.
options: Dry mouth and constipation
Blurred vision
Confusion in older adults
Increased sweating
Urinary retention
explain: Correct: E, A, B, C - 'can't pee, can't spit, can't see, can't think' captures anticholinergic effects. D is wrong - decreased sweating, not increased, occurs.

q: The PN is reinforcing cholesterol management teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Stopping medication once cholesterol improves without direction
Taking prescribed medications consistently
Reporting muscle pain or dark urine with statins
Following a heart-healthy diet low in saturated fat
Exercising as recommended
explain: Correct: D, E, B, C - diet, exercise, adherence, and statin warning signs are the management pillars. A is wrong - stopping without direction allows rebound.

q: Before IV contrast, a client reports a shellfish allergy. The PN should:
options: Proceed since shellfish allergy is unrelated, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time
Report the allergy history to the RN; prior allergic history is screened before contrast administration
Cancel the scan independently, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Give contrast without mentioning it and continue to monitor the patient closely for changes
explain: Correct: B - allergy history is part of pre-contrast screening; the team decides on premedication or alternatives. A is wrong - the history must be communicated regardless. C is wrong - the PN does not cancel orders. D is wrong - silence risks reaction.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A pre-op client is ordered a bowel prep. The PN's responsibilities include:
options: Telling the client the prep is optional, and verify the order against the medication administration record, for now
Giving extra doses for better cleaning, before the end of the shift
Skipping the prep to save time and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, on this occasion
Administering the prep as ordered, monitoring tolerance and output, and reporting concerns to the RN
explain: Correct: D - ordered preps are given with monitoring and reporting. C is wrong - skipping compromises surgery. B is wrong - extra doses cause electrolyte harm. A is wrong - the prep is required, not optional.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client reports uncontrolled bleeding from a wound despite pressure. The PN should:
options: Maintain direct pressure, call for help, notify the RN immediately, and prepare for emergency orders
Remove the dressing to check, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
Wait for the bleeding to stop on its own, while keeping the patient safe from injury at all times
Apply a tourniquet immediately without assessment, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: A - direct pressure with emergency notification is the hemorrhage response. D is wrong - tourniquets are a last resort for limb hemorrhage per protocol. B is wrong - removing dressings disrupts clotting. C is wrong - waiting risks exsanguination.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a client fall, the PN's neuro checks should monitor for:
options: Nothing; falls never cause head injury, as part of the routine care for this patient
Improved appetite, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
The client's mood only, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Level of consciousness, pupils, vital signs, and signs of bleeding, reporting changes to the RN
explain: Correct: D - post-fall neuro checks watch for intracranial injury. B is irrelevant. C is incomplete. A is dangerously false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client's family reports the client seems more confused after starting a new medication. The PN should:
options: Document the change, review the medication list, and report to the RN promptly
Tell the family confusion is expected, at the patient's bedside
Increase the dose to overcome the confusion
Stop the medication independently, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A - new confusion may be a drug effect needing provider review. B is wrong - it needs evaluation, not dismissal. D is wrong - the PN does not stop drugs independently. C is wrong - more drug worsens the problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which screening questions are important before IV contrast? Select all that apply.
options: Allergies, especially to medications
History of prior contrast reaction
Kidney problems
Use of metformin
Favorite foods
explain: Correct: B, C, A, D - prior reactions, renal function, allergies, and metformin use all affect contrast safety. E is irrelevant.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which assessments follow a client fall? Select all that apply.
options: Reviewing what happened and the environment
Blaming the client for the fall
Assessing for injury including head, neck, and limbs
Checking level of consciousness
Taking vital signs
explain: Correct: D, C, E, A - neuro status, injury survey, vitals, and event review are the post-fall assessments. B is wrong - blame has no place in fall evaluation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which pre-op GI preparations might the PN carry out or reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Bowel prep as ordered
Antiembolism stockings as ordered
Encouraging a large meal before surgery
NPO as ordered
Removing dentures before anesthesia
explain: Correct: D, A, E, B - NPO, bowel prep, denture removal, and stockings are standard pre-op measures. C is wrong - pre-op clients do not eat large meals.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before wheeling a client to a procedure, the PN verifies identity using two identifiers and checks the consent. This prevents:
options: Family visits, on this occasion
Wrong-client or wrong-procedure errors
Paperwork, in this case
Delays, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - identity verification with consent checks is the final guard against wrong-client/procedure errors. D is wrong - safety checks are worth the time. C and A are irrelevant.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: The surgical count comes up incorrect. The PN's role is to:
options: Document the count as correct, and verify the dosage calculation with another nurse
Finish closing quickly, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Report the discrepancy immediately per policy and assist as directed; retained items are a never event
Ignore it; counts are often wrong, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, for now
explain: Correct: C - count discrepancies stop closure until resolved; the PN reports and assists. D is wrong - discrepancies are never ignored. B is wrong - rushing risks retained items. A is wrong - false documentation is fraud.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with heart failure develops increasing dyspnea with diminished breath sounds at the bases. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Normal heart failure, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Asthma, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Pleural effusion, which should be reported to the RN
Pneumonia only, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C - fluid in the pleural space dampens breath sounds and worsens dyspnea in heart failure. D is wrong - infection is not the only cause. A is wrong - worsening dyspnea is never 'normal.' B is wrong - asthma wheezes rather than silences.

q: A client with pneumonia is not improving and develops severe dyspnea with refractory hypoxemia. The PN should:
options: Encourage the client to breathe faster, for the duration of the patient's stay
Give oxygen without reporting, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Continue routine care, on this occasion, for now
Report to the RN immediately; worsening hypoxemia despite treatment may signal ARDS
explain: Correct: D - ARDS is a life-threatening complication needing urgent escalation. C is wrong - routine care is insufficient. A is wrong - faster breathing does not fix shunt. B is wrong - the RN must be notified.

q: After chest trauma, the PN notes a flail segment moving paradoxically with breathing. The PN should:
options: Push on the segment to stabilize it, and assess the patient's pain level before and after
Keep the client still, support breathing, notify the RN immediately, and prepare for emergency orders
Document it for the next shift, in accordance with facility policy
Encourage deep breathing exercises, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
explain: Correct: B - flail chest impairs ventilation and needs urgent management. A is wrong - pushing on fractured ribs causes harm. D is wrong - exercises are inappropriate acutely. C is wrong - waiting is unsafe.

q: A client with pericarditis reports sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing and improves sitting forward. The PN should:
options: Report to the RN; positional pleuritic chest pain suggests pericarditis needing evaluation
Give antacids without an order and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response
Tell the client it is indigestion, as documented in the plan of care
Encourage lying flat, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A - the positional pattern is classic pericarditis. C is wrong - dismissing chest pain is unsafe. D is wrong - lying flat worsens pericardial pain. B is wrong - medicating without orders exceeds scope.

q: A client with dilated cardiomyopathy reports increasing fatigue, edema, and dyspnea. The PN should:
options: Document the worsening symptoms and report to the RN; they suggest heart failure progression
Encourage strenuous exercise, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Reassure the client this is expected and needs no report, at the patient's bedside, for now
Tell the client to double the diuretic, and verify the order against the medication administration record
explain: Correct: A - worsening HF symptoms need provider reassessment. C is wrong - progression needs evaluation. B is wrong - strenuous exercise is unsafe. D is wrong - dose changes need orders.

q: A client's blood pressure is 220/130 mmHg with chest pain and confusion. The PN should:
options: Recheck in an hour, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Recognize hypertensive emergency and notify the RN immediately
Give the home antihypertensive without an order
Encourage the client to relax and wait, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - severe hypertension with organ-damage signs (chest pain, confusion) is an emergency. A is wrong - waiting risks stroke or MI. C is wrong - medicating without orders exceeds scope. D is wrong - relaxation does not treat hypertensive emergency.

q: A laboring client with ruptured membranes develops fever, maternal and fetal tachycardia, and foul-smelling fluid. The PN should:
options: Encourage the client to push harder, using the equipment available at the bedside
Offer oral fluids and wait, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, for now
Document it as normal labor, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Report to the RN immediately; these suggest chorioamnionitis needing urgent treatment
explain: Correct: D - chorioamnionitis threatens mother and fetus and needs prompt antibiotics and delivery planning. C is wrong - fever with foul fluid is not normal. A is wrong - pushing does not treat infection. B is wrong - waiting risks sepsis.

q: After cesarean birth, a client's incision becomes increasingly red, swollen, and painful with fever. The PN should:
options: Reassure her it is normal healing, before the end of the shift
Apply heat without an order, during the current shift
Report to the RN promptly; these suggest wound infection
Remove the staples at the bedside, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - spreading erythema with fever after cesarean signals surgical site infection. A is wrong - these are not normal healing. D is wrong - staple removal needs orders. B is wrong - heat needs direction and does not treat infection.

q: A breastfeeding mother on day 3 has painfully engorged breasts. The PN reinforces that she should:
options: Feed frequently, use warm compresses before feeding and cold after, and report fever or unrelieved pain
Bind the breasts tightly, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, in full
Avoid all fluids, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion, in practice
Stop breastfeeding, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for now
explain: Correct: A - frequent emptying with warm/cold measures relieves engorgement. D is wrong - stopping worsens engorgement. B is wrong - binding is outdated and harmful. C is wrong - fluids are still needed.

q: A breastfeeding mother reports a painful lump in one breast without fever. The PN reinforces that she should:
options: Ignore it, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Continue breastfeeding, apply warm compresses, massage gently toward the nipple, and report worsening pain, redness, or fever
Apply ice only and never feed, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, for now
Stop feeding from that breast permanently, while observing standard isolation precautions for the unit
explain: Correct: B - plugged ducts resolve with continued emptying, warmth, and monitoring for mastitis. D is wrong - stopping worsens plugging. C is wrong - feeding must continue. A is wrong - ignoring risks mastitis.

q: A woman 2 weeks postpartum develops severe dyspnea, edema, and fatigue. The PN should:
options: Encourage her to exercise vigorously, and evaluate whether the patient's goals were met
Tell her postpartum fatigue is normal, then notify the provider of any abnormal findings
Report to the RN promptly; these suggest peripartum cardiomyopathy, a medical emergency
Advise waiting a month, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: C - peripartum cardiomyopathy causes heart failure around delivery and needs urgent care. B is wrong - severe dyspnea is not normal fatigue. A is wrong - exertion is dangerous. D is wrong - waiting risks death.

q: A postpartum client with hemorrhage develops oozing from IV sites and petechiae. The PN should:
options: Encourage ambulation, at the patient's bedside
Document it as normal, before the end of the shift
Apply more bandages and wait, during the current shift, for now
Report to the RN immediately; oozing with hemorrhage suggests DIC
explain: Correct: D - DIC causes simultaneous clotting and bleeding; oozing from puncture sites is a hallmark. B is wrong - this is not normal. C is wrong - bandages do not treat DIC. A is wrong - ambulation is unsafe.

q: A client with vasa previa is in labor. The PN understands the greatest danger is:
options: Mild bleeding, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Maternal discomfort, as documented in the plan of care
Fetal vessel rupture causing rapid fetal hemorrhage, needing emergency delivery
Slow labor, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
explain: Correct: C - unprotected fetal vessels over the cervix can rupture with membrane rupture, exsanguinating the fetus. A understates the catastrophe. B and D miss the fetal emergency.

q: Labor has not progressed for hours with adequate contractions. The PN should:
options: Perform a vaginal exam to speed labor, and verify the order against the medication administration record
Continue support, monitor maternal and fetal status closely, and report lack of progress to the RN
Encourage the client to push continuously without rest and hand off the information to the oncoming nurse
Tell the client failure is imminent, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
explain: Correct: B - prolonged labor needs close monitoring and provider evaluation for interventions. C is wrong - exhausting the mother harms both. A is wrong - exams do not speed labor and increase infection risk. D is wrong - negative predictions are nontherapeutic.

q: The PN notes the umbilical cord wrapped around the newborn's neck at delivery. The PN's role is to:
options: Report the finding to the RN/provider immediately and assist as directed
Pull the cord forcefully, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Ignore it, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Cut the cord without direction, and record the intake and output for the shift
explain: Correct: A - nuchal cord needs provider management; the PN reports and assists. B is wrong - forceful pulling injures the baby. D is wrong - cutting needs direction. C is wrong - it needs assessment.

q: Which findings suggest pleural effusion that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Dullness to percussion
Dyspnea
Diminished breath sounds over the affected area
Wheezing that clears with coughing
Pleuritic chest pain
explain: Correct: B, C, A, E - dyspnea, diminished sounds, dullness, and pleuritic pain suggest effusion. D is wrong - wheezing that clears suggests mucus, not effusion.

q: Which findings suggest ARDS that the PN must report at once? Select all that apply.
options: Severe dyspnea with rapid onset
Bilateral lung infiltrates
Refractory hypoxemia despite oxygen
Tachypnea and tachycardia
Gradual improvement with rest
explain: Correct: A, C, B, D - rapid severe dyspnea, refractory hypoxemia, bilateral infiltrates, and compensatory vitals define ARDS. E is wrong - ARDS worsens without intervention.

q: Which findings are consistent with pericarditis? Select all that apply.
options: Pericardial friction rub
Sharp chest pain worse with inspiration
Crushing pressure-like pain radiating to the jaw
Pain improved by sitting forward
Fever
explain: Correct: B, D, A, E - pleuritic positional pain, friction rub, and fever fit pericarditis. C is wrong - crushing pressure with jaw radiation suggests MI, not pericarditis.

q: Which findings suggest chorioamnionitis that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Maternal and fetal tachycardia
Uterine tenderness
Foul-smelling amniotic fluid
Clear fluid with normal vital signs
Maternal fever
explain: Correct: E, A, C, B - fever, tachycardias, foul fluid, and tenderness are chorioamnionitis signs. D is wrong - normal findings do not suggest infection.

q: Which findings suggest DIC that the PN must report immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Normal coagulation labs
Dropping platelet and fibrinogen levels
Petechiae and ecchymoses
Bleeding with clotting at the same time
Oozing from IV and puncture sites
explain: Correct: E, C, B, D - simultaneous bleeding and clotting with consumed factors define DIC. A is wrong - normal labs contradict DIC.

q: Which findings help distinguish mastitis from simple engorgement? Select all that apply.
options: Localized red, hot, painful breast area
Fever and chills
Wedge-shaped redness
Bilateral fullness that improves with feeding
Flu-like body aches
explain: Correct: B, A, E, C - fever, localized erythema, systemic symptoms, and wedge redness indicate mastitis. D is wrong - bilateral fullness improving with feeding describes engorgement, not mastitis.

q: Which findings suggest peripartum cardiomyopathy that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Severe dyspnea and orthopnea
Mild tiredness that resolves with rest
Tachycardia
Peripheral edema
Fatigue disproportionate to new motherhood
explain: Correct: A, D, E, C - dyspnea, edema, profound fatigue, and tachycardia in the peripartum period suggest cardiomyopathy. B is wrong - rest-relieved mild tiredness is normal postpartum.

q: The PN has four clients: one with chest pain, one requesting discharge papers, one with a bruise, and one asking for a blanket. The PN's priority is the client with:
options: The discharge request, for now
The bruise, in accordance with facility policy
The blanket request, on this occasion
Chest pain, reported to the RN immediately
explain: Correct: D - chest pain is potentially life-threatening and comes first. The others are routine needs addressed afterward.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client with an epidural for pain control reports numb legs and the PN notes decreased movement. The PN should:
options: Encourage the client to walk and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response
Report to the RN immediately; neuro changes with an epidural need urgent evaluation
Remove the epidural catheter, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Reassure the client this is normal and do nothing, and record the intake and output for the shift
explain: Correct: B - new neuro deficits with an epidural may signal hematoma or abscess; urgent reporting is required. D is wrong - it needs evaluation. C is wrong - the PN does not remove epidural catheters. A is wrong - walking with deficits is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is texting a photo of a wound to the provider for consultation. The correct practice is to:
options: Use only approved secure communication per policy, with client consent and no identifying information beyond what is needed
Use a personal phone and send it casually, and verify the order against the medication administration record, on this occasion
Text it to anyone available, and assess the patient's understanding of the teaching provided
Post it on social media for opinions, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, at this stage
explain: Correct: A - secure approved channels with consent protect privacy. B is wrong - personal phones breach security. D is wrong - social media posting violates confidentiality. C is wrong - only the care team receives clinical images.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A Jehovah's Witness client needs surgery. The PN's best advocacy includes:
options: Promising no blood will ever be needed, before checking the patient's allergy status for the medication
Telling the client the beliefs are wrong, and record the intake and output for the shift
Ignoring the belief system, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, as documented in the plan of care
Ensuring the team knows the client's wishes about blood products, documenting, and reporting concerns to the RN
explain: Correct: D - communicating and documenting the client's wishes respects autonomy. C is wrong - beliefs cannot be ignored. A is wrong - promises cannot be made. B is wrong - judging beliefs is inappropriate.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client asks the PN to explain the difference between a will and advance directives. The PN's best response is to:
options: Draft both documents, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Refuse to answer, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Explain generally that advance directives guide health care decisions while wills address property, and refer legal questions to appropriate resources
Tell the client they are the same, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, since the same approach was used during the previous shift
explain: Correct: C - general information with referral respects the PN's role without practicing law. A is wrong - the PN does not draft legal documents. B is wrong - the question deserves an answer. D is wrong - they are different documents.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: During a code, the family asks to be present. The PN's best action is to:
options: Stop the code, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, in accordance with facility policy
Forcibly remove the family, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, in this case
Ignore the family completely, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Follow facility policy, which often supports a staff member staying with the family, while the team continues resuscitation
explain: Correct: D - many facilities support family presence with a designated support person; policy guides the response. B is wrong - force is inappropriate. A is wrong - the code continues. C is wrong - the family needs communication.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN believes a client's care raises ethical concerns. The PN's best step is to:
options: Discuss with the RN and request an ethics consultation per facility policy
Decide the ethical answer alone, as part of the routine care for this patient
Ignore the concern, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Tell the client to sue, with the patient's safety as the stated priority
explain: Correct: A - ethics concerns go through the RN and formal consultation processes. C is wrong - ethical concerns deserve attention. B is wrong - ethics decisions are team-based. D is wrong - suggesting lawsuits is inappropriate.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is receiving a new graduate PN for orientation. The PN should:
options: Ignore the orientee, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Model safe practice within scope, provide guidance, and report concerns to the preceptor or manager
Have the orientee do all the work, before administering any further medication
Let the orientee practice beyond scope to learn faster
explain: Correct: B - orientation models safe, in-scope practice with support and feedback. D is wrong - beyond-scope practice endangers clients. A is wrong - orientees need guidance. C is wrong - dumping work is not orientation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is being transferred to the ICU. The PN's handoff should emphasize:
options: The PN's opinions about the ICU, at the patient's bedside
The client's hobbies, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Current instability, recent changes, pending tests, drips, and safety concerns
Old history only, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C - ICU handoff centers on instability, changes, pending items, and safety. B is irrelevant. A is unprofessional. D is incomplete without current status.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which PN actions are appropriate when a provider is unresponsive to pages about a deteriorating client? Select all that apply.
options: Continuing to monitor the client closely
Escalating through the chain of command
Notifying the charge RN or supervisor
Waiting silently for the provider to call back
Documenting the pages and responses objectively
explain: Correct: A, B, E, C - monitoring, escalation, documentation, and supervisor notification protect the client. D is wrong - silent waiting during deterioration is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which are within the PN's role when witnessing consent? Select all that apply.
options: Signing as witness after proper consent
Ensuring the form is complete
Answering the client's detailed medical questions about risks
Confirming the client appears to sign voluntarily
Confirming the provider explained the procedure
explain: Correct: D, E, A, B - voluntariness, explanation confirmation, witnessing, and completeness are the witness role. C is wrong - detailed risk questions go to the provider.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions support safe medication administration? Select all that apply.
options: Verifying allergies before each administration
Checking the order for clarity and completeness
Administering medications prepared by another nurse without checking
Monitoring for therapeutic and adverse effects
Reporting errors or adverse reactions promptly
explain: Correct: A, B, D, E - allergy checks, order verification, monitoring, and prompt reporting are safety pillars. C is wrong - every nurse verifies personally.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which statements about the PN's scope are true? Select all that apply.
options: The PN prescribes medications
The PN collects data and reports changes
The PN performs basic procedures within competence
The PN reinforces teaching initiated by the RN
The PN independently diagnoses medical conditions
explain: Correct: B, D, C - data collection, teaching reinforcement, and basic procedures define PN scope. E is wrong - diagnosis belongs to providers. A is wrong - prescribing belongs to authorized providers.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which handoff practices improve safety? Select all that apply.
options: Providing handoff in a private area
Rushing through handoff to save time
Including recent changes and pending items
Verifying the receiver understands
Using a standardized format like SBAR
explain: Correct: E, C, D, A - standardization, completeness, verification, and privacy make handoffs safe. B is wrong - rushing causes errors.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is discharged with activity restrictions. The PN should ensure the teaching covers: Select all that apply.
options: That restrictions never matter
Signs to report, such as increased pain or bleeding
Who to call with questions
When to follow up with the provider
What activities are restricted and for how long
explain: Correct: E, B, D, C - restriction details, warning signs, follow-up, and contacts are discharge essentials. A is wrong - restrictions protect healing and must be followed.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which are appropriate goals-of-care discussion supports by the PN? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting the client's statements to the RN/provider
Making the goals-of-care decision for the client
Listening to the client's values and wishes
Encouraging family discussion as the client wishes
Providing information about palliative options
explain: Correct: C, A, E, D - listening, reporting, informing, and facilitating family discussion support goals-of-care work. B is wrong - decisions belong to the client/surrogate with the team.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN reinforces drowsy driving prevention. The teaching includes:
options: Loud music cures drowsiness, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, in this case
Opening windows guarantees alertness, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Drive even when very sleepy, before administering any further medication
Pull over and rest when drowsy, avoid driving after sedating medications, and get adequate sleep
explain: Correct: D - rest stops, medication awareness, and adequate sleep prevent drowsy-driving crashes. C is wrong - drowsy driving kills. A is wrong - music does not cure sleepiness. B is wrong - cold air is not a substitute for sleep.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces motorcycle helmet safety. The teaching includes:
options: Always wearing a DOT-approved helmet, which reduces head injury and death
Helmets increase injury risk, at the patient's bedside
Helmets are optional for experienced riders
Only passengers need helmets, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A - approved helmets are the single most effective motorcycle safety measure. C is wrong - experience does not prevent crashes. B is wrong - helmets reduce injury. D is wrong - riders need them most.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces pedestrian night safety. The teaching includes:
options: Walk in the road facing away from traffic, during the current shift
Wear reflective clothing, carry a light, and use sidewalks and crosswalks
Wear dark clothing at night, in accordance with facility policy
Assume drivers can always see you, and record the intake and output for the shift
explain: Correct: B - visibility plus safe walkways protect night pedestrians. C is wrong - dark clothing hides walkers. A is wrong - roads are for vehicles. D is wrong - never assume visibility.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces snowmobile safety. The teaching includes:
options: Speed does not matter, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Riding on roads is safest, using the equipment available at the bedside
Helmet use, staying on marked trails, never riding on thin ice, and avoiding alcohol
No helmet needed on snow, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: C - helmets, trails, ice awareness, and sobriety prevent snowmobile deaths. D is wrong - helmets are always needed. B is wrong - roads are not for snowmobiles. A is wrong - speed kills.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces personal watercraft safety. The teaching includes:
options: Weaving through swimmers is fun, for the duration of the patient's stay
No life jacket needed for strong swimmers, during the current shift
Alcohol improves operation, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Life jacket use, sober operation, and keeping distance from swimmers and other craft
explain: Correct: D - life jackets, sobriety, and distance prevent watercraft tragedies. B is wrong - everyone needs a jacket. A is wrong - endangering swimmers is never acceptable. C is wrong - alcohol impairs operation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces scuba diving safety basics. The teaching includes:
options: Hold your breath while ascending, and wash hands before and after the procedure
Dive alone to build independence, at the patient's bedside
Never dive alone, get certified training, and follow dive tables and buddy procedures
Skip training to save money, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: C - buddy diving, certification, and table compliance prevent dive injuries. B is wrong - solo diving is dangerous. A is wrong - breath-holding on ascent causes lung injury. D is wrong - training is essential.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces weightlifting safety. The teaching includes:
options: Using spotters for heavy lifts, proper form, and gradual progression
Ignoring pain, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Lift maximum weight alone, at this stage
Holding breath through every lift, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A - spotters, form, and progression prevent injuries. C is wrong - solo max lifts risk crushing injuries. D is wrong - breath-holding spikes blood pressure dangerously. B is wrong - pain signals injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces marathon training safety. The teaching includes:
options: No water needed during long runs, for the duration of the patient's stay
Gradual training, hydration, proper shoes, and stopping for warning symptoms like chest pain or dizziness
New shoes on race day, while maintaining standard precautions throughout
Run through chest pain, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
explain: Correct: B - progressive training, fluids, broken-in shoes, and symptom awareness keep runners safe. D is wrong - chest pain needs evaluation. A is wrong - dehydration is dangerous. C is wrong - new shoes cause blisters.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which road safety measures should the PN reinforce for teen drivers? Select all that apply.
options: No texting or phone use while driving
Never driving under the influence
Seatbelt use on every trip
Obeying speed limits
Racing friends to build skills
explain: Correct: C, A, D, B - belts, distraction-free driving, speed compliance, and sobriety prevent teen crash deaths. E is wrong - racing is never safe or skill-building.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces flood safety. The teaching includes:
options: Floodwater is clean, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Play in floodwater, at this stage, for now
Drive through flooded roads if in a hurry, on this occasion
Turn around, don't drown: never walk or drive through floodwater
explain: Correct: D - floodwater hides hazards and sweeps vehicles away; avoidance is the rule. C is wrong - most flood deaths are in vehicles. B is wrong - floodwater carries sewage and debris. A is wrong - floodwater is contaminated.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces rip current safety. The teaching includes:
options: Swim parallel to shore to escape, then back in; swim near lifeguards
Swim directly against the current, for now
Panic and swim harder, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Rip currents only occur in pools, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A - parallel swimming escapes the current's pull; lifeguarded beaches are safest. B is wrong - fighting the current causes exhaustion and drowning. C is wrong - panic worsens outcomes. D is wrong - rip currents are ocean phenomena.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which hurricane preparedness actions should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Having an evacuation plan
Stocking water, food, and medications
Driving into the storm to leave faster
Securing outdoor items and boarding windows if advised
Ignoring evacuation orders
explain: Correct: A, B, D - evacuation plans, supplies, and property securing are hurricane essentials. C is wrong - driving into storms is deadly. E is wrong - evacuation orders save lives.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces Hib vaccine teaching. Which statement is correct?
options: Only adults need Hib, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission, for now
Hib vaccine protects against Haemophilus influenzae type b, which causes meningitis and epiglottitis in children
Hib is not a real disease, and verify the order against the medication administration record, on this occasion
Hib prevents hip injuries, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - Hib vaccine prevents serious childhood infections including meningitis. D confuses the acronym. A is wrong - it is primarily a childhood vaccine. C is wrong - Hib disease is real and serious.

q: A parent asks about the rotavirus vaccine. The PN reinforces that:
options: It is given to the elderly, before the end of the shift
It treats active diarrhea, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
It protects infants against severe rotavirus diarrhea per the infant schedule
Diarrhea vaccines are unnecessary, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: C - rotavirus vaccine prevents severe infant gastroenteritis. A is wrong - it is an infant vaccine. B is wrong - it prevents, not treats. D is wrong - rotavirus hospitalizes infants.

q: The PN reinforces hepatitis A vaccine teaching. Which statement is correct?
options: The vaccine is recommended for children and at-risk adults, and hand hygiene prevents spread
Hepatitis A spreads only through blood, before administering any further medication
The vaccine is only for travelers, while ensuring the call light is within the patient's reach
Hepatitis A is never serious and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response
explain: Correct: A - Hep A spreads fecal-orally; vaccine plus hygiene prevent it. B is wrong - Hep B is fecal-oral, not bloodborne. D is wrong - it can cause serious liver illness. C is wrong - it is routine for children.

q: The PN reinforces hepatitis B vaccine teaching. Which statement is correct?
options: The vaccine is experimental, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, on this occasion, for now
Hepatitis B always resolves without problems, before administering any further medication
Hepatitis B spreads through casual contact, then document the patient's response to the intervention
The vaccine series protects against bloodborne hepatitis B and is recommended for infants and at-risk adults
explain: Correct: D - Hep B vaccine is routine and prevents chronic liver disease. C is wrong - it spreads through blood and body fluids, not casual contact. A is wrong - it is well established. B is wrong - chronic infection causes cirrhosis and cancer.

q: An older adult asks about vitamin D. The PN reinforces that vitamin D:
options: Replaces all other nutrients, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Causes bones to weaken, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Supports bone health and is recommended per guidelines, especially with limited sun exposure
Is never needed, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for now
explain: Correct: C - vitamin D aids calcium absorption and bone strength. D is wrong - deficiency is common in older adults. A is wrong - no single nutrient replaces others. B is the opposite of its effect.

q: An adult asks about flexibility exercise. The PN reinforces that stretching:
options: Is dangerous for everyone, as documented in the plan of care
Is best done gently after warming up, holding without bouncing
Should be painful to work, for the duration of the patient's stay
Replaces aerobic exercise, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - gentle warm stretching without bouncing improves flexibility safely. C is wrong - pain signals injury. D is wrong - it complements, not replaces, aerobic exercise. A is wrong - it is safe when done properly.

q: Which are expected milestones for an 18-month-old? Select all that apply.
options: Riding a two-wheel bicycle
Walking independently
Writing sentences
Scribbling with a crayon
Saying several single words
explain: Correct: B, D, E - independent walking, scribbling, and word use are 18-month milestones. A and C are years away.

q: Which are expected milestones for a 3-year-old? Select all that apply.
options: Copying a circle
Driving a car
Riding a tricycle
Doing algebra
Speaking in short sentences
explain: Correct: C, A, E - tricycles, circle copying, and sentence speech are 3-year-old milestones. B and D are far in the future.

q: A client jokes about a frightening diagnosis to cope with fear. The PN recognizes this as:
options: Humor, a mature defense mechanism
Inappropriate behavior, for now
Denial, at the patient's bedside
Projection, at this stage
explain: Correct: A - humor reframes distress adaptively. B is wrong - coping humor is not misbehavior. C is wrong - the diagnosis is acknowledged. D is wrong - nothing is attributed to others.

q: A client avoids all social gatherings due to intense fear of embarrassment. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Rudeness, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
A physical illness, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Normal shyness, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Social anxiety disorder, which should be reported to the RN for evaluation
explain: Correct: D - impairing fear of social scrutiny suggests social anxiety disorder. C is wrong - avoidance that impairs life exceeds shyness. A is wrong - it is not rudeness. B is wrong - the pattern is psychological.

q: A client refuses to leave home, fearing panic in public places. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Laziness, on this occasion
Agoraphobia, needing report and supportive care
A vision problem, as documented in the plan of care
Normal behavior, at this stage
explain: Correct: B - homebound fear of public panic is agoraphobia. A is wrong - it is a disorder, not laziness. C is wrong - the fear is psychological. D is wrong - it impairs functioning.

q: A teen repeatedly pulls out their own hair, causing bald spots. The PN's best action is to:
options: Shave the teen's head as punishment, in accordance with facility policy
Ridicule the behavior, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Report to the RN; trichotillomania needs evaluation and a therapeutic plan, while the PN provides nonjudgmental support
Ignore it as a phase, and obtain a new order if the patient's condition changes
explain: Correct: C - hair-pulling disorder needs assessment; the PN supports without judgment. A is wrong - punishment is abusive. D is wrong - it needs evaluation, not dismissal. B is wrong - ridicule worsens shame.

q: A client cuts without suicidal intent, saying it 'relieves pressure.' The PN understands this as:
options: The same as a suicide attempt, then reassess the patient after the intervention
Attention-seeking that should be ignored, using the equipment available at the bedside
Harmless behavior, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Nonsuicidal self-injury, which still requires safety assessment and immediate RN notification
explain: Correct: D - NSSI differs from suicide attempts but still needs safety evaluation and reporting. A is wrong - intent differs, though risk remains. B is wrong - dismissing as attention-seeking is dangerous. C is wrong - self-injury is never harmless.

q: Which approaches support a client with social anxiety? Select all that apply.
options: Forcing the client into large crowds immediately
Teaching coping and relaxation skills
Praising social efforts
Reporting progress and setbacks to the RN
Gradual exposure to feared situations per the care plan
explain: Correct: E, B, C, D - gradual exposure, skills, reinforcement, and reporting support recovery. A is wrong - flooding without a plan overwhelms and harms.

q: Which are risk factors for suicide that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Access to lethal means
Strong supportive relationships
Substance abuse
Previous suicide attempt
Hopelessness and social isolation
explain: Correct: D, A, E, C - prior attempts, means access, hopelessness/isolation, and substance use all raise risk. B is wrong - strong supports are protective, not a risk factor.

q: Which factors protect against suicide that the PN should reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Access to mental health care
Strong connections to family and friends
Restricted access to lethal means
Social isolation
Effective coping and problem-solving skills
explain: Correct: B, E, A, C - connection, coping skills, care access, and means restriction protect. D is wrong - isolation increases risk.

q: The PN is reinforcing double-void technique for incomplete bladder emptying. The instruction is to:
options: Avoid urinating, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Strain forcefully once, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Urinate, wait a few minutes, then try again to empty residual urine
Urinate once quickly, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C - a second attempt after a short wait empties residual urine. D is insufficient for retention. A is wrong - avoidance worsens retention. B is wrong - forceful straining is discouraged.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client is ordered a rectal suppository. The PN's appropriate action is to:
options: Verify the order, explain the procedure, ensure privacy, and report the results to the RN
Skip it as embarrassing, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, for now
Have the UAP administer it, and verify the order against the medication administration record
Administer it without checking the order, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A - verification, explanation, privacy, and reporting are correct. D is wrong - orders are always verified. C is wrong - UAPs do not administer medications. B is wrong - embarrassment never justifies skipping care.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client is ordered a cleansing enema. The PN should:
options: Give it rapidly under high pressure, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change, on this occasion
Follow the order carefully, use lukewarm solution, position the client in left Sims, and report results and tolerance to the RN
Use very hot water for better results, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, as documented in the plan of care
Leave the client unattended, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - lukewarm solution, left Sims position, and monitoring are correct. C is wrong - hot water burns the colon. A is wrong - high pressure risks perforation. D is wrong - the client needs monitoring.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is assessing pain in a nonverbal older adult. The best approach is to:
options: Assume there is no pain and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, based on the findings documented so far, for now
Use a behavioral scale like PAINAD, observing breathing, vocalization, facial expression, body language, and consolability, and report findings
Ask the client to rate pain 1-10, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, as part of the routine care for this patient
Wait for the client to speak, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change, as documented in the plan of care, in full
explain: Correct: B - behavioral scales detect pain in nonverbal clients. A is wrong - inability to speak does not mean no pain. C is wrong - numeric scales need verbal ability. D is wrong - waiting misses suffering.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help prevent dry skin in older adults? Select all that apply.
options: Scrubbing vigorously with rough washcloths
Avoiding very hot water for bathing
Drinking adequate fluids as permitted
Using harsh soaps
Using moisturizers regularly
explain: Correct: E, B, C - moisturizers, lukewarm water, and hydration protect aging skin. D is wrong - harsh soaps strip oils. A is wrong - rough scrubbing injures fragile skin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN offers a hand massage to an anxious client. The benefits the PN can explain include:
options: Replacing all medications, before the end of the shift
Curing anxiety permanently, at this stage
Promoting relaxation and comfort through therapeutic touch
Diagnosing disease, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C - hand massage eases tension and provides comforting human contact. D is wrong - massage does not diagnose. A is wrong - it complements, not replaces, treatment. B is wrong - no permanent cure is promised.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN offers a warm blanket to a chilly client. The PN should ensure the blanket is:
options: Warmed safely per policy, checked for appropriate temperature, and free of hazards
Overheated for maximum warmth, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Applied directly to burned skin, before the end of the shift, for now
Left in the warmer for hours unattended, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A - blanket warmers have temperature and time policies to prevent burns. B is wrong - overheated blankets burn. D is wrong - unattended warming risks overheating. C is wrong - heat on burns worsens injury.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help reduce anxiety before a procedure? Select all that apply.
options: Providing a calm environment
Explaining what to expect in plain language
Being present with the client
Telling the client there is nothing to worry about
Answering questions honestly
explain: Correct: B, E, A, C - information, honesty, calm, and presence all reduce procedural anxiety. D is wrong - dismissive reassurance invalidates feelings.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help an NPO client with thirst? Select all that apply.
options: Giving full glasses of water
Ice chips if permitted by orders
Frequent mouth swabs with water
Lip moisturizer
Sucking on hard candy if permitted
explain: Correct: C, D, B, E - swabs, lip care, permitted ice chips or candy relieve thirst without violating NPO. A is wrong - full glasses break NPO status.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which measures help prevent oral mucositis in clients at risk? Select all that apply.
options: Avoiding tobacco
Rinsing with plain water or saline as directed
Using hard-bristled brushes aggressively
Using a soft toothbrush
Avoiding alcohol-based mouthwashes
explain: Correct: D, B, E, A - gentle brushing, saline rinses, avoiding irritants, and no tobacco protect oral mucosa. C is wrong - aggressive hard brushing injures tissue.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client takes ezetimibe. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Expect immediate results, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Double the dose if cholesterol stays high, before the end of the shift
Stop all diet efforts, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Continue heart-healthy diet and exercise, take it as prescribed, and report muscle pain
explain: Correct: D - ezetimibe complements lifestyle measures; muscle symptoms need reporting. C is wrong - diet remains essential. A is wrong - effect takes weeks. B is wrong - dose changes need orders.

q: A client takes fenofibrate. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Stop it once triglycerides drop without direction, at the patient's bedside
Drink heavily, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, as part of the patient's ongoing care
