Take it with no regard to meals, and encourage the patient to report any new symptoms
Follow diet and exercise plans, take as prescribed, and report muscle pain, dark urine, or gallbladder symptoms
explain: Correct: D - fibrates need lifestyle support and muscle/gallbladder surveillance. C is wrong - timing follows product instructions. A is wrong - stopping needs direction. B is wrong - alcohol raises triglycerides.

q: A client takes dutasteride. The PN reinforces which safety point also used for finasteride?
options: It is safe for children to handle, before administering any further medication
Blood donation is encouraged while taking it, and wash hands before and after the procedure
Pregnant women should not handle broken or crushed capsules due to risk to a male fetus
It works in days, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
explain: Correct: C - 5-alpha reductase inhibitors risk male fetal genital abnormalities. A is wrong - handling precautions apply. D is wrong - effect takes months. B is wrong - blood donation is restricted during and after therapy.

q: A client takes mirabegron for overactive bladder. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Stop it at the first dry mouth, for the duration of the patient's stay
Report increased blood pressure, urinary retention, or rapid heartbeat
Ignore blood pressure, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Expect immediate cure, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B - mirabegron can raise BP and cause retention; monitoring matters. C is wrong - BP needs watching. D is wrong - effect builds over weeks. A is wrong - dry mouth is managed, not a stop signal without direction.

q: A client takes tolterodine. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Report inability to urinate, severe constipation, confusion, or fast heartbeat, and manage dry mouth
Drive without concern, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Take extra doses for faster effect and complete the required documentation before the shift ends
Expect no side effects, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A - antimuscarinic effects need surveillance and dry-mouth management. B is wrong - confusion and blurred vision can impair driving. C is wrong - extra doses cause toxicity. D is wrong - side effects are common.

q: A client takes febuxostat for gout. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Report chest pain, stroke symptoms, rash, or liver symptoms promptly
Stop it during flares without direction, at the patient's bedside
Ignore chest pain, on this occasion
Take it only when joints hurt, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A - febuxostat carries cardiovascular warnings needing prompt reporting. C is wrong - chest pain needs evaluation. B is wrong - stopping needs direction. D is wrong - it is daily prevention.

q: A client takes propylthiouracil (PTU) for hyperthyroidism. Which findings must be reported immediately? The PN watches for:
options: Mild nausea, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Slight weight gain, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Mild headache, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Sore throat, fever, or unusual bleeding suggesting agranulocytosis
explain: Correct: D - PTU can cause agranulocytosis; sore throat and fever are warning signs. A, B, and C are milder issues reported routinely.

q: A client takes nifedipine extended-release. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Chew or crush the tablet for faster effect, as documented in the plan of care
Swallow it whole, report swelling, flushing, or dizziness, and rise slowly
Take it with grapefruit juice, in accordance with facility policy
Stop it if blood pressure is normal one day, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: B - extended-release tablets must stay intact; edema and hypotension need monitoring. A is wrong - crushing destroys the extended release. D is wrong - stopping needs direction. C is wrong - grapefruit raises levels dangerously.

q: The PN is reinforcing alpha blocker teaching for BPH. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Take the first dose at bedtime as directed to reduce fainting risk
Drive immediately after the first dose
Stop the drug without direction once symptoms improve
Report fainting or severe dizziness
Rise slowly to prevent dizziness
explain: Correct: E, A, D - slow rising, bedtime first dose, and reporting syncope manage orthostatic risk. B is wrong - driving after the first dose is unsafe. C is wrong - stopping needs provider direction.

q: The PN is reinforcing antimuscarinic teaching for overactive bladder. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Manage dry mouth with fluids and sugarless gum
Expect increased sweating
Report inability to urinate
Drive without any caution
Report confusion, especially in older adults
explain: Correct: C, A, E - retention, dry mouth management, and confusion surveillance are key. B is wrong - decreased sweating occurs. D is wrong - blurred vision and confusion can impair driving.

q: Which points are correct for safe OTC medication use that the PN should reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Reading labels for active ingredients and warnings
Checking with the pharmacist about interactions with prescriptions
Assuming OTC means risk-free
Reporting side effects
Following dose and duration limits
explain: Correct: A, B, E, D - label reading, interaction checks, dose limits, and reporting make OTC use safe. C is wrong - OTC drugs carry real risks.

q: The PN is reinforcing PTU teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Have blood counts monitored as ordered
Stop it abruptly once symptoms improve
Report sore throat or fever immediately
Report unusual bleeding or bruising
Take it as prescribed even when feeling well
explain: Correct: C, A, E, D - agranulocytosis surveillance, lab monitoring, adherence, and bleeding reports are PTU essentials. B is wrong - abrupt stop risks thyroid storm.

q: Before surgery, the PN ensures contact lenses are removed. The reason is:
options: Contacts are expensive, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Contacts improve surgical vision, on this occasion, for now
Lenses can injure the cornea during anesthesia when the eyes are closed and dry
Surgeons dislike contacts, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: C - closed dry eyes under anesthesia risk corneal abrasion from lenses. B is wrong - contacts do not help surgery. A is irrelevant. D is wrong - it is a safety issue, not preference.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A pre-op client smokes. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Avoid smoking before surgery as directed, since it impairs healing and anesthesia safety
Smoking has no surgical risks, using the equipment available at the bedside
Smoke right before surgery to relax, based on the findings documented so far
Smoke more to build tolerance, while encouraging the patient to ambulate as tolerated
explain: Correct: A - smoking worsens wound healing and pulmonary complications. C is wrong - pre-op smoking is hazardous. D is wrong - more smoking increases harm. B is wrong - risks are well established.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After general anesthesia, a client reports a sore throat. The PN's best response is to:
options: Tell the client something went wrong, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, on this occasion
Give antibiotics without an order, and verify the order against the medication administration record, at this stage
Ignore it, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, with the patient's safety as the stated priority
Explain it is common from the breathing tube, offer cool fluids or lozenges as permitted, and report severe or worsening symptoms
explain: Correct: D - intubation commonly irritates the throat; comfort measures plus surveillance are correct. C is wrong - the complaint deserves a response. A is wrong - alarming the client is nontherapeutic. B is wrong - antibiotics need orders and indications.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After laparoscopic surgery, a client reports shoulder pain. The PN recognizes this as:
options: A surgical error, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Referred pain from residual gas, which usually resolves; the PN reports severe or worsening pain
Unrelated to surgery, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for now
A heart attack, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B - diaphragmatic irritation from insufflation gas causes shoulder pain. D is wrong - the pattern fits laparoscopy, though cardiac causes are ruled out by the team if atypical. A is wrong - it is expected, not error. C is wrong - it is directly related.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A pre-op client takes herbal supplements. The PN should:
options: Ignore them as natural and safe, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Tell the client to double the dose, in accordance with facility policy
Document them and report to the RN; many herbals affect bleeding and anesthesia
Advise the client to hide them from the team, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - herbals like ginkgo and garlic increase bleeding risk and interact with anesthesia. A is wrong - natural does not mean safe. B is wrong - doubling is dangerous. D is wrong - hiding information endangers the client.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which personal items need attention before surgery? Select all that apply.
options: Securing dentures per policy
Wearing makeup to the operating room
Removing jewelry and piercings
Removing contact lenses
Removing nail polish or acrylic nails if they interfere with monitoring
explain: Correct: D, C, E, A - lenses, jewelry, polish, and dentures are all addressed for safety. B is wrong - makeup interferes with skin assessment.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which post-op discomforts are common that the PN should explain and monitor? Select all that apply.
options: Heavy bleeding from the incision
Shoulder pain after laparoscopy
Sore throat from intubation
Mild incisional pain
Nausea
explain: Correct: C, E, B, D - sore throat, nausea, gas-related shoulder pain, and mild incisional pain are common. A is wrong - heavy bleeding is not normal and must be reported.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which medications and substances should be reported before surgery? Select all that apply.
options: Daily multivitamin without any issues
Recreational drugs and alcohol use
Diabetes medications including insulin
Anticoagulants and antiplatelets
Herbal supplements
explain: Correct: D, E, C, B - blood thinners, herbals, diabetes drugs, and substance use all affect anesthesia and bleeding. A is wrong - a plain multivitamin is the least concerning, though still disclosed.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A visitor with a cold wants to visit a client who had surgery yesterday. The PN's best action is to:
options: Allow the visit but hide it from the team, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, in full
Allow the visit without restrictions, and verify the order against the medication administration record, for now
Scold the visitor, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for the duration of the patient's stay
Explain the infection risk and redirect the visitor per facility policy, suggesting alternatives like a phone call
explain: Correct: D - post-op clients are vulnerable; symptomatic visitors are redirected per policy with alternatives offered. B is wrong - exposure risks surgical site infection. C is wrong - scolding is nontherapeutic. A is wrong - hiding violates policy.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client's dentures go missing. The PN should:
options: Search the area, document the loss, report to the RN, and follow facility lost-item procedures
Ignore it; dentures are the client's problem, during the current shift
Buy new dentures personally, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Tell the client they do not need dentures, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule
explain: Correct: A - lost dentures affect nutrition and dignity; search, document, report, and follow policy. B is wrong - it is a care issue. C is wrong - personal purchase is inappropriate. D is wrong - dentures matter for eating and speech.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with lung cancer develops facial swelling, distended neck veins, and dyspnea. The PN should:
options: Document it for the next shift, then report the outcome to the registered nurse
Recognize superior vena cava syndrome and notify the RN immediately
Encourage the client to lie flat, within the scope of the practical nurse's role
Offer a cold compress and wait, using the equipment available at the bedside
explain: Correct: B - SVC syndrome from tumor compression is an oncologic emergency. D is wrong - compresses do not treat obstruction. C is wrong - flat positioning worsens venous congestion. A is wrong - waiting is unsafe.

q: A smoker reports shoulder pain, Horner syndrome (drooping eyelid, small pupil), and hand weakness. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Rotator cuff injury, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Normal aging, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Pancoast tumor, needing prompt RN notification for workup
Carpal tunnel, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C - apical lung tumors cause shoulder pain, Horner syndrome, and brachial plexus signs. A is wrong - cuff injuries do not cause Horner syndrome. D is wrong - carpal tunnel does not explain the full picture. B is wrong - this is not normal aging.

q: A client with asbestos exposure develops progressive dyspnea and chest pain. The PN recognizes the risk of:
options: A common cold, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Asthma only, on this occasion, for now
Anxiety, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Mesothelioma, which should be reported to the RN for workup
explain: Correct: D - asbestos exposure strongly links to mesothelioma. B is wrong - this exceeds asthma. A is wrong - a cold does not fit the history. C is wrong - dyspnea needs medical evaluation, not dismissal.

q: A client with pneumonia develops foul-smelling sputum, fever, and night sweats. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Allergies, on this occasion, for now
Normal recovery, in practice
Lung abscess, needing prompt RN notification
A common cold, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C - foul sputum with persistent fever suggests lung abscess. D is wrong - colds do not produce this picture. A is wrong - allergies lack fever and foul sputum. B is wrong - this is deterioration, not recovery.

q: A client with bronchiectasis produces large amounts of foul sputum daily. The PN reinforces that management includes:
options: Avoiding all fluids, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Airway clearance techniques, prompt treatment of infections, and reporting increased sputum or blood
Bed rest without movement, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Ignoring the sputum, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B - clearance techniques and infection surveillance are the mainstays. C is wrong - immobility worsens clearance. A is wrong - hydration thins secretions. D is wrong - sputum changes signal infection.

q: A child with cystic fibrosis has frequent lung infections and poor weight gain. The PN reinforces that management includes:
options: Airway clearance, pancreatic enzymes with meals, high-calorie diet, and reporting respiratory changes
Skipping enzymes when feeling well, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time
Restricting fluids, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Avoiding all exercise, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: A - clearance, enzymes, nutrition, and surveillance manage CF. D is wrong - exercise aids clearance. B is wrong - enzymes are lifelong. C is wrong - hydration thins secretions.

q: After chest trauma, the PN notes dyspnea with dullness to percussion on one side. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Pneumothorax with hyperresonance, for now
Anxiety, based on the findings documented so far
A bruise only, in accordance with facility policy
Hemothorax, needing immediate RN notification
explain: Correct: D - blood in the pleural space causes dullness with dyspnea after trauma. A is wrong - pneumothorax gives hyperresonance, not dullness. C is wrong - this exceeds a bruise. B is wrong - the findings are physical, not anxiety.

q: A client post-thoracic surgery has milky chest tube drainage. The PN should:
options: Increase the suction, on this occasion
Report to the RN; milky drainage suggests chylothorax
Document it as normal, for now
Clamp the tube, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: B - chyle in the pleural space needs evaluation and dietary management. C is wrong - milky drainage is abnormal. A is wrong - suction changes need orders. D is wrong - clamping needs direction.

q: A client with pneumonia develops persistent fever with pleuritic pain despite antibiotics. The PN recognizes possible:
options: Indigestion, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Recovery, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Empyema, needing prompt RN notification for further workup
Muscle strain, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
explain: Correct: C - pus in the pleural space complicates pneumonia. B is wrong - persistent fever is not recovery. D is wrong - the pattern fits pleural infection. A is wrong - indigestion does not cause this picture.

q: A young adult develops chest pain, fever, and fatigue weeks after a viral illness. The PN recognizes possible:
options: Myocarditis, needing prompt RN notification
Muscle strain only, in practice
Heartburn, during the current shift
Normal recovery, for now
explain: Correct: A - post-viral chest pain with systemic symptoms suggests myocardial inflammation. C is wrong - heartburn lacks fever and fatigue pattern. B is wrong - viral prodrome points beyond muscle. D is wrong - this is not normal recovery.

q: An older adult reports fainting with exertion and a harsh systolic murmur. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Normal aging, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Dehydration, in accordance with facility policy
Anemia only, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Aortic stenosis, needing prompt RN notification for cardiology workup
explain: Correct: D - exertional syncope with systolic murmur is classic aortic stenosis. C is wrong - anemia does not explain the murmur pattern. B is wrong - dehydration lacks the murmur. A is wrong - syncope is never normal aging.

q: A young woman reports a mid-systolic click with palpitations. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Pneumonia, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Aortic stenosis, before the end of the shift, for now
Mitral valve prolapse, which should be reported to the RN for evaluation
Normal heart sounds, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C - mid-systolic click is the hallmark of mitral valve prolapse. B is wrong - AS gives a systolic ejection murmur, not a click. D is wrong - clicks are abnormal. A is unrelated.

q: An older adult has alternating fast and slow heart rates with dizziness. The PN recognizes possible:
options: Sick sinus syndrome, needing prompt RN notification
Normal rhythm, at this stage
Anxiety, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Dehydration only, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: A - tachy-brady swings with symptoms suggest sinus node dysfunction. B is wrong - symptomatic swings are not normal. D is wrong - dehydration does not explain the pattern. C is wrong - the rhythm finding is organic.

q: A young client has episodes of rapid heart rate with a delta wave on ECG. The PN understands this as most consistent with:
options: Anemia, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, needing cardiology follow-up
Normal variant, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Dehydration, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B - delta waves with tachycardia define WPW's accessory pathway. C is wrong - it is not a normal variant. A and D do not cause delta waves.

q: A client with a new pacemaker reports dizziness and the PN notes the pulse is 40. The PN should:
options: Reassure the client the pacemaker is working, before the end of the shift
Encourage exercise, as documented in the plan of care
Report to the RN immediately; bradycardia with symptoms suggests pacemaker malfunction
Turn off the pacemaker, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: C - failure to pace needs urgent evaluation. A is wrong - symptoms contradict reassurance. B is wrong - exertion is unsafe. D is wrong - the PN never disables devices.

q: A client with an ICD receives a shock while awake. The PN's priority is to:
options: Assess the client, stay with them, notify the RN immediately, and prepare for emergency evaluation
Remove the ICD, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Tell the client shocks are harmless, before administering any further medication
Ignore it as normal, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A - shocks need assessment for cause and device function. D is wrong - shocks always need evaluation. C is wrong - they signal dysrhythmia. B is wrong - the PN never removes devices.

q: Which findings suggest superior vena cava syndrome that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Facial and neck swelling
Dyspnea
Leg swelling only
Distended neck and chest veins
Headache from venous congestion
explain: Correct: A, D, B, E - upper body swelling, venous distention, dyspnea, and congestion headache define SVC syndrome. C is wrong - isolated leg swelling suggests lower-body venous issues.

q: Which findings suggest lung abscess that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Clear, scant sputum
Foul-smelling sputum
Weight loss
Persistent fever and night sweats
Pleuritic chest pain
explain: Correct: B, D, E, C - foul sputum, prolonged fever, pleuritic pain, and weight loss suggest abscess. A is wrong - scant clear sputum does not fit.

q: The PN is reinforcing bronchiectasis management. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Seeking prompt treatment for respiratory infections
Reporting increased sputum volume or blood
Staying hydrated
Performing airway clearance techniques as taught
Avoiding all physical activity
explain: Correct: D, A, B, C - clearance, infection treatment, sputum surveillance, and hydration manage bronchiectasis. E is wrong - activity aids clearance.

q: The PN is reinforcing cystic fibrosis management. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Airway clearance as prescribed
High-calorie, high-protein diet
Reporting increased cough, sputum change, or weight loss
Skipping treatments when feeling well
Pancreatic enzymes with meals and snacks
explain: Correct: A, E, B, C - clearance, enzymes, nutrition, and surveillance are CF essentials. D is wrong - treatments are lifelong maintenance.

q: Which pacemaker precautions should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting dizziness, fainting, or palpitations
Avoiding strong electromagnetic interference as instructed
Attending regular device checks
Playing full-contact sports immediately
Keeping the incision clean and reporting redness or swelling
explain: Correct: A, B, E, C - symptom reporting, EMI avoidance, wound care, and follow-up protect pacemaker clients. D is wrong - contact sports risk lead dislodgement.

q: Which findings suggest worsening aortic stenosis that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Improved exercise tolerance
Dyspnea on exertion
Exertional syncope
Angina
Harsh systolic murmur
explain: Correct: C, D, B, E - syncope, angina, dyspnea, and the murmur are the AS triad plus exam finding. A is wrong - improvement contradicts worsening disease.

q: After spinal cord injury, a client develops warm dry skin, bradycardia, and severe hypotension. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Cardiogenic shock, at this stage
Sepsis, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Hypovolemic shock, on this occasion
Neurogenic shock, needing immediate RN notification
explain: Correct: D - loss of sympathetic tone causes warm vasodilated skin with bradycardia and hypotension. C is wrong - hypovolemic shock gives cool clammy skin and tachycardia. A is wrong - cardiogenic shock gives cool skin and tachycardia. B is wrong - sepsis has infectious signs.

q: Minutes after an IV antibiotic starts, a client develops hives, wheezing, and hypotension. The PN's priority is to:
options: Slow the infusion and observe, in accordance with facility policy
Stop the infusion, stay with the client, and call for help immediately
Give oral antihistamine and continue, before administering any further medication
Document and finish the infusion, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B - anaphylaxis needs immediate infusion stop, airway support, and emergency response. A is wrong - slowing is insufficient for anaphylaxis. C is wrong - oral drugs are too slow and continuing is dangerous. D is wrong - finishing the infusion worsens the reaction.

q: A client with a large pulmonary embolism develops sudden hypotension with distended neck veins and clear lungs. The PN recognizes this as most consistent with:
options: Anaphylaxis, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Hypovolemic shock, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Obstructive shock, needing immediate RN notification
Neurogenic shock, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C - blocked cardiac filling causes hypotension with JVD and clear lungs. B is wrong - hypovolemia gives flat neck veins. A is wrong - anaphylaxis has hives and wheezing. D is wrong - neurogenic gives warm dry skin.

q: A critically ill client develops worsening renal, respiratory, and hepatic failure despite treatment. The PN recognizes this progression as:
options: Normal critical illness, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
A single organ problem, during the current shift, in full
Recovery, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for now
Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), needing immediate RN notification
explain: Correct: D - sequential multi-organ failure is MODS. C is wrong - this is deterioration. B is wrong - multiple systems are failing. A is wrong - MODS is life-threatening, not normal.

q: A client in early shock has tachycardia, restlessness, and cool extremities with normal blood pressure. The PN understands this as:
options: Compensated shock, needing prompt RN notification before decompensation
Recovery, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Normal vital signs, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Decompensated shock, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A - compensatory mechanisms maintain BP while perfusion falls; early action prevents collapse. D is wrong - decompensation shows hypotension. B is wrong - this is deterioration. C is wrong - tachycardia and restlessness are abnormal.

q: The PN is monitoring a client receiving a fluid bolus for shock. Which findings suggest the bolus is helping? The PN watches for:
options: Increasing heart rate, on this occasion
Rising blood pressure, improved urine output, and better mentation
Worsening crackles alone, as documented in the plan of care
Falling blood pressure, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B - improved perfusion markers show resuscitation working. D is wrong - falling BP means worsening. C is wrong - crackles suggest overload. A is wrong - rising rate suggests ongoing shock.

q: A client on norepinephrine develops cold, pale fingers with a weak pulse at the IV site. The PN should:
options: Apply heat without direction, on this occasion, for now
Stop and assess; report to the RN immediately, as extravasation causes tissue injury
Increase the infusion, during the current shift
Massage the site vigorously, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B - vasopressor extravasation causes necrosis; stop, assess, and report. C is wrong - increasing worsens injury. D is wrong - massage spreads the drug. A is wrong - heat needs direction and may worsen injury.

q: The PN is caring for a client in septic shock with warm, flushed skin. The PN understands this as:
options: Warm shock from vasodilation, still needing urgent treatment and RN notification
A sign of recovery, as documented in the plan of care
Normal skin, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Neurogenic shock, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A - early distributive shock can present warm before progressing to cold shock. C is wrong - it is abnormal. B is wrong - it is not recovery. D is wrong - the cause is sepsis, not spinal injury.

q: The PN is monitoring urine output in shock. The finding that suggests adequate renal perfusion is:
options: Anuria, for now
Dark, scant urine
5 mL/hr, on this occasion
At least 30 mL/hr in an adult
explain: Correct: D - 30 mL/hr indicates adequate kidney perfusion. C is wrong - 5 mL/hr is oliguric. A is wrong - anuria means failure. B is wrong - dark scant urine shows hypoperfusion.

q: A client in shock has a rising lactate level. The PN understands this means:
options: A lab error, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Normal metabolism, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Worsening tissue hypoperfusion, needing prompt RN notification
Improving perfusion, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C - lactate rises with anaerobic metabolism from poor perfusion. D is the opposite. A is wrong - trending lactate is clinically meaningful. B is wrong - rising lactate is abnormal.

q: The PN is positioning a hypotensive client. The best position while awaiting the RN is:
options: Prone, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
High Fowler, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Supine with legs slightly elevated, unless contraindicated
Standing, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: C - supine with leg elevation aids venous return. B is wrong - upright worsens hypotension. A is wrong - prone impairs breathing. D is dangerous.

q: A client receiving dopamine develops tachycardia and chest pain. The PN should:
options: Increase the rate, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Report to the RN immediately; these suggest cardiac ischemia from the infusion
Document for the next shift, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Encourage the client to walk, based on the findings documented so far
explain: Correct: B - dopamine can cause tachydysrhythmias and ischemia needing urgent rate adjustment. A is wrong - increasing worsens ischemia. D is wrong - exertion is unsafe. C is wrong - waiting is unsafe.

q: The PN notes a client's central venous pressure trending upward with new crackles during fluid resuscitation. The PN should:
options: Hold and report to the RN; rising CVP with crackles suggests fluid overload
Increase the fluid rate, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Continue fluids rapidly, in accordance with facility policy
Ignore the trend, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A - rising filling pressures with pulmonary signs mean overload. C and B worsen overload. D is wrong - trends guide resuscitation.

q: A client with cardiac tamponade develops hypotension, JVD, and muffled heart sounds. The PN should:
options: Reassure and wait, on this occasion
Encourage deep breathing exercises, for now
Give oral fluids, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Recognize Beck's triad and notify the RN immediately
explain: Correct: D - Beck's triad signals obstructive shock needing emergency pericardial drainage. B is wrong - breathing exercises do not treat tamponade. C is wrong - fluids need orders and do not fix compression. A is wrong - waiting is unsafe.

q: The PN is monitoring a client with a pulmonary artery catheter. The PN's role is to:
options: Monitor the insertion site and waveforms for damping or dysrhythmia, and report changes to the RN
Remove the catheter when done, then reassess the patient after the intervention
Advance the catheter, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Interpret pressures to adjust medications, during the current shift, for now
explain: Correct: A - the PN monitors and reports; interpretation and adjustments belong to the RN/provider. C is wrong - advancing is not PN scope. D is wrong - interpreting to titrate is RN scope. B is wrong - removal needs direction.

q: A client in shock has cool, mottled extremities with delayed capillary refill. The PN understands this indicates:
options: Normal aging skin, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Poor peripheral perfusion from vasoconstriction, needing prompt RN notification
Good perfusion, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Allergic reaction, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B - mottling and delayed refill show compensatory vasoconstriction. C is the opposite. A is wrong - mottling is not normal aging. D is wrong - anaphylaxis gives warm flushed skin.

q: The PN is caring for a client with distributive shock. The PN understands the underlying problem is:
options: Heart pump failure, at this stage
Blocked cardiac filling, on this occasion
Widespread vasodilation with maldistribution of blood flow
Blood loss, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C - distributive shock (sepsis, anaphylaxis, neurogenic) involves vasodilation. D describes hypovolemic shock. A describes cardiogenic shock. B describes obstructive shock.

q: Which findings suggest anaphylaxis that the PN must act on immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Warm, dry skin with bradycardia
Wheezing and stridor
Tachycardia
Hives and angioedema
Hypotension
explain: Correct: D, B, E, C - skin, airway, and cardiovascular signs define anaphylaxis. A is wrong - warm dry skin with bradycardia suggests neurogenic shock.

q: Which findings suggest neurogenic shock that the PN must report? Select all that apply.
options: Warm, dry skin
Cool, clammy skin with tachycardia
History of spinal cord injury
Hypotension
Bradycardia
explain: Correct: D, E, A, C - hypotension, bradycardia, warm dry skin, and spinal injury history define neurogenic shock. B is wrong - cool clammy skin with tachycardia fits hypovolemic or cardiogenic shock.

q: Which conditions can cause obstructive shock that the PN should recognize? Select all that apply.
options: Hemorrhage
Cardiac tamponade
Severe sepsis without obstruction
Massive pulmonary embolism
Tension pneumothorax
explain: Correct: B, D, E - tamponade, massive PE, and tension pneumothorax all block cardiac filling or output. C is wrong - sepsis causes distributive shock. A is wrong - hemorrhage causes hypovolemic shock.

q: Which are late signs of shock that the PN must report immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Slight tachycardia only
Metabolic acidosis
Hypotension
Altered mental status
Decreased urine output
explain: Correct: C, E, D, B - hypotension, oliguria, confusion, and acidosis mark decompensation. A is wrong - isolated mild tachycardia is an early sign.

q: Which nursing actions help prevent MODS in critically ill clients? Select all that apply.
options: Monitoring organ function and reporting deterioration
Maintaining perfusion with ordered fluids and medications
Providing adequate nutrition as ordered
Preventing infection with hand hygiene and aseptic technique
Delaying treatment of infections
explain: Correct: D, B, A, C - infection prevention, perfusion support, surveillance, and nutrition all protect organs. E is wrong - delayed treatment worsens outcomes.

q: The PN is monitoring a client on vasopressors. Which precautions apply? Select all that apply.
options: Continuous blood pressure and cardiac monitoring
Never adjusting the rate without an order
Giving the infusion through any available peripheral vein without assessment
Assessing the IV site frequently for extravasation
Reporting tachycardia, chest pain, or diminished pulses
explain: Correct: A, D, E, B - monitoring, site checks, symptom reporting, and order-based titration are vasopressor essentials. C is wrong - large veins or central access are preferred and sites need assessment.

q: The PN is monitoring fluid resuscitation in shock. Which findings must be reported? Select all that apply.
options: Steady improvement in perfusion markers
New crackles or dyspnea
Decreasing urine output despite fluids
Rising CVP with signs of overload
Worsening hypotension
explain: Correct: B, D, C, E - overload signs, persistent oliguria, and refractory hypotension all need reporting. A is wrong - improvement is the goal, not a concern.

q: During a code, the RN directs the PN to perform chest compressions. The PN's appropriate action is to:
options: Take over leading the code, based on the findings documented so far
Leave to document, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Refuse; codes are RN-only, as documented in the plan of care
Perform compressions as directed within the team role and training
explain: Correct: D - the PN participates in codes per training under RN direction. C is wrong - PNs are code team members. A is wrong - leading the code exceeds PN scope. B is wrong - abandoning the code is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN receives a critical lab value. The PN should:
options: Call the provider directly with a new plan, as documented in the plan of care
Report it to the RN immediately per policy and document the notification
Repeat the lab in an hour first, and record the intake and output for the shift
File it for the next shift and inform the family of the patient's current condition
explain: Correct: B - critical values need immediate RN notification per policy. D is wrong - waiting endangers the client. A is wrong - the PN reports to the RN, who coordinates with the provider. C is wrong - delaying for a repeat is unsafe.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is asked to witness informed consent. The PN's role is to:
options: Witness the client's signature and confirm the client appears informed, reporting concerns to the RN
Sign as the person obtaining consent and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, in this case
Explain the procedure to the client, based on the findings documented so far
Coerce the client to sign quickly, while monitoring for signs of infection at the site
explain: Correct: A - the PN witnesses; the provider obtains consent. C is wrong - explaining the procedure is the provider's role. B is wrong - the PN does not obtain consent. D is wrong - coercion violates autonomy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN suspects a client is being abused at home. The PN should:
options: Confront the suspected abuser, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Ignore it as a family matter, within the scope of the practical nurse's role
Investigate alone, in accordance with facility policy
Report to the RN and follow mandatory reporting laws and facility policy
explain: Correct: D - suspected abuse triggers reporting per law and policy. A is wrong - confrontation endangers the client. B is wrong - abuse is never a private matter. C is wrong - investigation belongs to authorities.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client reports chest pain while the PN is about to give routine medications to another client. The PN should:
options: Finish the routine medications first, during the current shift, for now
Tell the chest pain client to wait, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Attend to the chest pain client first, staying with them and notifying the RN
Give the chest pain client aspirin without an order
explain: Correct: C - chest pain is potentially life-threatening and takes priority. A is wrong - routine tasks wait for emergencies. B is wrong - delaying is unsafe. D is wrong - medications need orders.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN delegates vital signs to the UAP for a stable client. The PN remains responsible for:
options: Supervising, verifying the results, and reporting abnormal findings to the RN
Nothing; delegation transfers responsibility, on this occasion, for now
Doing the vitals anyway, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Letting the UAP interpret the results, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A - the PN retains accountability for delegated tasks. B is wrong - responsibility is never transferred. C is wrong - duplication wastes resources. D is wrong - interpretation belongs to licensed nurses.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN believes a provider's order is unsafe. The PN should:
options: Carry it out anyway, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Hold the order, clarify with the prescriber, and notify the RN per chain of command
Ignore it silently, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Change the order independently, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
explain: Correct: B - unsafe orders are clarified through the chain of command. A is wrong - carrying out unsafe orders harms clients. D is wrong - the PN cannot change orders. C is wrong - silent ignoring leaves the issue unresolved.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is giving SBAR handoff to the RN. The correct order is:
options: Background, Recommendation, Situation, Assessment
Assessment, Situation, Recommendation, Background
Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
Recommendation, Background, Assessment, Situation
explain: Correct: C - SBAR is Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation. D, B, and A scramble the sequence, which confuses urgent communication.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A medication error occurs. The PN's first priority is to:
options: Blame the pharmacy, as documented in the plan of care
Complete the incident report, on this occasion
Hide the error, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Assess the client and notify the RN immediately
explain: Correct: D - client safety comes first; reporting follows. B is wrong - the report comes after the client is safe. C is wrong - hiding errors is unsafe and unethical. A is wrong - blame fixes nothing.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN notes a new neurological change: a stroke client's speech suddenly worsens. The PN should:
options: Wait to see if it improves, for the duration of the patient's stay
Increase the client's fluids, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Report to the RN immediately; new neuro deficits may signal extension or bleeding
Reassure the family it is normal, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - new deficits need urgent evaluation. A is wrong - waiting risks permanent damage. D is wrong - false reassurance misleads. B is wrong - fluids need orders and do not treat neuro changes.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The charge RN asks the PN to take a client requiring complex assessment and care planning. The PN should:
options: Accept without question, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Decline the assignment as beyond PN scope and discuss an appropriate reassignment with the RN
Accept and figure it out alone, without first verifying the patient's identity at the bedside
Delegate it to the UAP, since the finding is an expected effect of the prescribed treatment, at this stage
explain: Correct: B - the PN practices within scope and advocates for safe assignments. A is wrong - accepting beyond scope is unsafe. C is wrong - figuring it out alone risks harm. D is wrong - UAPs cannot take complex assignments either.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is assigning tasks to the UAP for a team of stable clients. Which assignments are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Helping a client with bathing
Administering oral medications
Performing the initial admission assessment
Measuring intake and output
Assisting a stable client with ambulation
explain: Correct: E, D, A - ambulation, I&O, and hygiene are appropriate UAP tasks for stable clients. C is wrong - admission assessment is licensed-nurse scope. B is wrong - UAPs do not administer medications.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which elements belong in an end-of-shift handoff report? Select all that apply.
options: Current client status and vital sign trends
Response to treatments
Changes during the shift
The nurse's personal opinions about the client's family
Pending labs, procedures, and orders
explain: Correct: A, E, C, B - status, pending items, changes, and responses ensure continuity. D is wrong - personal opinions do not belong in handoff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: The PN is prioritizing four clients. Which client should the PN see first?
options: A client with new chest pain
A client asking about discharge paperwork
A client due for a routine dressing change
A client requesting an extra blanket
explain: Correct: A - new chest pain is potentially life-threatening and takes priority over all routine needs. D is a comfort request that waits. C is a scheduled task that waits. B is nonurgent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which actions are appropriate when the PN witnesses a client's advance directive discussion? Select all that apply.
options: Ensuring the directive is placed in the chart per policy
Documenting the client's stated wishes accurately
Overriding the directive if the nurse disagrees
Reporting the discussion to the RN
Pressuring the client to change their wishes
explain: Correct: B, D, A - accurate documentation, reporting, and filing honor autonomy. C is wrong - nurses never override directives. E is wrong - pressuring violates autonomy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: Which post-operative findings must the PN report to the RN immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Saturated dressings with active bleeding
Systolic blood pressure of 80 with confusion
Mild incisional pain controlled by medication
Oxygen saturation of 89%
Sudden calf swelling and pain
explain: Correct: B, A, D, E - severe hypotension with confusion, active bleeding, hypoxemia, and possible DVT are all urgent. C is wrong - mild controlled incisional pain is expected.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Coordinated Care

q: A client is scheduled for an MRI. The PN should ensure that:
options: Oxygen tanks are wheeled in freely, and notify the charge nurse of the change in condition
Screening is unnecessary, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
The client brings all jewelry into the scanner, during the current shift
All metal objects and implants are screened per protocol before entering the MRI area
explain: Correct: D - the MRI magnet turns metal objects into projectiles and disrupts implants. C is wrong - jewelry is removed. A is wrong - only MRI-safe equipment enters. B is wrong - screening is mandatory.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN is caring for a client on home oxygen. The teaching includes:
options: Smoking is fine near oxygen, under the supervision of the registered nurse
No smoking or open flames near oxygen; post signs and keep oxygen away from heat
Oxygen is not flammable so precautions are unnecessary, during the current shift
Storing tanks near the stove, and assess the patient's understanding of the teaching provided
explain: Correct: B - oxygen accelerates combustion; no smoking or flames. A is wrong - smoking near oxygen causes fires. C is wrong - oxygen-enriched air ignites easily. D is wrong - heat near tanks is dangerous.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A fire breaks out in a client's room. Using RACE, the PN's first action is to:
options: Gather belongings, on this occasion
Extinguish the fire
Pull the alarm, in practice
Rescue clients in immediate danger
explain: Correct: D - RACE starts with Rescue. B is wrong - extinguishing comes after rescue and alarm. C is second, not first. A is wrong - belongings are never prioritized.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN uses a fire extinguisher. PASS stands for:
options: Pull, Alert, Squeeze, Stop, on this occasion, for now
Push, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep, as documented in the plan of care
Pull the pin, Aim low, Squeeze the handle, Sweep side to side
Pour, Aim, Spray, Stand, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: C - Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep is the correct sequence. B is wrong - pushing is not the first step. D and A are incorrect sequences.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client reports a latex allergy. The PN should:
options: Use latex-free gloves and equipment, document the allergy, and alert the team
Ignore it as minor, in accordance with facility policy
Use latex gloves anyway, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Avoid all medical care for the client, while maintaining standard precautions throughout
explain: Correct: A - latex-free alternatives and team alerts prevent anaphylaxis. C is wrong - latex exposure can kill. B is wrong - the allergy is serious. D is wrong - care continues with safe products.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN finds a frayed electrical cord on a client's IV pump. The PN should:
options: Remove the device from service, tag it, and report per policy
Tape it and continue use, before the end of the shift
Use it carefully, for the duration of the patient's stay
Ignore it, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A - damaged cords risk shock and fire; tag and report. B is wrong - tape does not make it safe. C is wrong - careful use still risks shock. D is wrong - ignoring endangers everyone.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A chemotherapy spill occurs. The PN's first action is to:
options: Mop it with regular supplies, and confirm the patient's identity using two identifiers
Clean it with bare hands, since the same approach was used during the previous shift
Follow the facility chemo-spill protocol using proper PPE and notify the appropriate team
Leave it for housekeeping without warning, and evaluate whether the patient's goals were met
explain: Correct: C - chemo spills need spill kits, PPE, and trained response. B is wrong - bare-hand contact absorbs cytotoxic drugs. A is wrong - regular mopping spreads contamination. D is wrong - unwarned staff get exposed.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client begins choking and cannot speak. The PN should:
options: Give back slaps indefinitely, as documented in the plan of care
Perform abdominal thrusts per current guidelines and call for help
Wait to see if it resolves, for the duration of the patient's stay
Offer water, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B - abdominal thrusts dislodge complete obstructions; help is summoned. A is wrong - back slaps alone are not the adult protocol for complete obstruction. D is wrong - water worsens obstruction. C is wrong - waiting risks death.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which fall-prevention measures should the PN use for an at-risk older adult? Select all that apply.
options: Leaving the bed in high position for convenience
Keeping the bed in low position with brakes locked
Encouraging nonskid footwear
Keeping personal items and a nightlight accessible
Ensuring the call light is within reach
explain: Correct: B, E, D, C - low locked bed, call light, accessible items with lighting, and nonskid footwear all prevent falls. A is wrong - high beds increase fall injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are alternatives to restraints the PN should try first? Select all that apply.
options: Calm redirection and reorientation
Applying restraints immediately for convenience
Frequent rounding and toileting
Addressing pain, hunger, or unmet needs
Family presence or sitters
explain: Correct: C, E, A, D - rounding, companionship, redirection, and meeting needs reduce restraint use. B is wrong - restraints are a last resort, never for convenience.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which seizure precautions should the PN implement? Select all that apply.
options: Restraining the client's limbs during a seizure
Staying with the client during a seizure and timing it
Placing objects in the client's mouth
Keeping suction and oxygen equipment available
Padding the bed rails
explain: Correct: E, D, B - padded rails, rescue equipment, and observation with timing are correct. C is wrong - objects in the mouth cause injury. A is wrong - restraining limbs causes injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which burn-prevention teachings should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Leaving cooking unattended
Keeping hot liquids away from children
Using sunscreen to prevent sunburn
Turning pot handles inward on the stove
Testing bath water temperature
explain: Correct: E, D, B, C - water testing, handle positioning, hot-liquid safety, and sun protection all prevent burns. A is wrong - unattended cooking causes fires.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The PN reinforces dental health for an older adult with dentures. The teaching includes:
options: Ignoring mouth sores, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, for now
Dentures never need cleaning, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Sleeping in dentures always, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Cleaning dentures daily, removing them at night, and reporting sore spots or poor fit
explain: Correct: D - daily cleaning, nightly removal, and fit monitoring protect oral tissue. B is wrong - dentures harbor bacteria. C is wrong - tissues need rest. A is wrong - sores need evaluation.

q: The PN reinforces testicular self-exam teaching. The correct instruction is to:
options: Only examine if pain occurs, as documented in the plan of care
Examine monthly, feeling for lumps or changes, and report abnormalities promptly
Examine once a year, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Avoid touching the area, on this occasion
explain: Correct: B - monthly exams catch testicular cancer early when most curable. C is wrong - yearly is too infrequent. A is wrong - cancer is often painless. D is wrong - avoidance misses disease.

q: The PN reinforces breast self-awareness. The teaching includes:
options: Mammograms replace all awareness, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion
Only young women need awareness, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, at this stage
Lumps are always cancer, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, going forward, for now
Knowing how breasts normally look and feel and reporting changes promptly, plus mammograms per guidelines
explain: Correct: D - self-awareness plus guideline mammograms detect cancer early. A is wrong - both matter. B is wrong - risk rises with age. C is wrong - most lumps are benign but need evaluation.

q: An adult asks about colorectal cancer screening. The PN reinforces that:
options: Screening is never needed, as documented in the plan of care
Screening is only for the elderly with symptoms
Screening per guidelines starting at age 45 helps find cancer early
Symptoms always appear early, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: C - guideline screening from 45 catches precancerous polyps. B is wrong - screening starts before symptoms. A is wrong - screening saves lives. D is wrong - early cancer is often silent.

q: The PN reinforces skin self-exam teaching. The client should watch for:
options: Only freckles
Skin exams are unnecessary
Moles that change in size, shape, color, or border, and report them
Changes are never concerning
explain: Correct: A - changing moles may signal melanoma and need evaluation. C is wrong - all changing lesions matter. D is wrong - changes can be malignant. B is wrong - skin exams detect cancer early.

q: An older man asks about prostate screening. Which points should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Assuming screening decisions are one-size-fits-all
Reporting urinary changes such as weak stream or blood
Ignoring urinary symptoms
Knowing family history and risk factors
Discussing benefits and risks with the provider to make an informed decision
explain: Correct: E, D, B - shared decision-making, risk awareness, and symptom reporting guide prostate care. A is wrong - decisions are individualized. C is wrong - symptoms need evaluation.

q: Which sleep hygiene measures should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping a consistent sleep schedule
Drinking alcohol to fall asleep
Making the bedroom dark, quiet, and cool
Exercising regularly but not right before bed
Limiting caffeine and screens before bed
explain: Correct: A, E, C, D - schedule, stimulant limits, environment, and timed exercise all improve sleep. B is wrong - alcohol fragments sleep.

q: Which stress management techniques can the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Using alcohol to cope
Adequate sleep
Regular physical activity
Deep breathing and relaxation exercises
Seeking social support
explain: Correct: C, D, B, E - exercise, relaxation, sleep, and support all manage stress healthily. A is wrong - alcohol worsens stress and health.

q: A client is crying and the PN sits quietly with them. This therapeutic technique is:
options: Ignoring the client, before the end of the shift
Silence, which gives the client space to process feelings
Avoidance, as documented in the plan of care
Rudeness, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
explain: Correct: B - purposeful silence communicates presence and acceptance. C is wrong - the nurse is present, not avoiding. A is wrong - attentive silence is not ignoring. D is wrong - it is deeply respectful.

q: A client says, 'I feel like a failure.' The PN responds, 'You feel like a failure.' This technique is:
options: Parroting rudely, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Giving advice, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Changing the subject, on this occasion
Reflecting, which encourages the client to explore the feeling
explain: Correct: D - reflecting mirrors feelings to deepen exploration. A is wrong - it is therapeutic, not rude. B is wrong - no advice was given. C is wrong - the topic was maintained.

q: A client gives a vague statement and the PN asks, 'What do you mean by that?' This technique is:
options: Clarifying, which ensures accurate understanding
Judging, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Probing aggressively, as documented in the plan of care
Minimizing, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A - clarifying prevents misunderstanding. C is wrong - the question is open, not aggressive. B is wrong - no judgment was expressed. D is wrong - it takes the statement seriously.

q: A client consciously decides to postpone worrying about surgery until after a family event. The PN recognizes this as:
options: Projection, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Denial, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Suppression, a conscious and adaptive defense mechanism
Repression, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C - suppression deliberately sets aside distress. B is wrong - denial is unconscious. D is wrong - repression is unconscious. A is wrong - nothing is attributed to others.

q: A client channels anger about illness into vigorous volunteer work. The PN recognizes this as:
options: Denial, before the end of the shift
Regression, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Displacement, for now
Sublimation, a mature defense mechanism
explain: Correct: D - sublimation redirects unacceptable impulses into valued activity. C is wrong - displacement shifts to a safer target, not a valued one. A is wrong - the illness is acknowledged. B is wrong - no childlike behavior occurs.

q: Which actions support a grieving family? Select all that apply.
options: Offering presence and listening
Acknowledging their loss with sincere condolences
Allowing cultural and spiritual practices
Respecting their need for privacy
Telling them to move on quickly
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - presence, acknowledgment, cultural respect, and privacy all support grief. E is wrong - rushing grief is harmful.

q: The PN is caring for a client with mania who is intrusive and grandiose. Which approaches are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Setting clear, consistent limits calmly
Reducing environmental stimulation
Redirecting to structured activities
Reporting escalation to the RN
Arguing with the grandiose beliefs
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - limits, low stimulation, redirection, and reporting manage mania safely. E is wrong - arguing escalates the client.

q: Which are vegetative signs of depression the PN should report? Select all that apply.
options: Increased goal-directed activity
Appetite and weight changes
Sleep disturbances
Loss of energy
Decreased libido
explain: Correct: C, B, D, E - sleep, appetite, energy, and libido changes are vegetative signs. A is wrong - increased goal-directed activity suggests mania.

q: A client with orthopnea is short of breath lying flat. The PN should position the client:
options: Prone, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion
Upright, such as high Fowler or sitting on the side of the bed leaning over a table
Supine, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Trendelenburg, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B - upright positioning eases breathing in orthopnea. C is wrong - flat worsens dyspnea. A is wrong - prone impairs breathing further. D is wrong - head-down worsens congestion.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is logrolling a client after spinal surgery. The correct technique is:
options: Letting the client turn alone, and encourage the patient to report any new symptoms
Twisting the spine gently, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Keeping the spine in straight alignment while the team turns the client as one unit
Turning the shoulders first, then the hips, and record the intake and output for the shift
explain: Correct: C - logrolling keeps the spine aligned. D is wrong - sequential turning twists the spine. B is wrong - twisting injures the surgical site. A is wrong - the client needs the team's help.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is transferring a weak client using a gait belt. The correct placement is:
options: Snugly around the client's waist over clothing
Loosely around the chest, during the current shift
Around the client's knees, for now
Around the client's neck, at this stage
explain: Correct: A - a snug waist belt gives a secure grip. D is dangerous - neck placement chokes. C is wrong - knees give no trunk control. B is wrong - loose belts slip.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is performing passive range of motion. The correct technique is to:
options: Move each joint gently through its range without forcing, supporting the limb
Push joints past resistance, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Skip painful joints without reporting
Move quickly to save time, and explain the procedure to the patient beforehand
explain: Correct: A - gentle supported movement prevents contractures safely. B is wrong - forcing causes injury. D is wrong - quick movement risks harm. C is wrong - pain needs reporting, not silent skipping.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is applying antiembolism stockings. The correct technique includes:
options: Leaving them on for days without checks, and verify the order against the medication administration record
Applying smooth, wrinkle-free, with toes checked for circulation, and removing periodically per policy to inspect skin
Using the wrong size, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Putting them on with wrinkles, because the provider is expected to review the case later today
explain: Correct: B - smooth fit and skin checks prevent injury and ensure venous return. D is wrong - wrinkles impair circulation. A is wrong - skin needs inspection. C is wrong - wrong size is ineffective or harmful.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is caring for a client with sequential compression devices. The PN should:
options: Turn them off for comfort, and report the findings to the healthcare provider
Wrap them tightly with tape, at this stage
Remove them permanently, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Keep them on and functioning, checking skin and fit, and report malfunction
explain: Correct: D - SCDs prevent VTE only when worn and working. A is wrong - turning off removes protection. C is wrong - removal needs an order. B is wrong - tape impairs function and skin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN reinforces diabetic foot care. The teaching includes:
options: Cutting toenails in curves, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Using heating pads on numb feet, then evaluate the patient's response within the hour
Daily foot inspection, proper footwear, and reporting cuts, blisters, or redness promptly
Walking barefoot to toughen feet, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C - inspection, protection, and prompt reporting prevent amputations. D is wrong - barefoot walking causes injuries. A is wrong - nails are cut straight across. B is wrong - numb feet burn easily.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which perineal care principles should the PN follow? Select all that apply.
options: Using gentle strokes and clean supplies
Scrubbing vigorously back and forth
Cleaning front to back
Providing privacy
Reporting redness, discharge, or odor
explain: Correct: C, A, D, E - front-to-back cleaning, gentleness, privacy, and reporting prevent infection. B is wrong - vigorous scrubbing injures tissue.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The PN is providing oral care for an unconscious client. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Using a soft toothbrush or swabs with minimal fluid
Pouring large amounts of water into the mouth
Inspecting the mouth and reporting abnormalities
Suctioning as needed to prevent aspiration
Positioning the client on the side with head turned
explain: Correct: E, A, D, C - side-lying, minimal fluid, suction, and inspection keep unconscious clients safe. B is wrong - large fluid volumes cause aspiration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which back rub techniques promote comfort? Select all that apply.
options: Rubbing over reddened bony prominences vigorously
Using warm lotion
Asking about pressure preference
Applying smooth, firm strokes
Maintaining privacy with draping
explain: Correct: B, D, E, C - warm lotion, smooth strokes, draping, and preference checks make back rubs therapeutic. A is wrong - vigorous rubbing over redness damages skin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client takes metoprolol. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Expect no side effects, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, on this occasion
Stop it abruptly when feeling well, before the end of the shift, for now
Double the dose if the pulse is fast, at the patient's bedside
Take it as prescribed, monitor pulse and blood pressure, rise slowly, and never stop abruptly
explain: Correct: D - beta blockers need adherence, pulse/BP monitoring, and tapering, not abrupt stops. B is wrong - abrupt stop risks rebound tachycardia and MI. C is wrong - dose changes need orders. A is wrong - fatigue and dizziness are common.

q: A client on lisinopril develops a persistent dry cough. The PN should:
options: Report to the RN; ACE inhibitor cough may require a medication change by the provider
Advise doubling the dose, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care, for now
Give cough syrup without an order, at the patient's bedside
Tell the client to ignore it, before administering any further medication
explain: Correct: A - dry cough is a classic ACE inhibitor effect needing provider review. D is wrong - persistent cough needs evaluation. B is wrong - doubling worsens it. C is wrong - OTC remedies need direction and do not fix the cause.

q: A client takes losartan. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Use salt substitutes freely, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, at the patient's bedside, for now
Expect a persistent cough, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Report swelling of the lips or tongue immediately, monitor blood pressure, and avoid potassium supplements without direction
Stop it if dizzy without telling anyone, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, in full
explain: Correct: C - angioedema is an emergency; potassium needs monitoring. A is wrong - salt substitutes raise potassium dangerously. B is wrong - ARBs rarely cause cough. D is wrong - dizziness needs reporting, not silent stopping.

q: The PN is reinforcing teaching for a client starting amlodipine. Which statement by the client indicates a need for further teaching?
options: I will rise slowly if I feel dizzy, in practice
I can stop the drug on my own if my ankles swell.
I will take it at the same time each day, for now
I will tell my provider about ankle swelling, in full
explain: Correct: B - stopping amlodipine abruptly needs provider direction; ankle edema is common and reported, not self-managed by stopping. C is correct behavior (adherence). D is correct (reporting edema). A is correct (orthostatic precautions).

q: A client takes hydrochlorothiazide. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Take it in the morning, monitor for dizziness and muscle cramps, and eat potassium-rich foods as directed
Expect increased potassium, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
Skip doses on hot days, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, at this stage
Take it at bedtime, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: A - morning dosing avoids nighttime urination; potassium loss needs monitoring. D is wrong - bedtime dosing disrupts sleep. C is wrong - skipping destabilizes control. B is wrong - thiazides lower potassium.

q: A client takes spironolactone. Which finding must be reported promptly?
options: Slight nausea, as documented in the plan of care
Muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat suggesting hyperkalemia
Increased urination, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Mild dizziness, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B - potassium-sparing diuretics raise potassium; weakness and dysrhythmia are warning signs. D and A are milder issues reported routinely. C is expected.

q: A client takes digoxin. The PN should hold the dose and notify the RN if the apical pulse is:
options: 68 and regular
80 and regular, in full
Below 60 per policy
72 and regular, for now
explain: Correct: C - bradycardia below 60 suggests digoxin toxicity risk; hold and report per policy. D, B, and A are within acceptable range.

q: A client takes clopidogrel after a stent. The PN reinforces that the client should:
options: Skip doses before dental work without direction, while maintaining the patient's privacy and dignity
Stop it once feeling well and notify the registered nurse of the patient's status
Use NSAIDs freely for pain, and obtain a new order if the patient's condition changes
Take it as prescribed, report unusual bleeding or bruising, and tell all providers about it before procedures
explain: Correct: D - dual antiplatelet adherence prevents stent thrombosis; bleeding needs reporting. B is wrong - stopping risks stent clotting. C is wrong - NSAIDs raise bleeding risk. A is wrong - changes need provider direction.

q: The PN is reinforcing apixaban teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Doubling up after a missed dose
Stopping it before surgery without direction
Tell all providers and the dentist about it before procedures
Report unusual bleeding, bruising, or blood in urine or stool
Take it as prescribed without skipping doses
explain: Correct: E, D, C - adherence, bleeding surveillance, and procedure disclosure are apixaban essentials. A is wrong - doubling raises bleeding risk. B is wrong - perioperative changes need provider direction.

q: The PN is reinforcing rivaroxaban teaching. Which points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Share the prescription with a spouse who has similar symptoms
Take it with food as directed for certain doses
Inform providers before procedures
Report bleeding or bruising
Do not stop abruptly without provider direction
explain: Correct: B, D, E, C - food timing, bleeding reports, adherence, and disclosure are key. A is wrong - prescriptions are never shared.

q: A client on heparin develops a platelet drop with new clots. The PN should recognize possible heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and:
options: Stop and report to the RN immediately; HIT needs urgent evaluation and alternative anticoagulation
Document for the next shift, before the end of the shift
Increase the heparin, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Continue heparin, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for now
explain: Correct: A - HIT is a medical emergency; heparin stops and alternatives start per orders. D and C worsen thrombosis. B is wrong - waiting is unsafe.

q: The PN is observing a client self-inject enoxaparin. Which actions by the client indicate correct technique? Select all that apply.
options: Rotating injection sites
Reporting unusual bleeding or bruising
Not rubbing the site afterward
Expelling the air bubble from the syringe
Injecting into the abdomen
explain: Correct: E, A, C, B - abdominal injection, site rotation, no rubbing, and bleeding surveillance are correct. D is wrong - the air bubble ensures full dose delivery and is not expelled.

q: Before surgery, the PN verifies the client's allergies. The reason is:
options: To choose the client's meals, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Allergy bands are decorative, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Allergies do not matter in surgery, with the patient's safety as the stated priority
To prevent allergic reactions to medications, latex, or prep solutions used perioperatively
explain: Correct: D - allergy verification prevents anaphylaxis from drugs, latex, or antiseptics. C is wrong - allergies are critical. A is wrong - meals are separate. B is wrong - bands are safety alerts.

q: The PN notes a client takes sedatives and antihypertensives. The PN recognizes these increase:
options: Wound healing, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Fall risk, which should be reported to the RN so precautions can be added
Appetite, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Intelligence, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
explain: Correct: B - sedatives and antihypertensives cause dizziness and orthostasis. C, D, and A are incorrect effects.

q: The PN is teaching incentive spirometer use post-op. The correct instruction is to:
options: Breathe through the nose rapidly, while keeping the patient warm and comfortable
Use it once a day, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, before the end of the shift
Inhale slowly and deeply through the mouthpiece, hold briefly, then exhale normally, repeating per schedule
Blow out hard into the device, under the supervision of the registered nurse
explain: Correct: C - slow deep inhalation with a breath hold re-expands alveoli. D is wrong - it is an inhalation device. B is wrong - frequent use is scheduled. A is wrong - rapid nose breathing defeats the purpose.

q: After abdominal surgery, a client has no bowel sounds, nausea, and abdominal distention. The PN recognizes possible:
options: Hunger, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Postoperative ileus, needing RN notification
Normal recovery, as documented in the plan of care
A urinary infection, on this occasion
explain: Correct: B - absent bowel sounds with distention and nausea suggest ileus. C is wrong - this is not normal recovery. A is wrong - hunger does not cause distention. D is unrelated.

q: A post-op client reports a popping sensation with visible tissue at the incision. The PN should:
options: Tell the client it is normal, since no change has been reported in the patient's condition
Push the tissue back in, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
Cover with a sterile moist dressing, keep the client still with knees flexed, and notify the RN immediately
Remove the dressing and leave it open to air and reassess the patient within the hour to evaluate the response, for now
explain: Correct: C - wound evisceration needs sterile moist coverage and emergency evaluation. B is wrong - the PN never replaces tissue. A is wrong - evisceration is an emergency. D is wrong - exposed tissue needs moist sterile coverage.

q: Which measures help prevent post-op atelectasis that the PN should reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Staying in bed without moving
Deep breathing and coughing exercises
Using the incentive spirometer as scheduled
Early ambulation as permitted
Adequate pain control to allow deep breathing
explain: Correct: C, B, D, E - spirometry, breathing exercises, ambulation, and pain control all re-expand alveoli. A is wrong - immobility causes atelectasis.

q: A post-op client cannot urinate 8 hours after surgery. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Reporting to the RN if unable to void
Catheterizing immediately without an order
Trying privacy, running water, and warm compresses per protocol
Encouraging fluids if permitted
Assessing bladder distention
explain: Correct: E, C, A, D - assessment, noninvasive measures, reporting, and permitted fluids address retention. B is wrong - catheterization needs an order.

q: Which wound findings must the PN report to the RN immediately? Select all that apply.
options: Increasing redness, warmth, or swelling
Purulent drainage
Wound separation or visible tissue
Fever with wound pain
Mild itching around a healing incision
explain: Correct: A, B, C, D - infection signs, dehiscence, and evisceration are all urgent. E is wrong - mild itching is normal healing.
